docs.title: Archy Agents developer documentation
docs.text:
Archy Agents is a multi-tenant platform for building AI features on your own data and tools. It gives you:

  • Knowledge bases (RAG): upload or import documents, index them, and retrieve grounded context.
  • Agents: configurable ReAct agents with a system prompt, a model, knowledge bases, skills and MCP tools.
  • Workflows: coordinate several agents with sequential, parallel, routing, debate and composite (graph) workflows, including human approval checkpoints.
  • Bring-your-own LLM: each organization connects its own provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
  • An MCP server: platform capabilities as tools for Claude, Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT and your own agents.
  • A REST API with an OpenAPI specification, bearer authentication and strict tenant isolation.

Start here

New to the platform? Follow Run Archy locally, then the Quickstart. You will have a working agent that answers from your documents.

docs.text: I want to... Read Understand the model (tenants, projects, agents, workflows) Core concepts Call the API from my backend or frontend Authentication and tokens, then the API reference Create customers (organizations), projects and users from my own product Provisioning tenants and users and the tutorial Connect an LLM provider LLM providers and models Add documents and search them Knowledge bases Build an assistant Agents and the support assistant tutorial Orchestrate several agents Workflows and Composite workflow graphs Use Archy from Claude, Copilot or Cursor MCP See how the system fits together Architecture Let an AI agent read these docs For AI agents

docs.title: Base URLs
docs.text:
Environment API MCP server Hosted https://archy-agents.fly.dev https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp Local (docker compose) http://localhost:8000 http://localhost:8001/mcp

All API routes live under /api/v1. A running API serves Swagger UI at /docs. The specification that powers this site is published at openapi.json.

docs.title: What is in these docs
docs.text:
• Guides explain each capability step by step with curl and Python examples.
  • Tutorials combine several guides into an end-to-end build.
  • Architecture has system, component, data model and sequence diagrams.
  • MCP documents the tool catalog and how to connect clients.
  • API reference lists every public endpoint with parameters, request bodies, examples and responses. It is generated from the code, so it matches the running service.

docs.title: Conventions used in the examples
docs.text:
Examples assume these environment variables. Each page repeats the ones it needs.

export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000   # or https://archy-agents.fly.dev
export ARCHY_TOKEN="<bearer token>"          # see Authentication and tokens
export ORG_ID="<organization id>"
export PROJECT_ID="<project id>"

Shell examples use jq to pick values out of JSON responses. Python examples use httpx (pip install httpx).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
These pages explain how Archy Agents is built, so that you can reason about performance, security and failure modes when you integrate.

  • System overview: the system context, the deployable units and the data stores.
  • Components: the building blocks inside the API and the MCP server.
  • Flows: sequence and state diagrams for the flows you will touch: provisioning, ingestion, agent queries, workflow runs, checkpoints and MCP authentication.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text: Principle What it means for you Tenant isolation first Every query is scoped by organization and project. A token for one tenant cannot read another tenant's data, even by guessing ids. Bring your own LLM Each organization owns its provider credentials. Archy does not use a shared key for your agents unless the operator enabled a platform fallback. Platform, not product The platform is domain neutral. Your product supplies the prompts, business rules and workflows; Archy supplies the runtime. Stateless MCP server The MCP server holds no database access. It calls the public API with the caller's token, so it can never do more than the API allows. Observable by default Runs persist their history, tool calls and token usage. Logs are structured JSON with request ids.

docs.title: Inside the API
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph Routes["HTTP and WebSocket routes (/api/v1)"]
        R1[auth, tenancy, integrations]
        R2[llm-providers]
        R3[rag]
        R4[agents, sessions, artifacts]
        R5[workflows]
        R6[mcp, mcp-tokens, skills]
        R7[realtime, voice]
    end

    subgraph Cross[Cross-cutting]
        AUTH[Principal resolution and token checks]
        TEN[Tenant context and guards]
        RL[Rate limits and request signing]
        OBS[Structured logging, request ids, audit]
    end

    subgraph Core[Core services]
        CRED[Credential and model resolver]
        AGENT[Agent runtime: ReAct, tools, memory, plans, hooks]
        RAG[RAG: readers, chunking, embeddings, indexing, retrieval]
        WF[Workflow engine: legacy executors and composite graph]
        MCPC[MCP client runtime and health scheduler]
        SESS[Sessions, run traces and artifacts]
        USE[Token usage metering]
    end

    subgraph Infra[Infrastructure adapters]
        DB[(PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy)]
        VEC[(Qdrant)]
        BLOB[(Object storage)]
        CACHE[(Redis)]
    end

    Routes --> Cross
    Cross --> Core
    AGENT --> CRED
    WF --> AGENT
    AGENT --> RAG
    AGENT --> MCPC
    AGENT --> SESS
    WF --> SESS
    AGENT --> USE
    Core --> Infra
Component Responsibility Routes Thin HTTP layer. They resolve the principal, validate the body and delegate to a service. Principal resolution Decodes user, service, external IdP and MCP API key tokens and rejects revoked ones. Tenant guards Ensure the organization and project in the path equal the token's tenant. Credential and model resolver Chooses (provider, model, credential) for each execution. See model resolution. Agent runtime Builds the agent from its stored config, registers tools (MCP servers, skills, knowledge base retrieval), manages memory and persists the session. RAG Reads PDF, Office, HTML, text, JSON and image files, chunks them, embeds with the knowledge base's model, indexes into Qdrant and retrieves with hybrid, vector or graph strategies. Workflow engine Executes legacy workflow types and composite graphs, supports checkpoints that pause for a human, versions every change and emits a unified run trace. MCP client runtime Connects agents to external MCP servers (HTTP, and stdio through organization templates), applies per-run tool allow-lists, and health-checks registered servers. Sessions and artifacts Persist conversation history, run traces, and files produced by runs. Usage metering Records token usage per call, aggregated by organization, project, model and time.

docs.title: The MCP server
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CL[MCP client] -- "stdio or streamable HTTP" --> SRV[FastMCP server]
    SRV --> AUTHN[Bearer or API key check]
    AUTHN --> TOOLS[Tool modules: agents, kb, rag, workflows, ...]
    TOOLS -- "httpx, caller token" --> API[Archy REST API]
  • It is a client of the REST API. There is no second implementation of any rule.
  • The org and project for each call come from the caller's token, per request.
  • You can restrict which tool modules a process exposes with MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS.

See MCP.

docs.title: Tenancy at the data layer
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T[Token: org_id, project_id] --> G{Path tenant equals token tenant?}
    G -- no --> F[403 Forbidden]
    G -- yes --> Q[Query with org_id AND project_id filters]
    Q --> D[(Database)]

Organization-scoped resources (agents, workflows, MCP servers, connections) use the organization filter alone and are visible in every project of that organization.

docs.title: Provision a tenant and bootstrap an admin
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant B as Your backend
    participant A as Archy API
    participant U as Admin user
    B->>A: PUT /integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id} (service token)
    A-->>B: org_id, created
    B->>A: PUT .../orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}
    A-->>B: project_id, created
    B->>A: POST .../orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite {email}
    A-->>B: invite_link (single use), user_id
    B->>U: Send the set-password link
    U->>A: POST /auth/reset-password {token, new_password}

docs.title: Ingest and index documents
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant S as Object storage
    participant Q as Indexing job queue
    participant W as Indexer
    participant E as Embedding model
    participant V as Qdrant
    C->>A: POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents/upload (multipart)
    A->>S: store original file
    A->>Q: enqueue one job per document
    A-->>C: documents with status "uploaded"
    W->>Q: take job (running)
    W->>S: read file
    W->>W: extract text and chunk
    W->>E: embed chunks (organization credential)
    W->>V: upsert vectors
    W->>Q: succeeded (document status "indexed")
    C->>A: GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/stats
    A-->>C: files_total, indexed_total, indexing_total

An indexing job moves through the states below. A failed job keeps error_type and error_message; re-run it with POST .../index.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> queued
    queued --> running
    running --> succeeded
    running --> failed
    failed --> queued: re-enqueue
    succeeded --> [*]

docs.title: Ask an agent
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant R as Model resolver
    participant K as Knowledge base
    participant L as LLM provider
    participant T as MCP tools
    C->>A: POST /agents/{id}/query {message, session_id?}
    A->>A: authenticate, check tenant
    A->>R: resolve provider, model, credential
    R-->>A: verified credential or credential error
    A->>K: retrieve top_k chunks (if the agent has a knowledge base)
    loop until final answer or max iterations
        A->>L: messages, tools, context
        L-->>A: text or tool call
        opt tool call
            A->>T: call tool
            T-->>A: result
        end
    end
    A->>A: persist session, record token usage
    A-->>C: output, session_id

docs.title: Run a workflow asynchronously
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant W as Workflow engine
    C->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/runs {message, inputs}
    A-->>C: 202 run_id, status pending
    A->>W: start in background
    loop poll
        C->>A: GET .../runs/{run_id}
        A-->>C: status running
    end
    W-->>A: finished
    C->>A: GET .../runs/{run_id}
    A-->>C: status succeeded, output, audit
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending
    pending --> running
    running --> awaiting_input: checkpoint node
    awaiting_input --> running: resume with answer
    awaiting_input --> cancelled: cancel
    running --> succeeded
    running --> failed
    succeeded --> [*]
    failed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]

docs.title: Pause for a human and resume
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant H as Human
    C->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/execute
    A-->>C: status awaiting_input, pending_input, session_id
    C->>H: show the question
    H-->>C: answer
    C->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/sessions/{session_id}/resume {answer}
    A-->>C: continues, status completed

docs.title: Connect an AI client to the MCP server
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as MCP client
    participant M as MCP server
    participant A as Archy API
    participant U as User (browser)
    C->>M: request without token
    M-->>C: 401 with resource_metadata
    C->>M: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
    M-->>C: authorization server = Archy API
    C->>A: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
    C->>A: POST /oauth/register (dynamic client registration)
    C->>U: open /oauth/authorize (PKCE S256)
    U->>A: sign in and approve
    A-->>C: authorization code on redirect URI
    C->>A: POST /oauth/token (code, code_verifier)
    A-->>C: access token
    C->>M: tools/call with Authorization: Bearer
    M->>A: same call with the caller token
    A-->>M: result scoped to the caller's tenant
    M-->>C: tool result

Clients that cannot run OAuth use an archy_mcp_ API key instead. See Connect a client.

docs.title: Which model runs
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    S([Execution starts]) --> A{Attachment on the agent?}
    A -- yes --> USE[Use that credential and model]
    A -- no --> B{Agent config pins credential_id and model_name?}
    B -- yes --> USE
    B -- no --> C{Project attachment?}
    C -- yes --> USE
    C -- no --> C2{Project platform default model?}
    C2 -- yes --> PLAT[Platform model, no credential]
    C2 -- no --> D{Organization attachment?}
    D -- yes --> USE
    D -- no --> D2{Organization platform default model?}
    D2 -- yes --> PLAT
    D2 -- no --> E{Agent config has a model_name?}
    E -- yes --> PLAT
    E -- no --> ERR[No model: error or echo mode]

A tier is skipped when its credential is missing or not verified. The platform tiers run only when the organization allows the platform fallback. When none applies the call fails with a credential_error rather than silently using a platform key.

docs.title: Deployable units
docs.text: Unit Purpose Scaling notes API (src.main:app) REST and WebSocket surface, authentication, agent and workflow execution, RAG Stateless; scale horizontally. Runs database migrations on release. MCP server (python -m src.mcp_server) MCP tools over stdio or streamable HTTP Stateless; one process per transport. Holds no database access. PostgreSQL Organizations, projects, users, agents, workflows, sessions, credentials (encrypted), audit Source of truth for metadata. Qdrant Vector index per knowledge base Rebuildable from documents by re-indexing. Redis Caching and queues Loss is recoverable. Object storage Uploaded documents and artifacts S3-compatible (S3, MinIO) or Azure Blob.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Public
        C[Client]
    end
    subgraph Edge[Edge: TLS, rate limits]
        A[API]
    end
    subgraph Inner[Private network]
        D[(Databases and storage)]
    end
    subgraph Egress[Outbound with SSRF guard]
        E[LLM providers and tool servers]
    end
    C -->|bearer token| A
    A --> D
    A --> E
  • Inbound: every route needs a bearer token except health probes and the OAuth discovery endpoints. Login and password reset are rate limited per client IP and per account.
  • Secrets: provider API keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never returned. MCP server configuration secrets are write-only. Sensitive workflow inputs are masked in stored traces.
  • Outbound: URLs that you configure (provider base URLs, MCP server URLs, document URLs) pass an SSRF validation that blocks private and loopback ranges unless the operator explicitly allows them.

docs.text: Local Hosted Start with docker compose up managed by the platform operator API http://localhost:8000 https://archy-agents.fly.dev Service tokens you mint them issued by the operator LLM credentials yours yours (per organization)

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This section takes you from nothing to a working agent.

  1. Core concepts: the vocabulary and the tenant model. Ten minutes of reading that saves hours later.
  2. Run Archy locally: start the API, database, vector store and MCP server with Docker Compose.
  3. Quickstart: provision an organization, connect an LLM, add documents, create an agent and ask it a question.

docs.title: Integration patterns
docs.text:
Most teams use one of three patterns. They can be combined.

Embedded in your productDirect API useThrough MCP

Your backend owns customers and users. It uses a service token to create an organization, a project and users in Archy for each of your customers, pushes their LLM credentials, and then calls the API on their behalf (or lets their users call it).

flowchart LR
    P[Your product backend] -- service token --> A[Archy Agents API]
    U[Your end users] --> P
    P -- user token --> A

Read: Provisioning tenants and users, Onboard customers from your backend.

A developer or a service registers (or is invited), logs in, and calls the API with a user token. Good for internal tools and scripts.

Read: Authentication and tokens, Quickstart.

AI clients (Claude, VS Code Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT or your own agent) connect to the Archy MCP server and use platform capabilities as tools: search a knowledge base, ask an agent, run a workflow.

Read: MCP overview, Connect a client.

docs.title: The tenant model
docs.text:
Everything in Archy belongs to a tenant. Isolation is enforced on every query, so one customer can never read another customer's data.

erDiagram
    ORGANIZATION ||--o{ PROJECT : has
    ORGANIZATION ||--o{ LLM_CREDENTIAL : owns
    USER ||--o{ PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP : has
    PROJECT ||--o{ PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP : grants
    PROJECT ||--o{ AGENT : contains
    PROJECT ||--o{ KNOWLEDGE_BASE : contains
    PROJECT ||--o{ WORKFLOW : contains
    PROJECT ||--o{ MCP_SERVER : registers
    PROJECT ||--o{ SESSION : records
    PROJECT ||--o{ ARTIFACT : stores
    KNOWLEDGE_BASE ||--o{ DOCUMENT : indexes
    WORKFLOW ||--o{ WORKFLOW_VERSION : versions
    AGENT }o--o{ KNOWLEDGE_BASE : "grounded in"
    AGENT }o--o{ MCP_SERVER : "uses tools of"
    WORKFLOW }o--o{ AGENT : orchestrates
Term Meaning Organization (org_id) A customer or company. Owns LLM credentials and org-wide defaults. Project (project_id) A workspace inside an organization. Most resources live in a project. User A person or service identity. A user can be a member of many organizations and projects and switches between them. Membership Links a user to a project with a role: admin or permission-admin.

Identifiers

All identifiers are UUIDs. Timestamps are ISO 8601 (UTC). Names are free text up to 255 characters.

Some resources can also be organization-scoped (agents, workflows, MCP servers and templates, connections). They are visible from every project in the organization and are addressed with /orgs/{org_id}/... routes instead of /orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/....

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: Resource What it is Guide LLM credential A provider connection (API key, base URL) owned by an organization or a project. Encrypted at rest and never returned by the API. LLM providers Model attachment A pin of (credential, model) to an agent, project or organization. Decides which model runs. LLM providers Knowledge base A named collection of documents embedded into a vector store for retrieval. Knowledge bases Agent A configured ReAct agent: system prompt, model, knowledge base, skills, tools, memory. Agents Workflow A definition that coordinates agents. Legacy types (sequential, parallel, routing, debate, ...) or composite graphs. Workflows Session The persisted history of a conversation with an agent or a workflow run. Sessions Run One execution of a workflow. Can be synchronous, streamed or asynchronous. Running and streaming Artifact A file produced by a run or uploaded to a project. Sessions MCP server An external Model Context Protocol server whose tools an agent can call. External MCP servers Skill A packaged set of instructions an agent can use. External MCP servers

docs.title: Identities and tokens
docs.text:
Every request carries Authorization: Bearer <token>. There are four kinds of token.

Token Obtained from Acts as Typical use User token (JWT) POST /auth/login, /auth/register, /tenancy/switch One user in one org and project Applications and scripts acting for a person Service token (JWT, token_type=service) Issued by the operator of the Archy deployment A backend system with explicit scopes (provision:org, ...) Provisioning tenants and users from your backend MCP API key (archy_mcp_...) POST .../mcp-tokens or OAuth One project, scope mcp:tools (or mcp:read through OAuth) IDEs and agent clients that use the MCP server External IdP token (JWT via JWKS) Your identity provider, when the deployment enables it The user in the token claims Single sign-on integrations

See Authentication and tokens for details.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
A project membership has one of two roles.

  • admin: manages the organization. Required for organization-level operations such as creating LLM credentials. Users created by provisioning get this role.
  • permission-admin: the role a user gets when they self-register with POST /auth/register. It can create and use agents, knowledge bases and workflows in its project, but it cannot manage organization-level LLM credentials.

Self-registered users cannot add LLM credentials

A user created with POST /auth/register owns a project but not organization admin rights. To add an LLM provider you need an admin membership. The fastest way to get one is the invite flow in Provisioning.

docs.title: How a request is resolved
docs.text:
1. The token is decoded and verified. Revoked or expired tokens return 401.
  2. The org_id and project_id in the path must match the token tenant. A mismatch returns 403.
  3. The route checks the role it needs (for example organization admin for LLM credentials).
  4. Every database query is filtered by organization and project.

docs.title: Models and credentials
docs.text: An agent runs on a model chosen by the model resolution order. In short: an attachment on the agent wins, then the project, then the organization, then the platform default. Only credentials that passed verification are used.

docs.title: Sync, streaming and async
docs.text: Mode Use when Endpoint style Synchronous A short request that returns a final answer POST .../query, POST .../execute Streaming You want progress as it happens Server-Sent Events (.../stream) or NDJSON Asynchronous run The caller cannot hold a connection (for example a serverless function) POST .../runs, then poll GET .../runs/{run_id}

docs.title: Run Archy locally
docs.text: You can run the full platform on your machine in a few minutes. This is the recommended way to learn the API and to develop against it.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Docker with Compose v2
  • curl and jq
  • Optional, for service tokens and the dev loop: Python 3.11 or 3.12 and Poetry
  • An API key for an LLM provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek or a local Ollama). You add it through the API later; nothing is baked into the stack.

docs.title: 1. Create the credential encryption key
docs.text:
Archy encrypts every stored LLM provider API key with AES-256-GCM. The key is required: without it, creating an LLM credential fails. Generate a 32 byte base64 key once and keep it. If you lose it, stored credentials can no longer be decrypted.

export LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

The stock docker-compose.yml does not forward this variable, so add a docker-compose.override.yml next to it. Compose merges it automatically:

services:
  api:
    environment:
      LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      # Only when you want to use a model server on your machine, for example Ollama.
      # SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS: "true"

docs.title: 2. Start the services
docs.text:
git clone <your archy-agents-scope repository url>
cd archy-agents-scope
docker compose up -d --build

Compose starts these services:

Service Port Purpose api 8000 The REST API. Runs database migrations on start. mcp-server 8001 The Archy Platform MCP server (streamable HTTP). postgres 5453 Metadata (organizations, projects, agents, workflows, sessions). qdrant 6333 Vector store for knowledge bases. redis 6379 Cache and queues. minio 9000, 9001 S3-compatible object storage for uploaded documents.

Check that the API is healthy:

curl -s http://localhost:8000/health
curl -s http://localhost:8000/health/readiness

Open the interactive API explorer at http://localhost:8000/docs.

Defaults are for development only

The stack signs tokens with JWT_SECRET_KEY=change-me. Never use the default outside your machine. Set your own value in the environment before docker compose up.

docs.title: Create a service token
docs.text:
Provisioning endpoints need a service token. In production the operator of your deployment issues it. Locally you mint one with the same signing secret the API uses:

JWT_SECRET_KEY=change-me poetry run python scripts/generate_service_token.py \
  --subject my-backend \
  --scopes provision:org provision:project provision:user provision:user:read \
  --expires-in-minutes 120

Export the output:

export SERVICE_TOKEN="<printed token>"
export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000

The command prints only the token. Service tokens carry scopes, not a tenant: the target organization is part of each request.

Why a service token?

A self-registered user cannot manage organization-level settings such as LLM credentials, and only a service token can create organizations with chosen ids. The Quickstart uses the service token once to create an organization and an admin, then continues with that admin's user token.

docs.title: The development loop
docs.text:
If you prefer to run the API on the host and only the dependencies in Docker:

docker compose up -d postgres qdrant redis minio minio-init
cp .env.example .env.local        # local development loads .env.local
# add LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<base64 key> to .env.local
poetry install
poetry run alembic upgrade head
poetry run uvicorn src.main:app --reload --port 8000

.env.local points DATABASE_URL at localhost:5433. Compose publishes Postgres on 5453. Update DATABASE_URL to the port you use.

Run the MCP server on the host:

export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
export ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN="<MCP API key>"      # see the MCP guide
poetry run python -m src.mcp_server

docs.title: Stop and reset
docs.text:
docker compose down          # stop, keep data
docker compose down -v       # stop and delete all data

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
The settings you are most likely to change. All are environment variables.

Variable Default Purpose DATABASE_URL local Postgres SQLAlchemy URL of the metadata database QDRANT_URL http://localhost:6333 Vector store REDIS_URL redis://localhost:6379/0 Cache and queues S3_ENDPOINT_URL, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, S3_BUCKET_NAME MinIO in compose Document storage JWT_SECRET_KEY, JWT_ALGORITHM change-me, HS256 Signing of user and service tokens EXTERNAL_AUTH_ENABLED, EXTERNAL_AUTH_ISSUER, EXTERNAL_AUTH_AUDIENCE, EXTERNAL_AUTH_JWKS_URL off Accept tokens from your identity provider SERVICE_TOKEN_BINDING_MODE audit enforce requires service tokens to name the organizations they may act for LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY none, required Base64 32 byte key that encrypts stored provider API keys. Optional rotation: LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS and LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID. SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS false Allow http:// and loopback provider URLs. Local development only (for example Ollama). ALLOW_PLATFORM_LLM_FALLBACK_DEFAULT true Whether an organization without credentials may use the platform default model PASSWORD_RESET_URL_BASE http://localhost:3001/reset-password Base of the set-password links the invite endpoint returns CORS_ORIGINS local origins Allowed browser origins LOG_LEVEL INFO Log verbosity (logs are structured JSON)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause and fix connection refused on port 8000 The API container is still migrating. Wait for docker compose ps to show it healthy. 401 Invalid token on provisioning The service token was signed with a different JWT_SECRET_KEY than the API uses. 403 Missing scopes: provision:... Mint the token with the scope named in the message. 500 when creating an LLM credential LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set on the API container. Port already in use Another process uses 8000, 5453, 6333 or 9000. Change the published port in docker-compose.yml.

More in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
In this tutorial you create a complete tenant and a working agent that answers questions from your own document. You use the API only.

You will:

  1. Provision an organization and a project.
  2. Create an organization admin and log in.
  3. Connect an LLM provider and choose the default models.
  4. Create a knowledge base and add a document.
  5. Create an agent grounded in the knowledge base and ask it a question.
flowchart LR
    S[Service token] -->|1. provision| O[Organization and project]
    O -->|2. invite admin| A[Admin user token]
    A -->|3. credential and models| L[LLM provider]
    A -->|4. upload and index| K[Knowledge base]
    A -->|5. create| G[Agent]
    K --> G
    G -->|ask| R[Grounded answer]

Before you start you need a running API (Run Archy locally), a SERVICE_TOKEN with scopes provision:org provision:project provision:user, and an OpenAI API key (any supported provider works; only the credential payload changes).

export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
export SERVICE_TOKEN="<service token>"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="<your provider key>"

docs.title: 1. Provision an organization and a project
docs.text:
Provisioning endpoints are idempotent upserts: you choose the ids, and repeating the call changes nothing.

export ORG_ID=$(uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')
export PROJECT_ID=$(uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Acme"}'

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Support", "description": "Customer support assistant"}'

Each call returns {"org_id": "...", "created": true} (the project call also returns project_id).

docs.title: 2. Create an admin and log in
docs.text:
The invite endpoint creates the user, grants admin on the project, and returns a single-use set-password link. You use the token from the link to set a password, then log in.

export ADMIN_EMAIL="admin@acme.example"
export ADMIN_PASSWORD="a-long-unique-passphrase"

INVITE=$(curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/admins/invite" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\": \"$ADMIN_EMAIL\"}")

RESET_TOKEN=$(echo "$INVITE" | jq -r '.invite_link' | sed 's/.*token=//')

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"token\": \"$RESET_TOKEN\", \"new_password\": \"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}"

export ARCHY_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\": \"$ADMIN_EMAIL\", \"password\": \"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}" | jq -r '.access_token')

Confirm the token works:

curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/whoami" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

{
  "subject": "9e0eb3c6-63d5-42db-98cd-f2ed378ca051",
  "org_id": "35af6d8d-f874-4b2b-9222-122092075307",
  "project_id": "117c77c5-5c13-49b1-aad7-9499442d967c"
}

From now on you use ARCHY_TOKEN. The service token is only for provisioning.

Why not just register?

POST /auth/register creates a user with its own organization in one call and is fine for experiments. That user has the permission-admin role and cannot create LLM credentials. See Roles.

docs.title: 3. Connect an LLM provider
docs.text:
Create the credential, then verify it. Verification makes a one token request to the provider. Only verified credentials are used at runtime.

CRED_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"provider\": \"openai\", \"display_name\": \"OpenAI\", \"api_key\": \"$OPENAI_API_KEY\", \"is_default\": true}" \
  | jq -r '.id')

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/$CRED_ID/verify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

A successful verification returns {"success": true, "is_verified": true, "verified_at": "...", "latency_ms": 412, "error": null}. A wrong key returns success: false with an error message and nothing is attached.

Now choose which models run by default. One attachment sets the chat model for the whole organization, and one sets the embedding model used by new knowledge bases:

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"gpt-4o-mini\"}"

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"text-embedding-3-small\", \"dimensions\": 1536}"

Verify first

The model attachment call returns 422 Credential must be verified before attaching a model if verification did not succeed. Fix the key first.

docs.title: 4. Create a knowledge base and add a document
docs.text:
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

export KB_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "handbook", "description": "Company handbook"}' | jq -r '.id')

cat > handbook.md <<'EOF'
# Acme handbook

Support hours are 08:00 to 18:00 CET, Monday to Friday.
Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.
Enterprise customers get a named contact and a four hour response target.
EOF

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/upload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -F "files=@handbook.md"

Upload stores the file and enqueues indexing. Check progress until indexed_total equals files_total:

curl -s "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
# {"files_total": 1, "indexed_total": 1, "indexing_total": 0}

Search it directly:

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?", "top_k": 3}' | jq '.results[0].content'

docs.title: 5. Create an agent and ask it a question
docs.text:
export AGENT_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"name\": \"support-assistant\",
    \"description\": \"Answers support questions from the handbook\",
    \"config\": {
      \"sys_prompt\": \"You are a support assistant. Answer only from the knowledge base and say when you do not know.\",
      \"knowledge_base_id\": \"$KB_ID\",
      \"knowledge_base_top_k\": 4,
      \"temperature\": 0.2
    }
  }" | jq -r '.id')

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "What are your support hours and what is the refund window?"}'

The response contains the answer and the session id. Pass session_id on the next call to continue the conversation.

{
  "agent_id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e",
  "session_id": "4e7c87f4-30d4-565f-a47b-9b4fca7f385a",
  "output": "Support hours are 08:00 to 18:00 CET, Monday to Friday. Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.",
  "meta": {}
}

You now have an organization, an admin, a connected model, an indexed knowledge base and a grounded agent.

docs.title: The same flow in Python
docs.text:
import os
import time
import uuid
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

import httpx

BASE = os.environ.get("ARCHY_API_URL", "http://localhost:8000")
SERVICE = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SERVICE_TOKEN']}"}
PASSWORD = "a-long-unique-passphrase"

client = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=120)


def ok(response: httpx.Response) -> dict | list:
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()


# 1. Provision
org_id, project_id = str(uuid.uuid4()), str(uuid.uuid4())
ok(client.put(f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}", headers=SERVICE, json={"name": "Acme"}))
ok(client.put(
    f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}",
    headers=SERVICE,
    json={"name": "Support"},
))

# 2. Admin: invite, set password, log in
invite = ok(client.post(
    f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite",
    headers=SERVICE,
    json={"email": "admin@acme.example"},
))
reset_token = parse_qs(urlparse(invite["invite_link"]).query)["token"][0]
ok(client.post("/api/v1/auth/reset-password", json={"token": reset_token, "new_password": PASSWORD}))
login = ok(client.post("/api/v1/auth/login", json={"email": "admin@acme.example", "password": PASSWORD}))
user = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {login['access_token']}"}

# 3. LLM provider and default models
cred = ok(client.post(
    "/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials",
    headers=user,
    json={"provider": "openai", "display_name": "OpenAI", "api_key": os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], "is_default": True},
))
verified = ok(client.post(f"/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/{cred['id']}/verify", headers=user))
assert verified["success"], verified["error"]
ok(client.put(
    "/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org",
    headers=user,
    json={"credential_id": cred["id"], "model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"},
))
ok(client.put(
    "/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default",
    headers=user,
    json={"credential_id": cred["id"], "model_name": "text-embedding-3-small", "dimensions": 1536},
))

# 4. Knowledge base
scope = f"/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}"
kb = ok(client.post(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases", headers=user, json={"name": "handbook"}))
ok(client.post(
    f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb['id']}/documents/upload",
    headers=user,
    files=[("files", ("handbook.md", b"Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase.", "text/markdown"))],
))
while True:
    stats = ok(client.get(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb['id']}/stats", headers=user))
    if stats["indexed_total"] >= stats["files_total"] > 0:
        break
    time.sleep(2)

# 5. Agent
agent = ok(client.post(
    f"{scope}/agents",
    headers=user,
    json={
        "name": "support-assistant",
        "config": {"sys_prompt": "Answer only from the knowledge base.", "knowledge_base_id": kb["id"]},
    },
))
answer = ok(client.post(
    f"/api/v1/agents/{agent['id']}/query", headers=user, json={"message": "What is the refund window?"}
))
print(answer["output"])

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Understand how the model is chosen: LLM providers and models.
  • Stream the answer instead of waiting: Running and streaming.
  • Combine agents: Workflows and the research pipeline tutorial.
  • Use the platform from an AI client: MCP.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Step-by-step guides for each capability. Every guide has runnable curl and Python examples and links to the matching API reference pages.

Guide You learn how to Authentication and tokens Get and use user tokens, service tokens, MCP API keys and external tokens Provisioning tenants and users Create organizations, projects, users and admins from your backend LLM providers and models Connect providers, verify credentials and choose which model runs Knowledge bases Ingest documents, index them and query them Agents Configure agents and talk to them Workflows Coordinate several agents with the built-in workflow types Composite workflow graphs Author graph workflows with nodes, edges, inputs and expressions Running and streaming Execute synchronously, stream with SSE or NDJSON, and run asynchronously External MCP servers and skills Give agents extra tools Sessions, artifacts and usage Read history, download files and track token usage Errors, limits and practices Handle errors, retries and rate limits

Recommended order for a new integration

Authentication → Provisioning → LLM providers → Knowledge bases → Agents → Running and streaming. Add workflows when one agent is not enough.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
An agent is a stored configuration that Archy turns into a reasoning-and-acting (ReAct) agent at run time. It reads the conversation, optionally retrieves from a knowledge base, calls tools and answers.

flowchart LR
    CFG[Agent config] --> RT[Agent runtime]
    MODEL[Resolved model] --> RT
    KB[Knowledge base] --> RT
    MCP[MCP tools] --> RT
    SK[Skills] --> RT
    MEM[Memory] --> RT
    RT --> OUT[Answer, tool calls, session history]

docs.title: Create an agent
docs.text:
Project agents live in /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents. Organization agents live in /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/agents and are visible from every project of the organization.

BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "support-assistant",
    "description": "Answers support questions",
    "config": {
      "sys_prompt": "You are a support assistant. Answer from the knowledge base and say when you do not know.",
      "knowledge_base_id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
      "knowledge_base_top_k": 4,
      "temperature": 0.2,
      "memory": {"mode": "buffer", "window_messages": 20}
    }
  }'

{
  "id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e",
  "org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865",
  "scope": "project",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "name": "support-assistant",
  "description": "Answers support questions",
  "type": null,
  "config": {"sys_prompt": "...", "knowledge_base_id": "...", "knowledge_base_top_k": 4, "temperature": 0.2, "memory": {"mode": "buffer"}},
  "avatar_path": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:19:16.984748",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:19:16.984750"
}
Field Meaning name Required, 1 to 255 characters description Optional text type Optional label, up to 50 characters config The runtime configuration, described below

docs.title: Manage agents
docs.text:
Action Request List GET .../agents Get GET .../agents/{agent_id} Update PUT .../agents/{agent_id} Delete DELETE .../agents/{agent_id} (returns {"status": "deleted"})

Stored config

Default values are not stored: for example "window_messages": 20 is dropped from a memory object. If the operator configured a default agent model, config.model is filled in when you omit it.

PUT replaces config

An update with a config object replaces the whole configuration; it is not merged. Read the agent first, change what you need and send the complete object. Fields you omit at the top level (name, description, type) are left unchanged.

docs.title: The configuration
docs.text:
The config object is validated when you save it. An unknown key or a wrong type returns 400:

{
  "detail": {
    "message": "Invalid config",
    "errors": [{"type": "extra_forbidden", "loc": ["bogus"], "msg": "Extra inputs are not permitted"}]
  }
}

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Key Type Meaning sys_prompt string The system prompt. Aliases instructions and system_prompt are accepted. Default: You are a helpful assistant. model object {provider, model_name, credential_id}. See Which model runs. Prefer attachments over this field. temperature number 0 to 2 Sampling temperature top_p number 0 to 1 Nucleus sampling max_tokens integer ≥ 1 Maximum tokens of one model reply max_iters integer 1 to 100 Maximum reasoning and tool iterations per reply token_budget integer ≥ 1 Overall token budget of one reply input_token_weight, output_token_weight number ≥ 0 Weights used when counting against the budget

docs.title: Knowledge and tools
docs.text: Key Type Meaning knowledge_base_id UUID Knowledge base used for retrieval knowledge_base_top_k integer ≥ 1 Chunks retrieved per question tools_enabled list of strings Stored tool labels. They are not used by the agent runtime; retrieval is driven by knowledge_base_id. skills_enabled list of strings Skills to attach automatic_mcp boolean Connect the MCP servers attached to the agent automatically. When unset it is off, unless the agent has a personal integration grant, in which case it is on. web_search object {enabled, provider: duckduckgo or tavily or brave, api_key} playwright object {enabled, headless} browser automation tool deep_research object {enabled, max_iterations (1-50), max_depth (1-10), search_provider, tavily_api_key}

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: Key Type Meaning memory object {mode, window_messages} with mode one of none, buffer, agentscope_db, in_memory, sqlalchemy, redis memory_window integer 0 to 50 Number of previous messages replayed long_term_memory object {enabled, mode: static_control or agent_control or both, provider: qdrant}; facts survive across sessions

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: Key Type Meaning model_routing object Per-reply routing: a router_model picks one of candidates (name, model, description) by the latest user message. Needs at least one candidate when enabled. structured_output boolean Ask the agent to return structured output allowed_agent_ids, default_participant_agent_ids list of UUID strings Used by multi-agent dialog orchestration hooks_enabled list of strings Lifecycle hooks to enable voice, elevenlabs_voice_id string Voice settings for realtime conversations external object Free-form metadata for provisioning systems

docs.title: One request, one answer
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "What are your support hours?"}'

{
  "agent_id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e",
  "session_id": "4e7c87f4-30d4-565f-a47b-9b4fca7f385a",
  "output": "Support hours are 08:00 to 18:00 CET, Monday to Friday.",
  "meta": {}
}

A session stores the conversation. Omit session_id to start a new one. Pass it back to continue:

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"message\": \"And on weekends?\", \"session_id\": \"$SESSION_ID\"}"

An unknown session_id returns 404.

No model resolved

If no model can be resolved for the agent (no attachment, no pinned credential and no platform default), the API may answer in echo mode instead of failing: output is Echo: <your message> and meta.mode is echo (or rag+echo when the agent has a knowledge base) with a fallback_reason such as missing_agent_model_config. When a credential cannot be used, meta.mode is credential_error and meta.credential_error explains why. In every case connect and attach a model. In automated tests assert that meta.mode is none of echo, rag+echo and credential_error.

docs.title: Stream the answer
docs.text:
For chat interfaces use Server-Sent Events. Events are start, repeated delta, then end (or error). See Running and streaming for parsers.

curl -N -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/chat/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Summarize our refund policy"}'

docs.title: Give the agent more abilities
docs.text:
• Knowledge: set knowledge_base_id (see Knowledge bases).
  • Tools from MCP servers: register a server and attach it to the agent (see External MCP servers and skills).
  • Skills: attach a skill with POST .../agents/{agent_id}/skills.
  • Another model: attach one with model attachments.
  • Personal Atlassian access: grant a connection to the agent with the integration-grants endpoints.

docs.title: State, memory and plans
docs.text: Capability Endpoints Session state GET and PUT /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/state Cross-session memory summaries GET .../agents/{agent_id}/memory Multi-step plans POST and GET /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/plans, PUT and DELETE .../plans/{plan_id} Avatar PUT and GET .../agents/{agent_id}/avatar Audit of an agent GET /api/v1/agents/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_id}/audit

docs.title: Write a good system prompt
docs.text:
• State the role and the audience in the first sentence.
  • Say what the agent must do when it lacks information ("ask a clarifying question", "say you do not know").
  • Name the sources it may use. For a knowledge base agent: "Answer only from the knowledge base."
  • Describe the format of the answer (length, language, bullet list, JSON).
  • Put business rules in the prompt, not in your code. Archy is domain neutral; your prompt is where your product's behavior lives.

docs.title: Python: create and chat
docs.text:
import httpx


def create_agent(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, name: str, prompt: str, kb_id: str | None = None) -> str:
    config = {"sys_prompt": prompt, "memory": {"mode": "buffer", "window_messages": 20}}
    if kb_id:
        config["knowledge_base_id"] = kb_id
    r = client.post(f"{scope}/agents", json={"name": name, "config": config})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["id"]


def chat(client: httpx.Client, agent_id: str) -> None:
    session_id = None
    while (message := input("you> ")) not in ("", "quit"):
        body = {"message": message, **({"session_id": session_id} if session_id else {})}
        r = client.post(f"/api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query", json=body, timeout=120)
        r.raise_for_status()
        reply = r.json()
        session_id = reply["session_id"]
        print("agent>", reply["output"])

docs.title: Authentication and tokens
docs.text:
Every API call needs a bearer token, except the health probes, the /auth/* endpoints (register, login, forgot and reset password) and the OAuth endpoints:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

A missing or malformed header returns 401 with {"detail": "Missing bearer token"}.

docs.title: Token types at a glance
docs.text: Token Identifies Lifetime Where it is accepted User token (JWT) A user acting in one org and project Login: 8 hours, or 7 days with remember_me. Register and tenant switch: 30 minutes. All tenant routes Service token (JWT) A backend system and its scopes Chosen by the issuer Provisioning routes, and tenant routes for the organization and project in the request MCP API key (archy_mcp_...) A project and a scope (mcp:tools; mcp:read when granted through OAuth) 1 to 365 days, or never MCP server and the MCP routes of the API External IdP token (JWT) The user named in the claims Set by your IdP All tenant routes, when the operator enabled it

docs.title: Register
docs.text:
Creates a user together with a new organization and project, and returns a token.

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/register" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "dev@example.com", "password": "a-long-unique-passphrase", "org_name": "Acme", "project_name": "Support"}'

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "user_id": "0888cd4e-1746-4009-ad52-53f369120227",
  "org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "available_orgs": [{"org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865", "name": "Acme", "project_count": 1}]
}
  • email must be unique; a duplicate returns 409.
  • password is 8 to 128 characters (a shorter one fails request validation with 422).
  • The returned token lasts 30 minutes. Use POST /auth/login (8 hours, or 7 days with remember_me) for longer sessions.
  • A self-registered user has the permission-admin role. See Roles.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "dev@example.com", "password": "a-long-unique-passphrase", "remember_me": false}'

The response has the same shape as register. Wrong credentials return 401 Invalid credentials for every cause (unknown email, wrong password, inactive account), so the response does not reveal which accounts exist.

docs.title: Inspect and switch tenant
docs.text:
A user can belong to several organizations and projects. The token is bound to one pair; switch to get a new token for another pair.

# Who am I, and in which tenant?
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/whoami" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Organizations and projects I belong to
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/orgs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/projects?org_id=$ORG_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Switch; the response contains a new access_token
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/switch" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG_ID\", \"project_id\": \"$PROJECT_ID\"}"

Switching to a project you are not a member of returns 403 Not a member of this project. The new token lasts 30 minutes, and the switched organization and project become your default for the next login.

docs.title: Reset a password
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/forgot-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email": "dev@example.com"}'

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"token": "<token from the email link>", "new_password": "a-new-long-unique-passphrase"}'

forgot-password always returns 200, whether or not the email exists. Reset tokens are single use and expire. A successful reset invalidates every token issued earlier for that user.

docs.title: Python helper
docs.text:
import os
import httpx


class ArchyClient:
    """Logs in, injects the bearer token and logs in again once on a 401."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, email: str, password: str) -> None:
        self.http = httpx.Client(base_url=base_url, timeout=60)
        self.email, self.password = email, password
        self.login()

    def login(self) -> None:
        r = self.http.post("/api/v1/auth/login", json={"email": self.email, "password": self.password})
        r.raise_for_status()
        body = r.json()
        self.org_id, self.project_id = body["org_id"], body["project_id"]
        self.http.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {body['access_token']}"

    def request(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs) -> httpx.Response:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code == 401:
            self.login()
            response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response


client = ArchyClient(os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"], os.environ["ARCHY_EMAIL"], os.environ["ARCHY_PASSWORD"])
print(client.request("GET", "/api/v1/tenancy/whoami").json())

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: Register and login are throttled per client IP and per account; reset-password per client IP and per reset token. When the budget is used up the API returns 429 with a Retry-After header (the length of the throttle window in seconds, 60 by default). Back off for at least that long. forgot-password is throttled silently: it keeps returning 200.

docs.title: Service tokens
docs.text:
A service token authenticates a system, not a person. It normally carries scopes and no tenant. You use it to provision organizations, projects and users.

Claims of a service token:

Claim Meaning sub Name of the calling system token_type service scope Space separated scopes org_ids Optional list of organization ids the token may act for exp Expiry

Scopes:

Scope Allows provision:org PUT /integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id} provision:project PUT .../orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id} provision:user PUT .../users/{user_id} and POST .../orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite provision:user:read GET .../users/by-email/{email} provision:credential Push and delete LLM credentials for an organization tenant:act Needed together with org_ids when the deployment runs in enforce binding mode

Tenant binding

A deployment can run service tokens in audit mode (default: every use is logged with the organization it targeted) or enforce mode (on routes that target an organization the token must have tenant:act and list the organization in org_ids, otherwise 403 Forbidden). The user lookup by email is only audited. Ask the operator which mode applies and request a token bound to the organizations you manage.

Service tokens are issued by the operator of the deployment. For local development you can mint one yourself, see Run Archy locally.

Using a service token on a route that needs a user returns 403 User token required; using a user token on a provisioning route returns 403 Service token required.

docs.title: Acting on tenant routes
docs.text:
A service token with at least one scope can also call the tenant routes (agents, knowledge bases, workflows, runs, ...) for the organization and project named in the path. This is how a backend operates a customer's workspace without holding a user session. Rules to know:

  • The tenant comes from the request: the org_id and project_id in the path (/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/...) or, on routes that take them as optional query parameters (for example /agents/{agent_id}/query), from ?org_id=...&project_id=.... Organization-scoped routes need only org_id. Without a tenant the API returns 401 Missing org_id, which is why GET /tenancy/whoami returns 401 for a service token.
  • It has no organization admin rights. Operations that need an admin user, such as POST /llm-providers/credentials?org_id=...&project_id=... or PUT /llm-providers/model-attachments/org?org_id=..., return 403 Org admin role required. Push credentials with the provisioning endpoint and pin a model in the agent config instead (see Onboard customers from your backend).
  • In enforce binding mode the token must carry the tenant:act scope and list the organization in org_ids, otherwise the API returns 403 Forbidden.
  • A run started this way has no initiating user, so personal connections are unavailable to it.

docs.title: MCP API keys
docs.text:
An API key lets an IDE or agent client use the MCP server without an interactive login.

# Create (a user token, or a service token for that organization and project). The raw token is shown once.
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "my-ide", "expires_in_days": 90}'

# List, revoke (stops working, row kept) or delete with DELETE .../mcp-tokens/$TOKEN_ID
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens/$TOKEN_ID/revoke" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

{
  "id": "0dd516ed-3c38-47a7-bfd1-3dd7cec3be3f",
  "name": "my-ide",
  "token_prefix": "archy_mcp_0a1b2c3d",
  "token": "archy_mcp_0a1b2c3d<random characters, shown once>",
  "expires_at": "2027-02-15T09:09:03.996701",
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:03.997580"
}

expires_in_days is 1 to 365 and defaults to 90 when omitted; send null explicitly for a key that never expires. The response (201) also contains org_id, project_id and description. Store the token value in a secret manager immediately. It cannot be read again. See Connect a client for scopes and usage.

docs.title: External identity provider tokens
docs.text:
If you operate your own deployment you can let Archy trust tokens from your IdP (Microsoft Entra, Auth0, Keycloak or any OIDC provider that publishes a JWKS):

EXTERNAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true
EXTERNAL_AUTH_ISSUER=https://login.example.com/
EXTERNAL_AUTH_AUDIENCE=archy-api
EXTERNAL_AUTH_JWKS_URL=https://login.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
EXTERNAL_AUTH_ALGORITHMS=RS256

The token must carry iss, aud and a subject (sub, or oid, appid, azp or client_id). A user token must also carry org_id and project_id claims, otherwise it is rejected. Application-only tokens (token_type=service, grant_type=client_credentials, idtyp=app, or roles without scp or scope) are treated as service tokens. Scopes come from the scope claim; if it is absent, from scp; if that is absent, from roles. The role org-admin grants organization admin rights. The deployment refuses external tokens when issuer and audience are not configured.

docs.title: Revocation and security notes
docs.text:
• Password reset revokes tokens. Tokens issued by Archy carry a version. Resetting the password increments it, so older tokens return 401 Token revoked.
  • Deactivated users stop working. A deactivated user's Archy tokens and MCP keys are rejected. External IdP tokens and service tokens are not revoked this way: they stay valid until they expire, so revoke them at the source.
  • Tenant mismatch is 403. If the org_id or project_id in the path differ from the token, the API returns 403 Forbidden without saying whether the resource exists.
  • Keep tokens out of logs and URLs. Send them only in the Authorization header and never log them in your own code.
  • Use the narrowest token. Keys created with the API carry the write-capable mcp:tools scope; for read-only clients let the client request mcp:read through OAuth. Bind service tokens to organizations in enforce mode.

docs.title: Composite workflow graphs
docs.text:
A composite workflow is a graph: typed nodes joined by typed edges, plus declared inputs and variables. It can branch on conditions, loop, run branches in parallel, merge results, pause for a human, call other workflows and save files.

This page teaches by building graphs. The authoritative, always current contracts are served by the API (and as MCP tools), so read them when you generate graphs programmatically:

Contract REST MCP tool Authoring guide (Markdown) GET /api/v1/workflow-authoring-guide workflow_authoring_guide_get Node type registry GET /api/v1/workflow-node-types workflow_node_types_get JSON Schema of the definition GET /api/v1/workflow-definition-schema workflow_definition_schema_get Validation and run error codes GET /api/v1/workflow-validation-codes workflow_validation_codes_get

docs.title: The definition
docs.text:
A composite workflow has type: "composite" and a config that is a version 2 definition:

{
  "version": 2,
  "inputs": [],
  "variables": {},
  "graph": {"nodes": [], "edges": []}
}
  • Node: {id, type, data, position}. id is unique. data.name is the reference name other nodes use as nodes.<name> (lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 48 characters). position is {x, y} and only matters for editors.
  • Edge: {id, source, target, sourceHandle?, targetHandle?, data?}. The connection type is read from data.connectionType, default sequential.
  • Exactly one start node and at least one end node. A path must lead from start to an end and no node may be left unconnected (ORPHAN_NODE); a node that start cannot reach is a warning (UNREACHABLE_NODE). A cycle is allowed only through a loop node.
  • Unknown keys are preserved, so editors can store their own fields.

docs.title: Your first graph
docs.text:
Two agents in a row, with a declared input:

{
  "name": "research-and-write",
  "type": "composite",
  "config": {
    "version": 2,
    "inputs": [{"name": "topic", "type": "string", "required": true}],
    "graph": {
      "nodes": [
        {"id": "start", "type": "start", "data": {}},
        {"id": "a1", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "researcher", "agentId": "<agent id>", "prompt": "Research: {{input.topic}}"}},
        {"id": "a2", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "writer", "agentId": "<agent id>", "prompt": "Write a summary of:\n{{nodes.researcher.output}}"}},
        {"id": "end", "type": "end", "data": {}}
      ],
      "edges": [
        {"id": "e1", "source": "start", "target": "a1"},
        {"id": "e2", "source": "a1", "target": "a2"},
        {"id": "e3", "source": "a2", "target": "end"}
      ]
    }
  }
}

flowchart LR
    S((start)) --> R[agent: researcher]
    R --> W[agent: writer]
    W --> E((end))

Create it with POST .../workflows, then run it:

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Research request", "inputs": {"topic": "vector databases"}}'

docs.title: Node types
docs.text:
Type Category Purpose Key data fields start terminal Entry point none end terminal Exit point none agent agent Runs a configured agent agentId (required), name, prompt, role, outputSchema, required_mcp_servers hub agent Coordinates agents as a hub. Passes its input through at run time. agentId (required), name, prompt msghub agent Multi-agent conversation on a shared hub name, maxRounds, announcement pipeline flow Runs several agents sequentially or fanned out agentIds (required), mode (sequential or fanout), prompt, outputSchema router flow Declares labelled route branches. Passes its input through at run time: all outgoing edges run. Use condition to choose one. agentId (required), name, prompt condition flow Branches on a field comparison field, operator (equals, not_equals, contains, greater_than), value loop flow Repeats a body until a condition holds or the limit is reached conditionField (required), conditionValue, maxIterations (required) merge flow Combines parallel branches strategy (concatenate, summarize, pick_best), instruction, outputSchema checkpoint flow Pauses for human input prompt, timeoutSeconds sub-workflow flow Runs another workflow as a step workflowId (required) save-file sink Saves output as a file (artifact) source, format, fileName, overwrite storage-read, storage-write, storage-list integration Read, write and list files in a storage connection connectionId, location, parent, ... satellite-mcp, satellite-kb, satellite-skill resource Attach an MCP server, knowledge base or skill to an agent or pipeline satelliteType, resourceId, toolAllowlist

GET /api/v1/workflow-node-types returns the full registry: required fields, ports (handles) and which node types each node may connect to.

docs.title: Connection types
docs.text: data.connectionType Meaning sequential (default) Run the target after the source consult An agent consults another agent handoff An agent hands the conversation over route A labelled branch out of a condition (or router); needs a label in data.condition attachment A resource node attached to an agent or pipeline; carries no data and schedules nothing

docs.title: Route to a specialist
docs.text:
router and hub nodes pass their input through

At run time a router (and a hub) node does not call its agent or choose a branch: every outgoing edge runs. To send a request to one of two specialists, classify it with an agent that returns structured output and branch with a condition node (Branch on a value). For more than two branches chain condition nodes, or use the legacy routing workflow type.

docs.title: Parallel branches and merge
docs.text:
Two edges leave start; a merge node combines the results. A merge needs at least two incoming branches.

{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "pricing", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "b", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "legal", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "m", "type": "merge", "data": {"name": "combined", "strategy": "summarize"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "s", "target": "b"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "a", "target": "m", "targetHandle": "target-top-1"},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "b", "target": "m", "targetHandle": "target-top-2"},
    {"id": "e5", "source": "m", "target": "e"}
  ]
}

Strategies: concatenate joins the outputs, summarize asks a model to summarize them, pick_best chooses one. maxConcurrency (1 to 32, default 8) at the top of the definition limits how many agent and sub-workflow calls run at the same time.

docs.title: Branch on a value
docs.text:
Use structured output so the condition has a field to read.

{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {
      "name": "classify", "agentId": "<agent>",
      "outputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"urgent": {"type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["urgent"]}
    }},
    {"id": "c", "type": "condition", "data": {"name": "gate", "field": "urgent", "operator": "equals", "value": "true"}},
    {"id": "x", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "escalate", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "y", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "normal", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "c"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "c", "target": "x", "sourceHandle": "source-true", "data": {"connectionType": "route", "condition": "yes"}},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "c", "target": "y", "sourceHandle": "source-false", "data": {"connectionType": "route", "condition": "no"}},
    {"id": "e5", "source": "x", "target": "e"},
    {"id": "e6", "source": "y", "target": "e"}
  ]
}

A condition needs at least two route edges with distinct labels. How it works at run time:

  • field is a key of the incoming JSON object, which is the output of the upstream node (use outputSchema so the agent returns JSON). It is not a template: {{nodes.classify.json.urgent}} would be rendered first and its result used as the key, which never matches. Leave field empty to compare the whole input text.
  • operator is equals, not_equals, contains or greater_than. Comparisons ignore case; greater_than compares numbers.
  • When the condition holds, edges labelled true or yes run; otherwise edges labelled false or no run. An edge labelled default (or with no label) always runs. Any other label is accepted by validation but never taken. The label is data.condition, or true/false from sourceHandle source-true/source-false when no label is set.

docs.title: Loop until done
docs.text:
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "l", "type": "loop", "data": {"name": "refine", "conditionField": "done", "conditionValue": "true", "maxIterations": 3}},
    {"id": "w", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "rewrite", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "v", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "review", "agentId": "<agent>", "outputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"done": {"type": "boolean"}}}}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "l"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "l", "target": "w", "sourceHandle": "source-body"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "w", "target": "v"},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "v", "target": "l"},
    {"id": "e5", "source": "l", "target": "e", "sourceHandle": "source-exit"}
  ]
}

The body leaves from source-body and comes back to the loop node; the continuation leaves from source-exit. conditionField is a key of the JSON output of the node that returns to the loop (here the review agent's structured output), not a template. The loop exits when that value equals conditionValue (ignoring case). maxIterations must be above 0; it is clamped to 1 to 50 and defaults to 5.

docs.title: Pause for approval
docs.text:
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "draft", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "k", "type": "checkpoint", "data": {"name": "approval", "prompt": "Approve this draft?\n{{nodes.draft.output}}"}},
    {"id": "b", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "publish", "agentId": "<agent>", "prompt": "Finalize: {{nodes.draft.output}}\nReviewer said: {{nodes.approval.output}}"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "k"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "k", "target": "b"},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "b", "target": "e"}
  ]
}

The run stops with status: "awaiting_input" and the rendered prompt. The answer becomes the checkpoint node's output, here {{nodes.approval.output}}. See Human approval checkpoint.

docs.title: Attach resources
docs.text:
Give an agent a knowledge base, MCP server or skill by adding a resource node and an attachment edge from the resource to the agent:

{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "support", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "kb", "type": "satellite-kb", "data": {"satelliteType": "kb", "resourceId": "<knowledge base id>"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "e"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "kb", "target": "a", "data": {"connectionType": "attachment"}}
  ]
}
  • resourceId is the id of the knowledge base, MCP server or skill. satelliteType is kb, mcp or skill and must match the node type.
  • For MCP you can add toolAllowlist (at most 100 unique tool names) to expose only some tools.
  • Limits per target: 5 MCP servers and 3 knowledge bases. One resource node may serve several agents. Routers, hubs and message hubs take no attachments.

docs.title: Save a file
docs.text:
{"id": "f", "type": "save-file", "data": {"name": "save", "format": "markdown", "fileName": "report", "source": "workflow_output"}}

Formats: markdown, text, json, html, csv, docx, xlsx. The node outputs the file as an artifact, also readable as nodes.save.files.

docs.title: Inputs, variables and expressions
docs.text:
Text fields of a node (for example prompt) accept {{ expression }}.

Source Reads input.<name> A declared run input. input.message is the run message. vars.<name> A value from variables nodes.<name>.output The text output of an earlier node nodes.<name>.json.<path> A field of a structured output, for example nodes.classify.json.items[0].id nodes.<name>.files Files an earlier node produced run, now, loop, item Run metadata, time, loop and item context

Filters chain with |: date, default, eq, first, gt, gte, if, join, json, last, length, lower, lt, lte, ne, not, number, replace, split, trim, truncate, upper, url_encode. Example: {{ input.topic | trim | upper }}.

Rules:

  • Reference only nodes that run before the node holding the expression, and only names that exist.
  • nodes.<name>.json.<path> must lie inside that node's outputSchema when it has one.
  • Declare inputs as {name, type, required, default, description, sensitive} with type string, number, boolean or json. message is reserved.
  • A sensitive input is masked as *** in stored traces. Do not use it in checkpoint prompts or file names.
  • Invalid inputs at run time return 422 with detail.code = WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID and a list of {name, code, message}.

docs.title: Structured output
docs.text: Set data.outputSchema (a JSON Schema subset) on an agent, pipeline or merge node to get validated JSON, readable as nodes.<name>.json.<path>. A result that does not match fails the node with SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED after the repair attempts, and a node error fails the run. On a merge node the schema applies only to the summarize and pick_best strategies (with concatenate it is ignored and validation warns OUTPUT_SCHEMA_IGNORED).

docs.title: Validate before you save
docs.text:
POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/validate checks a graph and returns every issue. Send an unsaved graph in the body, or an empty object to check the saved one. Add "requireNames": true to get NODE_NAME_MISSING warnings.

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/validate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"graph": {"nodes": [], "edges": []}}'

{
  "valid": false,
  "errors": [
    {"code": "NO_START", "message": "Workflow must have exactly one start node", "severity": "error", "node_id": null, "edge_id": null, "input_name": null, "field": null},
    {"code": "NO_END", "message": "Workflow must have at least one end node", "severity": "error", "node_id": null, "edge_id": null, "input_name": null, "field": null}
  ],
  "warnings": [
    {"code": "EMPTY_WORKFLOW", "message": "Workflow has no executable nodes", "severity": "warning", "node_id": null, "edge_id": null, "input_name": null, "field": null}
  ]
}

Errors must be fixed before you run the workflow; warnings are advice. Saving rejects (422) invalid, reserved or duplicate node names, errors in the inputs declaration, invalid outputSchema values, invalid required_mcp_servers and attachment errors, and an unsupported or invalid definition. Graph-shape errors (start and end nodes, reachability, branches, agent references, template references) are not rejected at save time and surface when the run starts (for example 400 Composite workflow must have a Start node), so always validate first. Common codes:

Code Meaning and fix NO_START, MULTIPLE_START, NO_END Exactly one start and at least one end START_UNREACHABLE_END Connect the graph so an end node is reachable ORPHAN_NODE (error), UNREACHABLE_NODE (warning) Connect the node or remove it CYCLE_OUTSIDE_LOOP Cycles are allowed only through a loop node NODE_NAME_INVALID, NODE_NAME_DUPLICATE, NODE_NAME_RESERVED Use a unique lowercase name that is not input, item, loop, nodes, now, run or vars AGENT_REF_MISSING An agent, router or hub node needs an agentId of an agent in this project CONDITION_BRANCHES, ROUTER_ROUTES Add route edges with distinct, non-empty labels MERGE_INPUTS A merge needs two or more incoming branches LOOP_BODY Set conditionField and maxIterations above 0 SCHEMA_INVALID outputSchema uses features outside the supported subset TEMPLATE_NODE_NOT_UPSTREAM A template reads nodes.<name> of a node that does not run before it. Reorder the graph or read an earlier node. MCP_UNAVAILABLE (run) A required MCP server was not connected

The complete catalog with meanings, severities and fix hints is GET /api/v1/workflow-validation-codes.

Workflow for generating graphs

  1. Read the node type registry and the definition schema.
  2. Draft the graph with one start and one end.
  3. Call validate with the draft in the body; fix every error; repeat until valid is true. Validation needs an existing workflow id in the path, so create a placeholder workflow first (for example with an empty graph) and update it when the draft is valid.
  4. Save with POST (new) or PUT (existing), then validate the saved workflow once more with an empty body.
  5. Run a test execution and inspect the trace.

docs.title: Run behaviour to know
docs.text:
• A node error fails the run. No later node starts and there are no error edges. The run status is failed, error is set and output is empty.
  • An agent node only sees the output of its incoming edges. To pass the run message plus the previous result plus an instruction, set the target's data.prompt, for example {{input.message}} then Previous result: {{nodes.<previous>.output}}. The prompt replaces the node input.
  • An edge data.instructions (legacy alias instruction) is rendered and appended to that edge's output for agent, sub-workflow, message hub and pipeline targets. A target's own non-empty prompt replaces the input, including the instruction.
