  • Top-level required_mcp_servers applies to every agent node (including agents a hub fans out to, but not agents inside router or pipeline nodes); data.required_mcp_servers adds servers for one node. If a required server is not connected the node fails with MCP_UNAVAILABLE. Without the list, an unreachable server is skipped.

docs.title: Storage nodes
docs.text:
storage-read, storage-write and storage-list use a storage connection (Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox) of the project.

  • data.connectionId is a literal UUID, never a template.
  • storage-read copies a file into an artifact and passes its input through. storage-write writes text or an earlier file into a folder and takes conflict of fail (default), overwrite or new_version. storage-list returns {entries, nextCursor}.
  • Errors carry stable codes such as storage_not_found, storage_permission_denied, storage_file_too_large and storage_path_not_allowed, and never a file path.
  • A connection without a root folder allows no write. For Google Drive the scope is drive.file: a node sees only files the app created or the user picked.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
Every PUT that leaves the workflow with a config stores a version snapshot (creating does not).

curl -s "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/versions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/versions/2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

POST .../versions/{n}/activate only changes which version is flagged active; it does not change the config that runs. To roll back, read the old version and PUT its config back.

docs.title: Python: create, validate, run
docs.text:
import httpx


def deploy_graph(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, name: str, config: dict) -> str:
    """Create the workflow, then refuse to use it when validation reports errors."""
    created = client.post(f"{scope}/workflows", json={"name": name, "type": "composite", "config": config})
    created.raise_for_status()
    workflow_id = created.json()["id"]

    report = client.post(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/validate", json={}).json()
    if not report["valid"]:
        client.delete(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}")
        raise ValueError([f"{e['code']}: {e['message']}" for e in report["errors"]])
    return workflow_id


def run(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, workflow_id: str, message: str, **inputs) -> dict:
    r = client.post(
        f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/execute",
        json={"message": message, "inputs": inputs or None},
        timeout=300,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

docs.title: Error format
docs.text:
Errors are JSON. Error bodies include a request_id that you should log and quote when you contact support. The same id is returned in the X-Request-ID response header. You can send your own X-Request-ID header to correlate a request across systems.

SimpleValidation (422)CodedConfig (400) 
{"detail": "Missing bearer token", "request_id": "7368bf69-6315-4840-aa0c-db87925e42f9"}

A malformed body names each problem. loc is the path to the field.

{
  "detail": [
    {"type": "missing", "loc": ["body", "name"], "msg": "Field required", "input": {}}
  ]
}

Some endpoints return a stable machine readable code. Branch on code, not on message.

{"detail": {"code": "email_in_use", "message": "Email is already used by a different user"}}

An invalid agent config:

{"detail": {"message": "Invalid config", "errors": [{"type": "extra_forbidden", "loc": ["bogus"], "msg": "Extra inputs are not permitted"}]}}

Streaming endpoints cannot change the HTTP status after the first byte. Failures arrive inside the stream: an SSE error event or an NDJSON object with "event": "error". Always handle them.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text: Status Meaning What to do 200, 201 Success. Creates return 201 for most resources. 202 Accepted for background work (POST .../runs) Poll the run 400 Invalid request that is not a schema error, for example an invalid agent config Fix the payload 401 Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token Log in again; do not retry blindly 403 The token is valid but not allowed: wrong tenant, missing role or scope Check the org and project ids, the role and the service token scopes 404 The resource does not exist in your tenant Check the id. A resource of another tenant also returns 404 or 403, never its content 409 Conflict, such as a duplicate email or a concurrent update Read detail.code; retry on concurrent_update 422 The body failed validation, or a workflow input is invalid Fix the payload; for workflows read detail.code and errors 429 Rate limited Wait for Retry-After seconds 5xx Server or dependency failure Retry with backoff; if it persists send the request_id to support

docs.title: Model and credential problems
docs.text:
These are not authentication errors:

Symptom Cause Fix credential_error in an agent result No verified LLM credential and the platform fallback is off Add and verify a credential, attach a model 422 Credential must be verified before attaching a model Attachment to an unverified credential Run POST .../credentials/{id}/verify 403 Org admin role required Creating credentials needs an admin membership Use an admin, see Roles Run fails with MCP_UNAVAILABLE A required MCP server is not connected Check server health Indexing stays failed The embedding model call failed Read the job's error_message; check the embedding default credential

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
• POST /auth/login, /auth/register and /auth/reset-password are limited per client IP and per account. A limited call returns 429 with Retry-After.
  • POST /llm-providers/test is limited per user.
  • Model providers apply their own limits. Archy retries rate-limited model calls with exponential backoff before failing a run.
  • Deployments can also enforce limits at their gateway. Treat every 429 as retryable after the indicated delay.

docs.title: Retrying safely
Pagination and filtering
docs.text: List endpoints that can grow take limit and offset query parameters (for example sessions, artifacts, handoff requests). Page until a response returns fewer items than limit. Filters are explicit query parameters, listed on each reference page.

docs.title: Security checklist
docs.text:
• Keep service tokens on servers only. Never ship them to browsers or mobile apps.
  • Give each integration its own service token with only the scopes it needs, and rotate it.
  • Do not log Authorization headers, provider keys or invite_link values.
  • Send provider keys only when creating or rotating a credential, over TLS.
  • Treat model output as untrusted input: validate structured output with structured_output_schema before acting on it.
  • Prefer organization-scoped credentials owned by customers (bring your own key) over sharing one key across tenants.

docs.title: Performance practices
docs.text:
• Stream for interactive UIs; use async runs for long jobs.
  • Reuse session_id for follow-up questions instead of resending history.
  • Keep knowledge bases focused and top_k small.
  • Use the cheapest model that meets quality for classification and routing steps, and a stronger one only where needed (see model attachments).
  • Set max_tokens, max_iters and token_budget on agents that call tools, so a bad prompt cannot run away.
  • Read usage regularly (token usage) and alert on spikes.

docs.title: Knowledge bases
docs.text:
A knowledge base (KB) is a collection of documents that Archy splits into chunks, embeds with your embedding model and stores in a vector index. Agents and your own code retrieve the most relevant chunks for a question (retrieval-augmented generation, RAG).

flowchart LR
    SRC[Files, URLs, Confluence] --> ING[Ingest]
    ING --> ST[(Object storage)]
    ING --> JOB[Indexing job]
    JOB --> CH[Extract and chunk]
    CH --> EMB[Embed]
    EMB --> VEC[(Vector index)]
    Q[Question] --> RET[Retrieve top-k]
    VEC --> RET
    RET --> AG[Agent or your code]

Before you start

You need a verified LLM credential and an embedding default, or a KB with its own embedding_model. All paths below start with /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}.

BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

docs.title: Create a knowledge base
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "handbook", "description": "Company handbook"}'

{
  "id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "name": "handbook",
  "description": "Company handbook",
  "embedding_model": "connection:864beb2b-32f1-4ee1-aa0c-ccdd1ba34948:text-embedding-3-small",
  "vector_store_config": {"dimensions": 1536}
}

With an organization embedding default the response shows the copied connection:<credential_id>:<model> value and may add the vector dimensions. Without a default both are null.

Field Meaning name 1 to 255 characters description Optional embedding_model Optional. Defaults to the organization embedding default. Use connection:<credential_id>:<model_name> to pin one. vector_store_config Optional vector store options, for example the vector dimensions

Choose the embedding model before you add documents. Vectors made with one model cannot be searched with another.

docs.title: Upload files
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/upload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -F "files=@handbook.pdf" -F "files=@faq.md"

Supported types: .txt, .md, .json, .html, .htm, .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .png, .jpg, .jpeg. Other extensions (for example .csv, .doc, .xls, .ppt) are rejected with 400 Unsupported file type. Each file may be up to 50 MB. An unsupported type or an oversized file is rejected for the whole request.

The response lists the created documents, normally with status: "uploaded", and indexing is queued automatically. Without a job queue the upload indexes synchronously before it returns, so a document can already be indexed or failed.

docs.title: Import from URLs
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/from-urls" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls": ["https://example.com/pricing", "https://example.com/terms"]}'

You can send up to 20 URLs. The response is a partial success: documents for the pages that were fetched and errors (url and detail) for the ones that failed. URLs pass the same SSRF validation as every outbound request.

docs.title: Import from Confluence
docs.text:
Confluence pages are read with a personal Atlassian connection that you create once (see Connections and integrations). Pass its id:

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/from-confluence" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"integration_id\": \"$INTEGRATION_ID\", \"page_urls\": [\"https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123/Runbook\"], \"include_children\": true, \"max_depth\": 3}"

For large spaces use the background import (POST .../confluence-imports) and refresh later with POST .../sources/{source_id}/confluence-sync. Each import is tracked as a source; GET .../sources lists them and POST .../sources/{source_id}/sync re-syncs one.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
After an upload Archy indexes each document in the background. You can also drive it yourself.

Goal Request Index every document (async) POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/index Index every document and wait POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/index-sync Index one document (async job) POST .../documents/{doc}/index-jobs Poll one job GET .../documents/{doc}/index-jobs/{job} Summary of the whole KB GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/stats 
curl -s "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

{"files_total": 12, "indexed_total": 10, "indexing_total": 2}

A job has status queued, running, succeeded or failed; a failed job reports error_type and error_message. A document's own status moves uploaded, indexing, indexed or failed. POST .../index re-queues every document of the knowledge base (each document has at most one job, which is reset) and returns 503 when the queue is unavailable. POST .../index-sync processes only documents that are not yet indexed and waits for the result.

docs.title: Query
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?", "top_k": 5, "retrieval_strategy": "hybrid"}'

{
  "kb_id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
  "query": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?",
  "results": [
    {
      "chunk_id": "c1f0...",
      "score": 0.83,
      "content": "Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.",
      "metadata": {"filename": "handbook.md"}
    }
  ]
}
Field Values query 1 to 20,000 characters top_k 1 to 50, default 5 retrieval_strategy hybrid (default: vector plus lexical), vector (similarity only), graph (expands results by shared entities for multi-hop questions)

docs.title: Use a knowledge base from an agent
docs.text:
Set the KB in the agent config. The agent retrieves context before it answers.

{
  "name": "support-assistant",
  "config": {
    "sys_prompt": "Answer only from the knowledge base. Say when you do not know.",
    "knowledge_base_id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
    "knowledge_base_top_k": 4
  }
}

POST .../agents/{agent_id}/query with {"kb_id", "query", "top_k", "min_score"} is a retrieval preview, not a model call: it streams NDJSON events agent_start, retrieval (the retrieved chunks) and agent_final, whose response joins the retrieved chunks. It does not use the agent's model or configuration. To get a model answer, query the agent normally (Running and streaming).

docs.title: Manage
docs.text: Action Request List knowledge bases GET .../knowledge-bases Usage across knowledge bases GET .../knowledge-bases/usage List documents GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents Delete a document DELETE .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents/{doc} Export metadata, sources and documents GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/export Delete a knowledge base DELETE .../knowledge-bases/{kb}

docs.title: Python: upload and wait
docs.text:
import time
import httpx


def add_files_and_wait(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, kb_id: str, paths: list[str], timeout: int = 600) -> dict:
    files = [("files", (p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], open(p, "rb"))) for p in paths]
    client.post(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/documents/upload", files=files).raise_for_status()

    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        stats = client.get(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/stats").json()
        if stats["indexing_total"] == 0 and stats["files_total"] > 0:
            return stats
        time.sleep(2)
    raise TimeoutError("indexing did not finish")


# scope = f"/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}"

If indexed_total is lower than files_total after indexing_total reaches 0, some documents failed: list them with GET .../documents and look at status.

docs.title: Practices that improve answers
docs.text:
• One knowledge base per subject. Mixing unrelated material lowers precision. Attach several KBs through workflows when an agent needs more than one.
  • Test retrieval first. Call /query with real questions and read the chunks before you blame the agent prompt.
  • Keep top_k small. 3 to 8 chunks is usually enough; more adds noise and cost.
  • Prefer text-rich sources. Scanned images contain less retrievable text than PDFs with a text layer.
  • Do not change the embedding model of a populated KB. Create a new KB and re-ingest instead.
  • Tell the agent what to do when the answer is missing. "Say you do not know" in the system prompt prevents invented answers.

docs.title: LLM providers and models
docs.text:
Archy uses a bring-your-own-LLM model: every organization connects its own provider and chooses which model each agent runs on. Provider API keys are encrypted at rest and are never returned by any endpoint.

flowchart LR
    CRED[LLM credential<br/>provider, base URL, API key] -->|verify| OK[Verified]
    OK --> ATT[Model attachment<br/>credential + model name]
    ATT --> A1[Agent]
    ATT --> A2[Project default]
    ATT --> A3[Organization default]
    OK --> EMB[Embedding default<br/>for knowledge bases]

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/llm-providers/presets returns the catalog (no secrets). A preset maps a friendly choice to a backend provider type plus defaults.

Preset key provider to send Default base_url Notes azure_openai azure_openai your resource endpoint (required) Also needs api_version (default 2024-12-01-preview). The model name is the deployment name. openai openai https://api.openai.com/v1 groq openai_compatible https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 deepseek deepseek https://api.deepseek.com Chat only; no embeddings. gemini openai_compatible https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai claude openai_compatible https://api.anthropic.com/v1 cloudflare openai_compatible none; the preset returns base_url_template https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/v1 Replace {account_id} and send the result as base_url. ollama ollama http://localhost:11434 Local models. The operator must allow local URLs. custom openai_compatible none (required) Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Providers whose models can be listed (supports_model_list is true in the presets) are openai, deepseek, ollama and every openai_compatible preset. azure_openai cannot list deployments.

docs.title: Add a credential
docs.text:
Changing LLM configuration needs an admin: creating, updating, deleting, setting a default and verifying credentials, and also model attachments, the platform default model and the embedding default. You are an admin when you have the admin role on the project in your token, the org-admin role from your identity provider, or a platform admin grant. Reads (list, get, models, presets, test) need only membership. See Roles.

The credential belongs to the organization of your token. Set project_id to scope it to one project.

OpenAIAzure OpenAIAnthropic ClaudeOllama (local) 
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider": "openai", "display_name": "OpenAI production", "api_key": "<key>"}'

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "azure_openai",
    "display_name": "Azure EU",
    "api_key": "<key>",
    "base_url": "https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/",
    "api_version": "2024-12-01-preview",
    "extra_config": {"test_model": "<your deployment name>"}
  }'

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "openai_compatible",
    "display_name": "Claude",
    "api_key": "<key>",
    "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1",
    "extra_config": {"test_model": "<a Claude model id>"}
  }'

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider": "ollama", "display_name": "Local Ollama", "base_url": "http://localhost:11434"}'

Outbound URLs are validated against private and loopback ranges. For local development the operator sets SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS=true; keep it false in shared environments.

The response never contains the key. has_api_key tells you that one is stored:

{
  "id": "864beb2b-32f1-4ee1-aa0c-ccdd1ba34948",
  "org_id": "35af6d8d-f874-4b2b-9222-122092075307",
  "project_id": null,
  "provider": "openai",
  "display_name": "OpenAI prod",
  "has_api_key": true,
  "base_url": null,
  "api_version": null,
  "extra_config": {},
  "is_default": false,
  "is_verified": false,
  "verified_at": null,
  "key_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:35.717955",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:35.717957"
}

docs.title: Test and verify
docs.text:
You can test a key before saving it. This makes a one token request and is rate limited per user:

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider": "openai", "api_key": "<key>", "model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"}'
# {"success": true, "latency_ms": 380, "model_used": "gpt-4o-mini", "error": null}

After saving, verify the stored credential. Runtime only uses verified credentials.

Verification sends a one token request to the model named in extra_config.test_model. Without it, openai and azure_openai use gpt-4o-mini, deepseek uses deepseek-chat and ollama uses llama3. openai_compatible providers (Groq, Gemini, Claude, Cloudflare, custom) have no default: verification fails with "No test model configured" until you set extra_config.test_model. For Azure, use a deployment name that exists in your resource.

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/$CRED_ID/verify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

{"success": false, "is_verified": false, "verified_at": null, "latency_ms": null, "error": "Authentication failed — check your API key"}

Changing api_key or base_url resets verification, so verify again after a rotation.

List the models a credential offers (providers that support listing return names; for the others supports_listing is false and you type the model name):

curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/$CRED_ID/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
# {"models": ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "text-embedding-3-small"], "supports_listing": true}

docs.title: Manage credentials
docs.text: Action Request List GET /llm-providers/credentials Get one GET /llm-providers/credentials/{id} Rename, rotate key or change URL PUT /llm-providers/credentials/{id} with only the fields to change Mark as the default of its scope POST /llm-providers/credentials/{id}/set-default Delete DELETE /llm-providers/credentials/{id}

docs.title: Choose the model: attachments
docs.text:
A model attachment pins a (credential, model_name) pair to a target. There are three targets.

Target Endpoint Effect Agent /llm-providers/model-attachments/agents/{agent_id} Only that agent Project /llm-providers/model-attachments/projects/{project_id} Agents in that project without their own attachment Organization /llm-providers/model-attachments/org Agents everywhere without a closer attachment

Each target supports GET, PUT and DELETE. The credential must be verified or PUT returns 422.

# Organization default model
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"gpt-4o-mini\"}"

# A stronger model for one agent
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/agents/$AGENT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"gpt-4o\"}"

docs.title: Which model runs
docs.text:
For every execution Archy walks this list and uses the first tier that applies:

  1. Agent attachment.
  2. Agent config pin: config.model with both credential_id and model_name.
  3. Project attachment.
  4. Project platform default model (see below).
  5. Organization attachment.
  6. Organization platform default model.
  7. Legacy agent model_name with no credential. This runs on the platform's own model service, not on your credential.

If none of these applies, the agent has no model and the call fails (or answers in echo mode, see Agents). Agents built by the platform itself fall back to the operator's default model through tier 7.

A tier is skipped when its credential is missing or unverified. A stored credential that cannot be decrypted is an error, never a silent fallback. A project platform default model (tier 4) wins over an organization attachment (tier 5). The flow diagram shows the same logic.

is_default does not choose the model

The is_default flag marks a credential as the default of its scope in the credential list, but only attachments decide which model runs for organization and project defaults. Always create an attachment.

Do not set only config.model.model_name

An agent whose config.model has a model_name but no credential_id does not pin a model. If a project or organization attachment (or a platform default model) exists, that wins and the agent's model_name is ignored. Otherwise the agent runs model_name on the platform model service, not on your provider. To pin a model to one agent use an agent attachment, or set both credential_id and model_name.

docs.title: Platform default model overrides
docs.text:
Organizations that use the platform's hosted model (no credential) can still pick the deployment name. These tiers, and tier 7, run only when the organization allows the platform fallback (allow_platform_llm_fallback); otherwise the call fails with a credential_error.

Scope Endpoint Organization GET, PUT, DELETE /llm-providers/platform-default-model with {"model_name": "..."} Project .../platform-default-model/projects/{project_id}

docs.title: When nothing is configured
docs.text:
If an organization has no usable credential and the platform fallback is disabled for it, execution fails with a clear message instead of using a shared key:

{
  "mode": "credential_error",
  "credential_error": "No LLM provider credential is configured for this organization and platform fallback is disabled. Add an LLM provider credential ..."
}

Add and verify a credential, attach a model, and retry. This is not an authentication error; 401 always means the bearer token is bad.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Knowledge bases embed text with a model from one of your credentials. Set the organization default once; each new knowledge base created without its own embedding_model copies it, so changing the default later never invalidates vectors that already exist.

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"text-embedding-3-small\", \"dimensions\": 1536}"
  • Providers with embeddings: azure_openai, openai, openai_compatible, ollama. DeepSeek has no embeddings endpoint.
  • GET returns the default with available: false if its credential was deleted or is no longer verified; new knowledge bases then fail until you change or clear it (DELETE).
  • A knowledge base can also name its own model: embedding_model: "connection:<credential_id>:<model_name>".

docs.title: A helper in Python
docs.text:
import httpx


def connect_openai(client: httpx.Client, api_key: str) -> str:
    """Create, verify and attach an OpenAI credential as the organization default. Returns its id."""
    cred = client.post(
        "/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials",
        json={"provider": "openai", "display_name": "OpenAI", "api_key": api_key},
    )
    cred.raise_for_status()
    cred_id = cred.json()["id"]

    check = client.post(f"/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/{cred_id}/verify").json()
    if not check["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(check["error"])

    for url, body in (
        ("/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org", {"credential_id": cred_id, "model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"}),
        (
            "/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default",
            {"credential_id": cred_id, "model_name": "text-embedding-3-small", "dimensions": 1536},
        ),
    ):
        client.put(url, json=body).raise_for_status()
    return cred_id

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Each credential records the key_id it was encrypted under, so operators can rotate encryption keys without downtime.
  • Responses and logs never include the key. Provide it only when creating or rotating.
  • base_url values are validated against SSRF rules before any request leaves the platform.
  • Credentials are tenant scoped. An organization can never resolve another organization's credential.

docs.title: External MCP servers and skills
docs.text:
Agents become more useful when they can act: search Jira, query a database, call your internal API. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the standard way to expose such tools. In Archy you register an MCP server once and attach it to the agents that may use it.

Two different MCP topics

This page is about MCP servers that agents call (tools for your agents). To let an AI client call Archy (Claude, Copilot, Cursor, ...), see MCP.

flowchart LR
    REG[Registered MCP server] -->|attach| AG[Agent]
    AG -->|tool call| REG
    REG --> EXT[Your tool service]
    HC[Health scheduler] -->|checks| REG
    AG --> LOG[Tool invocation log]

All paths below start with /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}.

BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

docs.title: Register a server
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/mcp-servers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "tickets",
    "transport": "http",
    "config": {
      "base_url": "https://mcp.example.com",
      "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <service key for that server>"}
    }
  }'
Field Meaning name Human readable name (not enforced unique). required_mcp_servers entries match a server by id or by name, ignoring case and punctuation. transport http (or streamable-http) for a remote server. stdio servers are created from an organization template (see below); transport is ignored for template instances. config For http: base_url, optional path (default /mcp), headers and stateful. env values apply only to stdio template instances; for template instances config is validated against the template's schema (422 on mismatch). template_id, instance_label Create an instance of an organization template

Secrets are write-only. All headers and env values, keys with credential-like names (token, api_key, password, secret), template fields marked x-sensitive and credentials inside URLs are encrypted at rest and returned as ***REDACTED*** by every endpoint. To keep a secret, send the placeholder back unchanged. To change it, send the new value. If an update adds a new URL origin, or changes a non-secret entry in the same headers or env block, re-enter the secrets too. Values that start with enc:v1: are rejected (422), and saving a secret fails with 503 when the deployment has no encryption key.

Remote server URLs are validated against SSRF rules. URLs must use https://; plain http://, private and loopback addresses need an operator setting (SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS, SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS or SSRF_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS), and cloud metadata hosts are always blocked.

docs.title: Attach to an agent
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/mcp-servers/$SERVER_ID/attach" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/mcp-servers" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/mcp-servers/$SERVER_ID/detach" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

In a composite workflow you can attach a server to one node with a satellite-mcp resource node instead. See Attach resources.

docs.title: Control which tools run
docs.text:
Where How Per workflow node toolAllowlist on the satellite-mcp node (omit to allow all) Per run mcp_enabled: false turns MCP off; mcp_tool_allowlist: ["jira_get_issue"] registers only those tools (server side names, without the server prefix) Required servers required_mcp_servers on a sequential or composite workflow fails the run with MCP_UNAVAILABLE when a server is down, instead of silently skipping it

Pass the per-run options in the body of /execute, /execute/stream or /runs. They are not stored.

docs.title: Health and observability
docs.text:
Need Request Latest health of a server GET .../mcp-servers/{server_id}/health/latest History GET .../mcp-servers/{server_id}/health Check now (platform admins only; at most once per 30 seconds per server, otherwise 429) POST .../mcp-servers/{server_id}/health/check Status of an agent's servers GET .../agents/{agent_id}/mcp-status Tool invocation log GET .../mcp/tool-invocations One invocation GET .../mcp/tool-invocations/{invocation_id} Metrics of invocations GET .../mcp/tool-invocations/metrics Re-run an invocation (at most 10 per minute per project) POST .../mcp/tool-invocations/{invocation_id}/replay

A background scheduler checks each project's servers every 60 seconds by default (GET {base_url}/health for HTTP servers) and backs off up to 300 seconds after failures. The interval cannot be changed through the API; operators can turn the scheduler off with HEALTH_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false.

docs.title: Organization templates
docs.text:
Platform administrators publish templates that describe how to reach or launch a server and which config fields are sensitive. Projects then create instances from a template with their own values. Templates are the only way to run stdio servers: creating a stdio server without a template returns 403, and the command always comes from the template and must be an approved command (default npx, uvx, uv, node, python, python3). An instance can only set the env keys its template declares.

# List the templates of the organization
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/mcp-templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Create an instance from a template
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/mcp-servers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"name\": \"jira-prod\", \"transport\": \"stdio\", \"template_id\": \"$TEMPLATE_ID\", \"instance_label\": \"production\", \"config\": {}}"

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is an instruction set (a SKILL.md document) that is appended to the system prompt on every run of an agent it is enabled or attached on. There are two kinds.

  • Skills on disk: shipped with the deployment. GET /api/v1/skills lists them, GET /api/v1/skills/{skill_id} shows metadata and GET /api/v1/skills/{skill_id}/content returns the SKILL.md. Enable them on an agent with config.skills_enabled.
  • Skills in the database: created through the API and scoped to a project.
# Create a skill
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/skills" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "refund-policy", "description": "How to handle refund requests", "skill_content": "# Refund policy\n\nRefunds are allowed within 30 days..."}'

# Attach it to an agent
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/skills" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"skill_id\": \"$SKILL_ID\"}"

# List, detach
curl -s "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/skills" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/skills/$SKILL_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

docs.title: Atlassian access for agents
docs.text: An agent can use Jira and Confluence on behalf of a person. The person creates a personal Atlassian connection (POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/integrations/atlassian), then grants it to an agent (PUT .../agents/{agent_id}/integration-grants). The credentials never leave the platform and the agent acts only while that person initiates the run. See the Connections and integrations reference.

docs.title: Provisioning tenants and users
docs.text:
If you embed Archy in your own product, your backend creates the tenants. Provisioning endpoints let a service token create organizations, projects and users with ids that you choose, so your customer records and Archy tenants map one to one.

You need

A service token with the scopes you use (see Authentication). All provisioning calls are idempotent upserts: calling them again with the same ids is safe, which makes them easy to retry from an outbox or a job queue.

flowchart LR
    CUST[Your customer record] -->|deterministic UUID| ORG[Organization]
    CUST -->|per workspace| PRJ[Project]
    CUST -->|per user| USR[User and membership]
    ORG --> PRJ
    PRJ --> USR

docs.title: Choose your ids
docs.text:
Archy accepts any UUID. Derive them deterministically from your own ids so that you never have to store a mapping and a retry is always the same call:

import uuid

ARCHY_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("6f1c2f66-8f5b-4c60-9a32-0d8f0a1a2b3c")  # pick one and keep it forever


def archy_id(kind: str, your_id: str) -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid5(ARCHY_NAMESPACE, f"{kind}:{your_id}"))


org_id = archy_id("org", "customer-1042")
project_id = archy_id("project", "customer-1042/default")
user_id = archy_id("user", "user-77")

docs.title: Create an organization
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id} · scope provision:org

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Globex", "settings": {"plan": "team"}}'

{"org_id": "084d6557-5155-4851-88e3-192bea708c64", "created": true}

settings is a free-form object stored on the organization. Calling again updates name, replaces settings as a whole (omitting it clears it) and returns created: false.

Settings also hold platform keys

Archy stores the organization's embedding default, platform default model and the allow_platform_llm_fallback flag in the same settings object. A later upsert that does not send them removes them. Keep your own keys in settings and read the current value (or re-apply those defaults) before you re-provision an organization that already has LLM settings.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id} · scope provision:project

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Helpdesk", "description": "Support workspace"}'
Status Meaning 200 Created or updated 404 The organization does not exist. Create it first. 409 with project_org_conflict The project id already exists under another organization. Archy never moves a project between organizations.

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/{user_id} · scope provision:user

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/$USER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\": \"ada@globex.example\", \"org_id\": \"$ORG_ID\", \"project_id\": \"$PROJECT_ID\"}"

{
  "user_id": "3a2f6241-68c1-441a-bc51-fafa36ac9fda",
  "org_id": "084d6557-5155-4851-88e3-192bea708c64",
  "project_id": "5348cb7c-a373-498c-9daf-bf74e24abbb8",
  "created": true
}

What this call does:

  • Creates the user if the id is new, with a random unusable password. Your system, or the invite flow, is the source of truth for how this user signs in.
  • Adds a membership with the admin role on the project. A user can be provisioned into many projects and organizations by calling again.
  • For an existing user it only adds the membership. It never changes the email, the password, is_active or the user's active tenant.

Conflicts return 409 with a machine readable detail.code:

Code Cause email_in_use Another user already owns this email email_mismatch The user id exists with a different email; emails never change concurrent_update Two writers raced; retry

If the user_id already belongs to another user, the call fails with email_mismatch (or email_in_use).

docs.title: Bootstrap an organization admin
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite · scope provision:user

Creates (or finds) a human admin by email, grants access to projects, and returns a single-use set-password link you can send in your own onboarding email.

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/admins/invite" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "boss@globex.example"}'

{
  "user_id": "71130610-41da-45f8-a058-9c4ba739a71d",
  "org_id": "084d6557-5155-4851-88e3-192bea708c64",
  "project_ids": ["5348cb7c-a373-498c-9daf-bf74e24abbb8"],
  "created_user": true,
  "existing_user": false,
  "existing_org_ids": [],
  "invite_link": "https://app.example.com/reset-password?token=Fg3UMgFDs8J-25ic0K3gBsEK_9H_sw83XSpfgfqx10Y",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-17T10:09:04.679975Z"
}
Request field Meaning email Required. Matched case-insensitively. user_id Optional id to use when the user is created. If it already belongs to another user the call fails with 409 user_id_in_use. project_ids Projects to grant. Omit to grant all current projects of the organization. role admin (default) or permission-admin. A re-invite changes a role only when you pass one. is_active Applied only when the user is created.

Notes:

  • The organization must already have at least one project (400 otherwise).
  • For an existing user (same email) no link is issued: invite_link and expires_at are null, existing_user is true, and only memberships are added. existing_org_ids is internal information; do not show it to tenant users.
  • The link base is the deployment setting PASSWORD_RESET_URL_BASE. The link carries a token query parameter. Your onboarding page posts it to POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password with the new password, and the user can then log in.

To finish the bootstrap without a browser (scripts, tests, CI):

TOKEN=$(echo "$INVITE" | jq -r '.invite_link' | sed 's/.*token=//')
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"token\": \"$TOKEN\", \"new_password\": \"a-long-unique-passphrase\"}"

docs.title: Look up a user by email
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/by-email/{email} · scope provision:user:read

curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/by-email/ada@globex.example" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN"

Returns the user id and active tenant, or 404. Several accounts that differ only by case give 409 email_ambiguous.

docs.title: Push LLM credentials (optional)
docs.text:
If your product stores the customer's provider keys, you can push them instead of asking the customer to call the LLM endpoints. Scope provision:credential.

PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/llm-credentials

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/llm-credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "credentials": [{
      "credential_id": "5e1f3c52-2f67-4b5e-9d51-0c2f7f3e8a10",
      "provider": "openai",
      "display_name": "Customer OpenAI",
      "api_key": "<provider key>",
      "is_default": true
    }]
  }'

{"org_id": "...", "upserted": 1, "created": 1, "updated": 0}
  • Items are upserted by credential_id, which you supply, so retries are safe.
  • A credential can be scoped to a project with project_id.
  • DELETE .../llm-credentials/{credential_id} is idempotent: deleting an absent credential returns deleted: false, not 404. A credential owned by another organization is never deleted (409).
  • Every push sets is_verified, verified_at and is_default to the values you send (all default to false). Send is_verified: true on every push if you verified the key yourself; a later push without it un-verifies a credential, and unverified credentials are skipped at runtime. To verify through Archy instead, an admin user calls POST /llm-providers/credentials/{id}/verify.
  • project_id is fixed when a credential is first created; later pushes do not move it.

docs.title: Signed requests
docs.text:
A deployment can require signed requests on this channel (PROVISIONING_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED). The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical string, sent in three headers:

import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time


def signed_headers(secret: str, method: str, path: str, body: bytes) -> dict[str, str]:
    timestamp = str(int(time.time()))
    nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
    signing_string = "\n".join([method.upper(), path, timestamp, nonce, hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()])
    signature = hmac.new(secret.encode(), signing_string.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return {"X-Archy-Timestamp": timestamp, "X-Archy-Nonce": nonce, "X-Archy-Signature": signature}

path is the request path without query string. The timestamp must be within the configured window (300 seconds by default) and every nonce is accepted once. A failed check returns 401 Invalid request signature.

docs.title: How your users sign in
docs.text:
The provisioned user exists; now they need a token. Pick one:

Approach How Choose when Set-password link Send the invite_link; the user sets a password and logs in with POST /auth/login You want Archy to own the credentials Your identity provider The operator enables external auth; your IdP issues tokens with org_id and project_id claims You already run SSO Your backend as proxy Your backend holds a user token (for example from a service account user) and calls Archy for your users The end user never talks to Archy directly

docs.title: A provisioning client in Python
docs.text:
import os
import httpx


class Provisioner:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, service_token: str) -> None:
        self.http = httpx.Client(
            base_url=base_url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {service_token}"}, timeout=30
        )

    def _send(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code == 409:
            raise RuntimeError(response.json()["detail"])  # {"code": ..., "message": ...}
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()

    def ensure_org(self, org_id: str, name: str) -> dict:
        return self._send("PUT", f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}", json={"name": name})

    def ensure_project(self, org_id: str, project_id: str, name: str) -> dict:
        return self._send(
            "PUT",
            f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}",
            json={"name": name},
        )

    def invite_admin(self, org_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
        return self._send(
            "POST", f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite", json={"email": email}
        )


p = Provisioner(os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"], os.environ["SERVICE_TOKEN"])
# archy_id is the helper from "Choose your ids"
org, project = archy_id("org", "customer-1042"), archy_id("project", "customer-1042/default")
p.ensure_org(org, "Globex")
p.ensure_project(org, project, "Helpdesk")
print(p.invite_admin(org, "boss@globex.example")["invite_link"])

docs.title: Error reference
docs.text:
Status Typical cause 400 Inviting an admin into an organization without projects 401 Invalid token or invalid request signature 403 Missing scopes: ... Mint the token with the named scope 403 Service token required A user token was used on a provisioning route 403 Forbidden enforce binding mode and the token lacks tenant:act or does not list the organization in org_ids (PUT .../users/{id} checks the organization in the request body) 404 Organization or project not found 409 See the codes above

Continue with LLM providers and models.

docs.title: Running and streaming
docs.text:
Archy offers three ways to execute an agent or workflow. Pick by what your caller can do.

Mode Use when Agent Workflow Synchronous Short tasks; you can wait for the final result POST /agents/{id}/query POST .../workflows/{id}/execute Streaming A UI should show progress as it happens POST .../agents/{id}/chat/stream (SSE) POST .../workflows/{id}/execute/stream (SSE) Asynchronous Your caller cannot hold a connection open (serverless, Atlassian Forge, queues) POST .../workflows/{id}/runs, then GET .../runs/{run_id}

All requests need a bearer token (Authentication).

docs.title: Server-Sent Events (SSE)
docs.text:
Streaming endpoints respond with Content-Type: text/event-stream. Each event is two lines and a blank line:

event: delta
data: {"delta": "Support hours are "}

Use fetch, not EventSource

Browsers' EventSource cannot send an Authorization header or a POST body. Read the stream with fetch and a ReadableStream, or let your backend relay it.

docs.title: Agent chat stream
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_id}/chat/stream with {"message": "...", "session_id": "..."}.

Event data start {"agent_id", "session_id"} delta {"delta": "<text chunk>"}, repeated end {"agent_id", "session_id", "output", "meta"} error {"error": "execution_failed", "detail": "..."}

The error event replaces end. Handle it: the HTTP status is already 200 when it is sent.

delta events are chunks of a finished answer

The agent runs to completion first; delta events then deliver the final output in chunks of about 20 characters. There is no token-level streaming, so the first delta arrives only after the agent has finished. Use the stream to render text progressively, and show your own progress indicator until the first delta arrives. POST /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query/stream is a test stub that echoes the message; do not use it.

curlPythonTypeScript 
curl -N -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/agents/$AGENT_ID/chat/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Summarize our refund policy"}'

import json
import os

import httpx


def sse_events(response: httpx.Response):
    """Yield (event, data) pairs from an SSE response."""
    event, data_lines = "message", []
    for line in response.iter_lines():
        if line == "":
            if data_lines:
                yield event, json.loads("\n".join(data_lines))
            event, data_lines = "message", []
        elif line.startswith("event:"):
            event = line[6:].strip()
        elif line.startswith("data:"):
            data_lines.append(line[5:].lstrip())


base = os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"]
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ARCHY_TOKEN']}"}
url = f"{base}/api/v1/orgs/{os.environ['ORG_ID']}/projects/{os.environ['PROJECT_ID']}/agents/{os.environ['AGENT_ID']}/chat/stream"

with httpx.stream("POST", url, headers=headers, json={"message": "Hello"}, timeout=None) as response:
    response.raise_for_status()
    for event, data in sse_events(response):
        if event == "delta":
            print(data["delta"], end="", flush=True)
        elif event == "error":
            raise RuntimeError(data["detail"])

export async function* sse(response: Response): AsyncGenerator<{ event: string; data: any }> {
  const reader = response.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
  let buffer = "";
  for (;;) {
    const { value, done } = await reader.read();
    if (done) return;
    buffer += value;
    let boundary: number;
    while ((boundary = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
      const block = buffer.slice(0, boundary);
      buffer = buffer.slice(boundary + 2);
      let event = "message";
      const data: string[] = [];
      for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
        if (line.startsWith("event:")) event = line.slice(6).trim();
        else if (line.startsWith("data:")) data.push(line.slice(5).trimStart());
      }
      if (data.length) yield { event, data: JSON.parse(data.join("\n")) };
    }
  }
}

const response = await fetch(`${base}/api/v1/orgs/${org}/projects/${project}/agents/${agent}/chat/stream`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ message: "Hello" }),
});
for await (const { event, data } of sse(response)) {
  if (event === "delta") process.stdout.write(data.delta);
}

docs.title: NDJSON: knowledge base retrieval preview
docs.text:
POST .../agents/{agent_id}/query with {"kb_id": "...", "query": "...", "top_k": 3, "min_score": 0.2} returns application/x-ndjson: one JSON object per line with an event field: agent_start, retrieval (the retrieved chunks), agent_final (its response joins the chunks) or error (with a message). It is a retrieval preview: no model is called.

with httpx.stream("POST", url, headers=headers, json={"kb_id": kb_id, "query": "Refund window?"}, timeout=None) as r:
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line:
            event = json.loads(line)
            print(event)

docs.title: Synchronous
docs.text: POST .../workflows/{id}/execute returns when the run finishes. See Workflows for the response. Use a generous client timeout: runs can take minutes.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
POST .../workflows/{id}/execute/stream accepts the same body as execute.

Event Meaning start {"workflow_id", "workflow_type", "session_id", "run_id"} step_started, step_completed Per agent (orchestrator workflows) token, discussion Text from agents (other types) run.started, node.started, node.delta, node.completed, edge.active, run.completed The unified trace envelope: {"v", "seq", "ts", "run_id", "workflow_id", ...} structured_output The complete, validated object, sent once when a structured_output_schema is set; run.completed carries the same object end {"session_id", "output", "structured_output", "audit", "error", "structured_output_error", "run_id", "status", "pending_input"}. status is awaiting_input when the run paused at a checkpoint. error Replaces end on failure

Treat unknown fields and event types as forward compatible. Each trace envelope has a seq.

A stream cannot reattach to a run in progress

Calling the endpoint again with a session_id and ?after_seq=<last seq> first replays the persisted trace envelopes of that session with a higher seq (they are written when a run ends), and then starts a new run of the workflow with your message on that session. It does not attach to a run that is still executing, and seq restarts at 1 for each execution. For runs that must survive a disconnect, use asynchronous runs.

url = f"{base}/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/workflows/{workflow_id}/execute/stream"
body = {"message": "Run the weekly report", "inputs": {"week": "2026-W46"}}
with httpx.stream("POST", url, headers=headers, json=body, timeout=None) as r:
    for event, data in sse_events(r):
        if event == "node.started":
            print("running", data.get("node_id"))
        elif event == "end":
            print(data["status"], data["output"])

docs.title: Asynchronous runs
docs.text:
For callers that cannot stream, start a run and poll it.

# 1. Start. Same body as /execute. Returns immediately.
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/runs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Run the weekly report", "inputs": {"week": "2026-W46"}}'
# {"run_id": "…", "status": "pending"}   (HTTP 202)

# 2. Poll
curl -s "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/runs/$RUN_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

status is pending, running, awaiting_input, succeeded, failed or cancelled (a run paused at a checkpoint that was cancelled). output, structured_output, audit and error are filled once the run is succeeded or failed.

import time


def run_and_wait(client, scope: str, workflow_id: str, message: str, *, timeout: float = 600, **inputs) -> dict:
    started = client.post(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs", json={"message": message, "inputs": inputs or None})
    started.raise_for_status()
    run_id = started.json()["run_id"]

    delay, deadline = 1.0, time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        run = client.get(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs/{run_id}").json()
        if run["status"] in ("succeeded", "failed", "awaiting_input", "cancelled"):
            return run
        time.sleep(delay)
        delay = min(delay * 1.5, 10)  # back off to a 10 second poll
    raise TimeoutError(f"run {run_id} still running")

There is no endpoint that lists asynchronous runs, so keep the run_id you receive. GET .../workflows/{id}/sessions lists sessions.

Service-token runs

A run started with a service token and no acting-user identity has no initiating user. Storage nodes can then only use project and organization connections that have a root folder, not personal connections.

docs.title: Pause and resume at a checkpoint
docs.text:
When a composite workflow reaches a checkpoint node the response has status: "awaiting_input", output is the rendered prompt and pending_input describes the question: {status, question, node_id, node_name, iteration}. This holds for /execute, /resume and the stream end event. An asynchronous run reports status: "awaiting_input" with the prompt in output and the run's session_id; read the structured question from the session (GET .../workflows/{id}/sessions/{session_id}, state.pending_input).

# Resume with the answer
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/sessions/$SESSION_ID/resume" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"answer": "Approved. Add the pricing table."}'

# Or cancel; the run is marked cancelled and cannot resume
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/sessions/$SESSION_ID/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
  • answer is 1 to 32,768 characters.
  • Declared sensitive inputs are not stored with the paused run; send them again in inputs on resume. Any other key returns 422 with detail.code = WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID (INPUT_UNKNOWN), and a missing required sensitive input gives INPUT_REQUIRED. The run keeps waiting.
  • Passing the session_id of a paused run to /execute also resumes it. Invalid inputs return 422 and the run stays resumable.
  • Checkpoints expire after 7 days by default. Expiry is detected when a resume is tried: that call returns 409 and marks the run failed. Until then the session still shows awaiting_input.

The full walkthrough is in Human approval checkpoint.

docs.title: Dialog runs
docs.text: Multi-agent dialogs have their own resource: POST .../dialog-runs creates one, POST .../dialog-runs/{run_id}/execute streams it as NDJSON, and GET, PATCH and DELETE manage it. See the Workflows reference.

docs.title: Choosing timeouts
docs.text: Layer Recommendation Client read timeout for streams None (disabled) with your own idle watchdog Client timeout for sync execute 5 minutes or more Proxies and gateways Disable response buffering for text/event-stream and raise idle timeouts Polling interval 1 s growing to 10 s

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
A session is the persisted record of a conversation with an agent or a run of a workflow: messages, tool calls, retrievals, errors and the per-node trace of workflow runs.

All paths start with /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}.

Action Request List sessions (agent and workflow) GET .../sessions?limit=50&offset=0 Read one with its history GET .../sessions/{session_id} Activity events (tool calls, retrievals, errors) GET .../sessions/{session_id}/activity Files created during the session GET .../sessions/{session_id}/artifacts Rename PATCH .../sessions/{session_id}/rename Generate a name from the content POST .../sessions/{session_id}/regenerate-name Delete DELETE .../sessions/{session_id} Sessions that involved an agent GET /api/v1/agents/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_id}/sessions Workflow sessions GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/sessions (optional status filter) One workflow session with its trace GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/sessions/{session_id} 
curl -s "$BASE/sessions?limit=20" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

[
  {
    "session_id": "4e7c87f4-30d4-565f-a47b-9b4fca7f385a",
    "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:03",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:12:44",
    "name": "Refund policy question",
    "last_agent_id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e"
  }
]

Workflow sessions expose a status: completed, awaiting_input (paused at a checkpoint), failed (a checkpoint failed, for example expired) or cancelled. Note that completed only means "no waiting, failed or cancelled marker".

Build an audit view

Combine GET .../sessions/{id} (messages), .../activity (tool calls and retrievals) and, for workflows, the session trace to show users exactly what an agent did and why.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
An artifact is a file stored with a project: the output of a save-file or storage-read node, an export of a run, or an upload.

flowchart LR
    RUN[Workflow run] -->|save-file node| ART[(Artifact)]
    RUN -->|export run output| ART
    UP[Your upload] --> ART
    ART --> DL[Download]
    ART --> NODE[Later node: nodes.x.files]

docs.title: Upload
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/artifacts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@report.pdf" -F "name=weekly-report.pdf" -F "media_type=application/pdf"

Optional form fields link the file to its origin: run_id, session_id, node_id (up to 255 characters) and agent_id.

docs.title: List, read, download, delete
docs.text:
# Filter by run, node, session, media type or source
curl -s "$BASE/artifacts?run_id=$RUN_ID&limit=50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Metadata: name, media type, size, sha256, source, expiry
curl -s "$BASE/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Download (always served as an attachment)
curl -s -o report.pdf "$BASE/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID/download" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Delete (soft delete; the stored blob is removed within 24 hours)
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

docs.title: Export a run's output as a file
docs.text:
After a run finishes, turn its final output (or one node's output) into a file:

POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/runs/{run_id}/exports

The response is the new artifact. Supported formats include markdown, text, json, html, csv, docx and xlsx.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Defaults are set by the operator and can differ per deployment.

Limit Default File size 25 MB Files per run 100 Storage per project 1 GB Storage per organization 2 GB Retention 90 days

Exceeding a limit returns an error naming the limit.

docs.title: Token usage
docs.text:
Every model call records its token usage. Query it at project or organization level.

Question Project endpoint Organization endpoint Totals grouped by something GET .../token-usage/aggregations GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/aggregations Per model GET .../token-usage/metrics/by-model GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/metrics/by-model Over time GET .../token-usage/metrics/timeseries GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/metrics/timeseries Chart ready data GET .../token-usage/charts GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/charts Individual events GET .../token-usage/events 
curl -s "$BASE/token-usage/aggregations?group_by=model&token_type=total" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

{"group_by": "model", "token_type": "total", "items": []}

Query parameters of aggregations:

Parameter Values group_by model, provider, agent, workflow, project, day, week, month token_type input, output, total since, until Time window model, models, agent_id, workflow_id, session_id Filters period last_7d, last_30d or last_90d order_by, order_dir tokens, calls or group; asc or desc min_tokens, max_tokens, limit, offset Thresholds and paging (limit 1 to 200)

The timeseries endpoint takes granularity of day or hour and returns buckets with call_count, prompt_tokens and completion tokens.

Use usage data for showback and quotas in your product: group by agent or workflow to attribute cost, and poll the timeseries to alert on spikes.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
A workflow coordinates several agents (and sometimes tools and other workflows) to complete a task that one agent cannot do alone. Archy supports two families:

  • Legacy typed workflows (this page): choose a pattern such as sequential or debate and list the agents. Quick to set up.
  • Composite workflows (next page): a graph of nodes and edges with inputs, variables, conditions, loops, human checkpoints and file output. Use it when you need control.

Workflows live in /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/workflows (or /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workflows for organization scope). Every PUT that leaves the workflow with a config stores a snapshot as a new version you can list and read (creating a workflow does not). Organization-scope workflows support only create, list, get and execute; everything else on this page is project-scoped.

docs.title: Create a workflow
docs.text:
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"name\": \"draft-and-edit\",
    \"description\": \"A writer drafts, an editor improves\",
    \"type\": \"sequential\",
    \"config\": {\"agent_ids\": [\"$WRITER_ID\", \"$EDITOR_ID\"]}
  }"

{
  "id": "313bacab-956b-4366-8f82-f134407f0d61",
  "org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "scope": "project",
  "name": "draft-and-edit",
  "description": "A writer drafts, an editor improves",
  "type": "sequential",
  "config": {"agent_ids": ["26fc2a0e-...", "dd7b220d-..."]},
  "legacy_history": false,
  "executable": true
}

The config is validated against the type. A violation returns 422:

{"detail": [{"type": "value_error", "loc": ["body"], "msg": "Value error, config.agent_ids is required"}]}

docs.title: Workflow types
docs.text:
type Pattern Required config sequential Agents run one after another; each receives the previous output agent_ids (list) parallel All agents work on the same input at once; outputs are combined agent_ids dialog Agents take turns in a conversation agent_ids, optional turns (1 to 100) conversation Multi-agent conversation over a shared message hub agent_ids (at least 2), optional turns (1 to 200) routing A router agent, keyword routes or a default agent decide who handles the request (see below) default_agent_id; optional router_agent_id, routes, route_map, routing_tool_names orchestrator A manager delegates to workers, or a RAG orchestrator compares two knowledge bases manager_agent_id and worker_agent_ids, or kb_a_id and kb_b_id (optional top_k 1 to 50) business-pipeline Business agents first, then pipeline agents business_agent_ids, pipeline_agent_ids, optional business_mode (parallel or sequential) staged Ordered stages, each parallel or sequential, optionally fanned in stages (list of {agent_ids, mode, name}), optional fanin handoff Workers (agents, tools or sub-workflows) are selected by keyword matches workers (at least 2) with kind agent, tool or sub_workflow; optional max_workers debate Solver agents argue for several rounds and a moderator decides solver_agent_ids (at least 2), moderator_agent_id, optional rounds (1 to 20) interactive-orchestrator Multi-turn orchestration with one manager manager_agent_id; optional knowledge_base_id, structured_output_schema composite A graph definition See Composite workflow graphs two-agent Legacy; only used by the two-agent SSE endpoint none

A workflow with no type is treated as sequential.

Read-only legacy rows

Old history rows of types intake_generation, backlog_refine, backlog_enhance and backlog_split can still be listed. They show executable: false and legacy_history: true, and new ones can no longer be created.

docs.title: Sequential step input
docs.text:
By default a sequential step only sees the previous step's output. To also give every step the original assignment, set:

{
  "agent_ids": ["...", "..."],
  "step_input_mode": "assignment_plus_previous",
  "handoff_instructions": "Keep the tone formal."
}

step_input_mode is previous_output (default) or assignment_plus_previous. handoff_instructions is text of at most 8000 characters that is appended to each step's input when step_input_mode is assignment_plus_previous (it is ignored otherwise).

docs.title: Require MCP servers
docs.text:
For sequential and composite workflows you can fail fast when a tool server is down:

{"agent_ids": ["..."], "required_mcp_servers": ["jira", "confluence"]}

When a listed server is not connected the node fails with MCP_UNAVAILABLE and the run fails.

docs.title: How routing and handoff decide
docs.text:
Routing decides in this order: (1) the router agent (router_agent_id) replies with JSON {"route": "<key>"}, a key of route_map, or {"agent_id": "<uuid>"} (a tool call also works when routing_tool_names is set); (2) otherwise routes entries {contains, agent_id} are matched case-insensitively against the message; (3) otherwise default_agent_id handles it. Without a router_agent_id there is no model-based routing.

Handoff first picks the workers whose matches keywords appear in the message (case-insensitive), then fills up to max_workers (default 2) with the remaining workers in configuration order. Every selected worker runs. kind defaults to agent; kind: tool supports only the built-in test tools echo, uppercase and fail.

docs.title: Examples
Manage workflows
docs.text: Action Request List GET .../workflows Get GET .../workflows/{workflow_id} Update PUT .../workflows/{workflow_id}; a new version is stored Delete DELETE .../workflows/{workflow_id} List versions GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/versions Read a version GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/versions/{version_number} Mark a version active POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/versions/{version_number}/activate (changes the active flag only, not the config that runs; to roll back, read the version and PUT its config) Usage per workflow GET .../workflows/usage

docs.title: Run a workflow
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Write a short note about our new refund policy"}'

{
  "session_id": "5c9ef9bb-4dd5-4c14-b2ac-0f93f4b5f4d1",
  "output": "...",
  "structured_output": null,
  "audit": [{"agent": "writer", "...": "..."}],
  "error": null,
  "status": "completed",
  "pending_input": null
}

The response has the final output and an audit trail of the steps. Streaming and asynchronous runs are covered in Running and streaming.

Useful request options (all optional except message):

Field Purpose session_id Continue a session, or resume a run paused at a checkpoint inputs Values for the inputs a composite workflow declares structured_output_schema JSON Schema; the final result is validated and returned as structured_output knowledge_base_id_override Use another knowledge base for this run mcp_enabled, mcp_tool_allowlist Turn MCP tools off or restrict them for this run only instructions_overlay Extra per-turn context for interactive orchestrators

docs.title: Convert a legacy workflow to a graph
docs.text: POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/convert-to-composite returns {type, config, acknowledged_losses} for the equivalent composite graph without saving it. Types with no conversion return 400. If the conversion would drop settings or merge a repeated agent it fails with CONVERSION_LOSSES and lists them; call it again with {"acknowledge_losses": true} once you accept them. Validate the result and save it with PUT using "type": "composite" and the returned config. See Composite workflow graphs.

docs.title: Choosing a type
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Q{What do you need?}
    Q -->|A fixed pipeline| S[sequential]
    Q -->|Independent opinions at once| P[parallel]
    Q -->|Pick the right specialist| R[routing or handoff]
    Q -->|Stages with fan-out and fan-in| ST[staged]
    Q -->|A manager and workers| O[orchestrator]
    Q -->|Challenge and decide| D[debate]
    Q -->|Conditions, loops, human approval, files| C[composite]

docs.title: MCP
docs.text:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI applications use tools. Archy exposes its capabilities through an MCP server, so an AI client can create agents, search knowledge bases, run workflows and read results in natural language or in code.

Two directions

  • This section: AI clients and agents call Archy through its MCP server.
  • External MCP servers and skills: Archy agents call other MCP servers as tools.
flowchart LR
    subgraph Clients
        C1[Claude]
        C2[VS Code Copilot]
        C3[Cursor, Windsurf, Cline]
        C4[ChatGPT]
        C5[Your agent with the MCP SDK]
    end
    C1 & C2 & C3 & C4 & C5 -->|MCP| S[Archy MCP server]
    S -->|REST, caller token| API[Archy API]

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Dozens of tools across agents, knowledge bases, RAG search and upload, workflows (including authoring and validation), sessions, artifacts, usage, plans, dialogs, research, Confluence, GitHub and more. See the Tool catalog, which is generated from the server.
  • Prompts that guide a client through designing, converting and repairing a workflow.
  • Resources with the workflow node types, definition schema, validation codes and authoring guide, so an agent can read the contracts before it writes a graph.

docs.title: Transports
docs.text:
Transport Start Use when stdio (default) python -m src.mcp_server An IDE or desktop app launches the server as a local process streamable-http MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http python -m src.mcp_server A hosted server that many clients reach over HTTPS at /mcp sse MCP_TRANSPORT=sse ... Older clients that only speak SSE

The hosted server is at https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp. A local compose stack serves http://localhost:8001/mcp. GET /health and the protected resource metadata (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/...) are public; everything else needs credentials.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Credential Where Notes OAuth 2.0 with PKCE Hosted server, clients that support it (Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf) The client discovers the authorization server, registers itself and asks the user to sign in. No token to copy. archy_mcp_ API key Any client Create with POST .../mcp-tokens. Bound to one project. Works only on a reviewed list of tool routes (see the note below). User JWT Hosted HTTP or stdio A project-scoped REST API token (it must carry org_id and project_id). Works with every tool.

Every HTTP request must carry Authorization: Bearer <credential>. A request without it receives 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header that points to the protected resource metadata, which is how OAuth clients start the flow:

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer scope="mcp:tools", resource_metadata="https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"

API keys and OAuth tokens cover a subset of tools

OAuth access tokens are archy_mcp_ keys, and the API accepts such a key only on a reviewed list of routes: agents, knowledge bases and RAG, workflows, sessions, artifacts, connections, MCP servers and skills. Tools for usage, plans, dialogs, research, Confluence and listing organizations and projects call other routes, so they answer [INVALID_REQUEST] Invalid token with a key or an OAuth token and need a user JWT.

The org and project of each call always come from the credential, per request. Two clients with different credentials can never reach each other's data.

Details and per-client setup: Connect a client.

docs.title: Read-only access
docs.text: A credential with scope mcp:read can call only read tools. Anything that writes (create, update, delete, execute) is refused with a clear error. API keys created with the REST API get mcp:tools (read and write). An OAuth client can request mcp:read if it included that scope in the scope it sent to POST /oauth/register; otherwise it gets mcp:tools.

docs.title: Example: a conversation with tools
docs.text:
You: Which knowledge bases do we have, and does any of them mention refunds?

Client calls kb_list, then rag_search with knowledge_base_id and query: "refund policy".

Client answers from the returned chunks and cites the source file names.

You: Create an agent called "refund-helper" that answers from the handbook knowledge base.

Client calls agent_create with name, system_prompt and knowledge_base_ids, then agent_query to test it.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Tool errors carry a code and the API's message:

API status MCP error code 400, 404, 409, 422 INVALID_PARAMS 401, 403 INVALID_REQUEST 429, 5xx and any other status INTERNAL_ERROR Refused locally for a read-only credential FORBIDDEN

Some tools also return NOT_FOUND or INVALID_PARAMS before they call the API. The text is [CODE] message. Coded API errors keep their JSON shape inside the message, for example CONVERSION_LOSSES when converting a workflow.

docs.title: Server configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning ARCHY_API_URL http://localhost:8000 The Archy API the server calls ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN empty Credential used by the stdio transport. HTTP transports never use it. MCP_TRANSPORT stdio stdio, streamable-http or sse MCP_HTTP_HOST, MCP_HTTP_PORT 0.0.0.0, 8001 HTTP bind address MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS all Comma separated tool module names to expose. Valid names: agents, artifacts, auth_tools, confluence, confluence_write, connections, dialog, github, health, kb, mcp_registry, plans, rag, research, sessions, skills, usage, workflow_authoring, workflows. Unknown names are ignored. Include workflow_authoring for the workflow prompts and resources and auth_tools for auth_whoami. MCP_CORS_ORIGINS none Allowed browser origins (a bare * is ignored) MCP_KEY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 60 How long a validated API key is reused (0 to 60). Bounds how long a revoked key keeps working. INTERNAL_VALIDATE_SECRET empty Shared secret with the API for validating API keys. Required in production: set it to the same value on the API and on the MCP server, or every API key and OAuth token is refused. ARCHY_API_PUBLIC_URL ARCHY_API_URL Public origin of the API advertised in OAuth discovery. Set it to the same value as the API's OAUTH_ISSUER_URL. MCP_PUBLIC_URL built from the request headers Public origin of the MCP server advertised in OAuth discovery MCP_LOG_LEVEL INFO Log level

Reduce risk by exposing only the modules a client needs with MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS.

docs.title: Connect a client
docs.text:
Pick the setup that matches your client. The hosted HTTP server is the easiest: no checkout, and OAuth clients sign in without copying a token.

Option Needs Best for Hosted server with OAuth A client that supports remote MCP with OAuth Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf Hosted server with an API key An archy_mcp_ key Clients without OAuth, scripts, CI Local stdio server The repository and Python 3.11+ Offline development, custom builds

Client configuration formats change

The snippets below show the shape each client expects at the time of writing. Check your client's documentation if a key name differs.

docs.title: Prerequisite: an LLM credential
docs.text: Tools that run agents need the organization to have a verified LLM credential and an attached model. Without one, agent calls return a clear credential_error; see LLM providers and models. Tools that only read or store data (listing, searching, uploading) do not need one.

docs.title: Hosted server with OAuth
docs.text:
Point the client at the MCP URL:
