https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp

The client then performs this standard flow on its own:

  1. It calls the server without a token and receives 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header that names resource_metadata.
  2. It reads /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, which names the Archy API as the authorization server.
  3. It reads /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on the API and registers itself with POST /oauth/register (dynamic client registration, RFC 7591).
  4. It sends you to /oauth/authorize with PKCE (S256). You sign in and approve the requested scope (mcp:tools, or mcp:read when the client registered with it).
  5. It exchanges the code at /oauth/token and calls the server with the access token.

The hosted API allows Claude (claude.ai, claude.com), ChatGPT (chatgpt.com, chat.openai.com, platform.openai.com), vscode.dev, insiders.vscode.dev and the schemes cursor, vscode, vscode-insiders and windsurf; loopback redirects are always allowed. A self-hosted API allows only loopback until the operator sets OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI_ALLOWLIST (origins) and OAUTH_REDIRECT_SCHEME_ALLOWLIST (schemes), both JSON lists, and OAUTH_ISSUER_URL.

VS CodeClaude CodeClaude and ChatGPTCursor

.vscode/mcp.json:

{
  "servers": {
    "archy": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}

Open the Command Palette, run MCP: List Servers, start archy and follow the sign-in prompt.

claude mcp add --transport http archy https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp

Then run /mcp inside Claude Code to authenticate.

Add a custom connector (remote MCP server) in the product's settings and enter the URL. Both complete the OAuth flow in the browser.

~/.cursor/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "archy": { "url": "https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp" }
  }
}

docs.title: Hosted server with an API key
docs.text:
Create a key in a project (it is shown once):

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "my-ide", "expires_in_days": 90}'

Send it as a bearer token on every request:

VS CodeCursorMCP SDK 
{
  "servers": {
    "archy": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:archy_key}" }
    }
  },
  "inputs": [
    { "id": "archy_key", "type": "promptString", "description": "Archy MCP key (archy_mcp_...)", "password": true }
  ]
}

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "archy": {
      "url": "https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer archy_mcp_..." }
    }
  }
}

Use the official SDK; see Build with the MCP SDK.

How the hosted server treats a key:

  • The server validates it against the API and binds the request to the org, project and scope stored with the key. Nothing in the request can change them.
  • Validations are cached for at most MCP_KEY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default and maximum 60 seconds), for the MCP server's own check. The API checks the key again on every forwarded call, so tool calls with a revoked key fail at once.
  • The API accepts a key only on a reviewed list of routes used by the agent, knowledge base, RAG, workflow, session, artifact, connection, MCP server and skill tools. Any other route returns 401 Invalid token, so the usage, plans, dialogs, research, Confluence and organization or project listing tools do not work with a key (use a user JWT).
  • A deactivated creator invalidates the key.

docs.title: API key scopes
docs.text:
Scope Allows mcp:tools Read and write tools. Default for keys created with POST .../mcp-tokens. mcp:read Read-only tools. An OAuth client gets it when it registered with that scope. mcp:admin Reserved. Treated as write-capable, but neither the API nor OAuth issues it.

A scope that is empty or unknown is treated as read-only. Through MCP tools a write attempt with a read scope fails with [FORBIDDEN] Token scope mcp:read does not allow this operation; the REST API returns 403 Token scope does not allow this operation for the same key.

docs.title: Local stdio server
docs.text:
The client starts the server as a child process. You need the repository and a token.

git clone <your archy-agents-scope repository url>
cd archy-agents-scope
poetry install
poetry run which python        # note this path

Every client uses the same four settings:

Setting Value Command the repository's .venv/bin/python (absolute path) Args ["-m", "src.mcp_server"] Working directory the repository root (required, otherwise No module named 'src') Environment ARCHY_API_URL (your API) and ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN (an archy_mcp_ key or a JWT) VS CodeClaude DesktopCursor, Windsurf, Cline 
{
  "servers": {
    "archy": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/path/to/archy-agents-scope/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "src.mcp_server"],
      "cwd": "/path/to/archy-agents-scope",
      "env": {
        "ARCHY_API_URL": "http://localhost:8000",
        "ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN": "${input:archy_key}"
      }
    }
  },
  "inputs": [
    { "id": "archy_key", "type": "promptString", "description": "Archy MCP key", "password": true }
  ]
}

~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json on macOS, %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json on Windows:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "archy": {
      "command": "/path/to/archy-agents-scope/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "src.mcp_server"],
      "cwd": "/path/to/archy-agents-scope",
      "env": { "ARCHY_API_URL": "http://localhost:8000", "ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN": "archy_mcp_..." }
    }

}

Use the same JSON as Claude Desktop in ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or .cursor/mcp.json), ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json, or Cline's cline_mcp_settings.json.

In stdio mode the key is validated once at startup. Reload the server entry after any config change.

docs.title: Verify the connection
docs.text:
Ask the client to run these tools in order:

  1. auth_whoami: shows the organization, project and subject the server resolved from the credential (it makes no API call).
  2. kb_list: lists knowledge bases, which confirms that the API accepts the credential.
  3. rag_search: searches one.

Or check a key directly:

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/internal/mcp-tokens/validate" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"token": "archy_mcp_..."}'

Outside local development this internal endpoint requires the X-Internal-Secret header, so prefer the tools above.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No module named 'src' cwd not set or wrong interpreter Set cwd to the repository root and use its .venv/bin/python httpx.ConnectError The API is not running or ARCHY_API_URL is wrong Start the API and fix the URL Hosted: 401 Invalid or expired MCP API key. stdio: startup fails with MCP API key validation failed (HTTP 401) The key is unknown, expired, revoked or belongs to another environment Create a new key against the API you connect to [INVALID_REQUEST] Invalid token from a tool The tool's route is not on the API key route list Use a user JWT for that tool 401 Missing Authorization header An HTTP request had no bearer token Send Authorization: Bearer ... on every request 401 Token validation service unavailable The hosted server cannot reach the API, or the API returned a 5xx while validating an API key Check ARCHY_API_URL and API health [FORBIDDEN] Token scope mcp:read does not allow this operation (REST: 403 Token scope does not allow this operation) A read-only credential used a write tool Use a mcp:tools credential Tools missing after a change The client did not reload Restart the server entry or the client credential_error from an agent tool The organization has no verified LLM credential Connect a provider Browser clients blocked by CORS CORS is off by default The operator sets MCP_CORS_ORIGINS

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Treat archy_mcp_ keys like passwords: use secure prompts, never commit them, revoke keys you no longer use (POST .../mcp-tokens/{token_id}/revoke).
  • Prefer OAuth for people and short-lived keys for automation.
  • Expose only the tool modules a client needs with MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS on your own deployment.

docs.title: Build with the MCP SDK
docs.text:
Use the official MCP SDKs when you want your own application or agent to call Archy tools directly, without an AI client in between.

PythonTypeScriptstdio (Python) 
pip install mcp

import asyncio
import json
import os

from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client

URL = os.environ.get("ARCHY_MCP_URL", "https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp")
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ARCHY_MCP_KEY']}"}


def unwrap(result):
    """Return parsed JSON when the tool returned JSON text, otherwise the text."""
    if result.isError:
        raise RuntimeError(result.content[0].text)
    text = result.content[0].text
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return text


async def main() -> None:
    async with streamablehttp_client(URL, headers=HEADERS) as (read, write, _):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()

            print([t.name for t in (await session.list_tools()).tools][:5])

            who = unwrap(await session.call_tool("auth_whoami", {}))
            print(who)

            kbs = unwrap(await session.call_tool("kb_list", {}))
            print(kbs)


asyncio.run(main())

npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk

import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js";
import { StreamableHTTPClientTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/streamableHttp.js";

const url = new URL(process.env.ARCHY_MCP_URL ?? "https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp");
const transport = new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(url, {
  requestInit: { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ARCHY_MCP_KEY}` } },
});

const client = new Client({ name: "my-app", version: "1.0.0" });
await client.connect(transport);

const { tools } = await client.listTools();
console.log(tools.slice(0, 5).map((t) => t.name));

const result = await client.callTool({ name: "auth_whoami", arguments: {} });
console.log(result.content);
await client.close();

from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

params = StdioServerParameters(
    command="/path/to/archy-agents-scope/.venv/bin/python",
    args=["-m", "src.mcp_server"],
    cwd="/path/to/archy-agents-scope",
    env={"ARCHY_API_URL": "http://localhost:8000", "ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN": "archy_mcp_..."},
)

async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
    async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
        await session.initialize()
        print(await session.list_tools())

docs.title: Call tools
docs.text:
Arguments are plain JSON matching the tool's input schema from the Tool catalog (or from list_tools). All ids are UUID strings.

# Search a knowledge base
hits = unwrap(await session.call_tool("rag_search", {
    "knowledge_base_id": kb_id,
    "query": "How long is the refund window?",
    "top_k": 5,
}))

# Create an agent grounded in a knowledge base
agent = unwrap(await session.call_tool("agent_create", {
    "name": "refund-helper",
    "system_prompt": "Answer from the knowledge base.",
    "knowledge_base_ids": [kb_id],
}))

# Ask it
answer = unwrap(await session.call_tool("agent_query", {
    "agent_id": agent["id"],
    "message": "What is the refund window?",
}))

Same data, different door

Every tool maps to a REST endpoint and returns the same data. Use MCP when your caller already speaks MCP (an agent framework, an IDE). Use REST for everything else.

docs.title: Read the contracts
docs.text:
Resources let an agent load the exact shapes before it writes a workflow:

guide = await session.read_resource("archy://workflows/authoring-guide")
schema = await session.read_resource("archy://workflows/definition-schema")
node_types = await session.read_resource("archy://workflows/node-types")
codes = await session.read_resource("archy://workflows/validation-codes")
print(guide.contents[0].text)

The prompts design_workflow, convert_legacy_workflow and repair_workflow_validation return step-by-step instructions you can hand to a model:

prompt = await session.get_prompt("design_workflow", {})

docs.title: An agent that designs and validates a workflow
docs.text:
The loop below is what an AI client does for you. Use it as a blueprint for your own automation.

flowchart TD
    A[Read authoring guide and node types] --> B[Draft the graph]
    B --> C[workflow_validate]
    C -->|errors| D[Read workflow_validation_codes_get for each code]
    D --> B
    C -->|valid| E[workflow_create or workflow_update]
    E --> F[workflow_execute test run]
    F --> G[workflow_execution_trace]
async def design(session, name: str, agent_ids: list[str], graph: dict) -> str:
    created = unwrap(await session.call_tool("workflow_create", {
        "name": name,
        "workflow_type": "composite",
        "agent_ids": agent_ids,
        "config": {"version": 2, "graph": {"nodes": [], "edges": []}},
    }))
    workflow_id = created["id"]
    for _ in range(5):
        report = unwrap(await session.call_tool("workflow_validate", {"workflow_id": workflow_id, "graph": graph}))
        if report["valid"]:
            break
        graph = revise(graph, report["errors"])  # your code or an LLM call
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("could not produce a valid graph")
    await session.call_tool("workflow_graph_set", {"workflow_id": workflow_id, "graph": graph})
    return workflow_id

docs.title: Handle errors
docs.text: A failed tool call sets result.isError and puts [CODE] message in the text (see errors). Treat INVALID_PARAMS as a bug in your arguments, INVALID_REQUEST as an authentication or permission problem, and INTERNAL_ERROR as retryable with backoff.

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• One ClientSession per connection. Reuse it for many calls.
  • The org and project come from the credential. To work in another project use another credential (or auth_switch_tenancy with a user JWT).
  • For a long-running job prefer REST async runs, or poll with workflow_execution_get.

docs.title: MCP tool catalog
docs.text:
The Archy Platform MCP server exposes 93 tools, 3 prompts and 4 resources. This page is generated from the server itself.

Every tool runs inside the organization and project of the credential the client connected with. Tools that change data are not available to a read-only (mcp:read) credential; see Connect a client. Argument names and types below are exactly what the server accepts; all ids are UUID strings. A deployment can expose fewer tools with MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS.

Domain Tools Agents 8 Artifacts 7 Authentication and tenancy 4 Confluence 4 Storage connections 3 Multi-agent dialogs 3 GitHub 5 Health 1 Knowledge bases 5 External MCP server registry 7 Plans 5 RAG documents and search 6 Deep research 2 Sessions 3 Skills 2 Token usage 4 Workflows 24

docs.title: artifact_export_node_output

Limit: the run keeps only the first 500 characters of each node output, so a node whose output is 500 characters or longer cannot be exported after the run (node_output_not_found). Use artifact_export_run_output for the run result, or add a Save file node to the workflow to store long node output while it runs.

docs.title: workflow_convert_to_composite
docs.text:
Convert a legacy-typed workflow to an equivalent composite graph.

One-way transform: does not persist any change. The converted graph is validated server-side before being returned. Review it, check it with workflow_validate, then save it with workflow_update (workflow_type composite, config = the returned config). See workflow_authoring_guide_get.

The conversion keeps only what the graph can express. If it would drop config settings or merge a repeated agent, it fails with CONVERSION_LOSSES and lists each loss; set acknowledge_losses to convert anyway after you have decided the losses are acceptable.

Argument Type Required Description workflow_id string yes UUID of the legacy-typed workflow to convert. acknowledge_losses boolean no Convert even though settings are dropped or agents are merged.

Returns: {"type": "composite", "config": {"version": 1, "graph": {...}}, "acknowledged_losses": [...]}. The save endpoint upgrades this definition to the current version.

docs.title: workflow_create
docs.text:
Create a workflow.

Prefer composite: a graph of nodes and connections. Its config is {"version": 2, "graph": {"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}, "inputs": [...], "variables": {...}}; agent_ids may be empty. Read workflow_authoring_guide_get and workflow_definition_schema_get first. The legacy types (sequential, parallel, routing, debate, concurrent, handoff, group chat and similar) take a type specific config and are kept for existing workflows; workflow_convert_to_composite migrates them.

The requested type is now applied; an unsupported type or a legacy config that is missing its required keys is rejected with 4xx instead of silently creating a sequential workflow.

Argument Type Required Description name string yes Workflow display name. workflow_type string yes composite or a legacy type. agent_ids array of string yes Ordered list of agent UUIDs (legacy types; empty for composite). Sent as config.agent_ids unless the config already has that key. config object no Optional configuration. Unknown keys are kept.

Returns: Created workflow object with ID.

docs.title: workflow_definition_schema_get
docs.text:

Sent as config.agent_ids: merged into config when given, otherwise into the saved config. config object no New configuration (optional). Unknown keys are kept. workflow_type string no New type (optional), for example composite after a conversion.

Returns: Updated workflow object.

docs.title: workflow_validate

Argument Type Required Description workflow_id string yes UUID of the workflow to validate. graph object no Optional unsaved graph ({"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}) to validate instead of the saved workflow's config. inputs any no Optional unsaved inputs declaration to validate instead of the saved one.

Returns: ValidationResult object: {"valid": bool, "errors": [...], "warnings": [...]}.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The reference lists every public endpoint of the Archy Agents API: parameters, request body fields, curl and Python examples, and response shapes. It is generated from the OpenAPI specification, which is generated from the code, so it matches the running service.

  • Conventions: authentication, tenant paths, errors, streaming, versioning
  • Endpoint index: every operation by group
  • Schemas: every request and response model
  • openapi.json: the machine-readable specification

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Group Covers Authentication and tenancy Register, login, password reset, tenant switching, OAuth server Provisioning Organizations, projects, users, admin invites and credential push with a service token LLM providers and models Credentials, presets, model attachments, platform and embedding defaults Knowledge bases and RAG Knowledge bases, documents, sources, indexing, retrieval Agents Agent CRUD, query and streaming, state, memory, plans, skills, voice Workflows Workflows, validation, versions, execution, runs, checkpoints, dialog runs Sessions and artifacts History, activity, files and exports MCP servers and tokens External server registry, templates, health, API keys, tool invocations Connections and integrations Storage connections and personal Atlassian connections Token usage Consumption metrics Intake and campaigns Document intake, PRD and backlog generation, research tasks Governance and self-improvement Handoff requests, checkpoints, scoped credentials, policies, audit Health Liveness and readiness

docs.title: The OpenAPI specification
docs.text:
The specification is published at openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1). A running API also serves its live copy at /openapi.json and an interactive explorer at /docs.

Use it to:

Generate a Python clientGenerate TypeScript typesExplore interactivelyValidate your integration 
pip install openapi-python-client
openapi-python-client generate --path openapi.json

npx openapi-typescript openapi.json -o archy.d.ts

Import openapi.json into Postman, Insomnia, Bruno or any OpenAPI viewer. Set the server to your API and add a bearer token.

npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.json

What the specification omits

Operator-only surfaces (platform administration, operations console, sandbox, promotions and environment transitions) are not part of the public specification.

docs.title: How to read an endpoint entry
docs.text:
Each entry has:

  • Method and path, with a stable anchor you can link to.
  • Summary and description, including the authentication and tenancy rule.
  • Parameters: path, query and header parameters with type and whether they are required.
  • Request body: a field table with type, required flag and constraints, plus a link to the schema.
  • Example: curl and Python. Placeholders such as $ORG_ID are shell variables or <org_id> values you replace. Request bodies are generated from the schema, so replace sample values with real ones.
  • Responses: status codes, body type and an example of the success response.

Streaming endpoints (SSE and NDJSON) use curl -N and httpx.stream in their examples. Their event formats are described in Running and streaming.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Rules that apply to every endpoint.

docs.title: Base URL and versioning
docs.text:
Environment Base URL Hosted https://archy-agents.fly.dev Local http://localhost:8000

All routes are under /api/v1. Within v1, treat responses as forward compatible: ignore fields and stream events you do not know. New optional request fields, endpoints and event types can appear at any time. The OAuth discovery documents live at /.well-known/... and /oauth/...; health probes at /health.

The examples use two environment variables:

export ARCHY_API_URL=https://archy-agents.fly.dev
export ARCHY_TOKEN="<bearer token>"

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Send Authorization: Bearer <token> on every request except health probes and OAuth discovery. Token types and how to get them: Authentication and tokens.

docs.title: Tenant scoping
docs.text:
Resources belong to an organization and usually a project. Most routes carry both in the path:

/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/...
  • The ids in the path must equal the tenant of the token, otherwise the API returns 403 Forbidden.
  • Organization-scoped resources use /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/....
  • Some routes take the tenant from the token and accept org_id and project_id only as optional query parameters (for example /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query, /api/v1/llm-providers/...). A service token must supply them as query parameters on those routes.
  • Several older alias paths exist (for example /api/v1/agents/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/... and /api/v1/workflows/orgs/...). They behave like the canonical ones. Prefer the canonical /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/... form in new code.

docs.title: Data formats
docs.text: Topic Rule Content type application/json for bodies, multipart/form-data for file uploads Ids UUID strings (lowercase, hyphenated) Timestamps ISO 8601, UTC Unknown request fields Rejected for strictly validated objects (for example agent config); ignored elsewhere. Check the schema. Secrets Write-only. API keys, MCP headers and similar values are never returned.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors return JSON with a detail and, for server-generated errors, a request_id that matches the X-Request-ID response header.

Status Body shape 401, 403, 404, most 400 {"detail": "message", "request_id": "..."} 422 {"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input"}]} Coded conflicts and workflow errors {"detail": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} Invalid agent config (400) {"detail": {"message": "Invalid config", "errors": [...]}}

See Errors, limits and practices for handling and retries.

docs.title: Pagination and filtering
docs.text: Collections that can grow take limit and offset query parameters. Filters are explicit query parameters documented on each endpoint.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Endpoint kind Behavior Provisioning PUT Idempotent upserts keyed by the id in the path PUT on resources Replaces the provided fields; agent config is replaced as a whole POST that creates Not idempotent; a retry creates a second resource DELETE Check the endpoint. Only the provisioning credential delete is documented as idempotent (it returns deleted: false for an absent credential).

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Format Content-Type Used by Server-Sent Events text/event-stream .../chat/stream, .../execute/stream NDJSON application/x-ndjson Knowledge base retrieval preview, dialog runs, orchestrator runs

Streams report failures in-band after a 200 status. See Running and streaming.

docs.title: Rate limits and size limits
docs.text:
• Authentication endpoints are rate limited per IP and per account (429 with Retry-After).
  • Document uploads are limited to 50 MB per file; artifacts to 25 MB by default.
  • Operators can configure additional limits per deployment.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Direction Purpose Authorization request Bearer token Content-Type request application/json or multipart/form-data X-Request-ID both Correlation id. Send your own or read the generated one. Retry-After response Seconds to wait after 429 Cache-Control response private, max-age=300 on the workflow contract endpoints; no-cache on streams

docs.title: CORS
docs.text: Browser access is limited to the origins the operator configured (CORS_ORIGINS). Call the API from your backend unless you control the deployment, and never expose service tokens to a browser.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Every endpoint of the public Archy Agents API, generated from the OpenAPI specification. Pages share the conventions in Conventions: bearer authentication, tenant path parameters and error format.

Group Endpoints What it covers Authentication and tenancy 12 Register, log in, reset passwords, inspect or switch the active tenant and the OAuth server used by hosted MCP clients. Provisioning 7 Service-token endpoints that create organizations, projects and users and push LLM credentials. LLM providers and models 28 Bring-your-own provider credentials and the model attachments that decide which model an agent uses. Knowledge bases and RAG 30 Create knowledge bases, ingest documents, index and query them. Agents 49 Create agents, query them, stream answers, read memory and manage plans and skills. Workflows 47 Create, validate, version and run workflows; async runs, checkpoints and dialog runs. Sessions and artifacts 14 Conversation and run history, and files produced by runs. MCP servers and tokens 28 Register external MCP servers for agents and manage tokens for the Archy Platform MCP server. Connections and integrations 33 Storage connections and personal Atlassian connections. Token usage 9 Token consumption by organization, project, model and time. Intake and campaigns 33 Document intake, PRD and backlog generation, and campaign research. Governance and self-improvement 19 Change requests, checkpoints, scoped credentials, policy rules and the audit trail. Health 3 Liveness and readiness probes.

Total: 312 operations, 288 schemas. See also Schemas.

docs.title: Governance and self-improvement
docs.text:
Change requests, checkpoints, scoped credentials, policy rules and the audit trail.

This page documents 19 endpoint(s). Replace $ARCHY_API_URL and $ARCHY_TOKEN as described in Conventions.

Besides the responses listed for each endpoint, any endpoint can return 401 (missing or invalid token), 403 (wrong tenant, role or scope) and 404 (resource not found in your tenant). See Errors.

Method Path Summary POST /api/v1/checkpoints Write a state checkpoint GET /api/v1/checkpoints/{correlation_id} Get latest checkpoint and validate integrity GET /api/v1/checkpoints/{correlation_id}/history List all checkpoint versions POST /api/v1/credentials/issue Issue a time-bound, scope-limited credential POST /api/v1/credentials/validate Validate a credential token against a scope POST /api/v1/credentials/{credential_id}/revoke Revoke a credential immediately GET /api/v1/handoffs/requests List handoff requests POST /api/v1/handoffs/requests Create handoff request GET /api/v1/handoffs/requests/{correlation_id} Get handoff request by correlation ID GET /api/v1/policies/rules List policy rules for org POST /api/v1/policies/rules Create a policy rule PUT /api/v1/policies/rules/{rule_id} Update a policy rule (increments version) DELETE /api/v1/policies/rules/{rule_id} Soft-delete a policy rule (set active=False) POST /api/v1/policies/evaluate Evaluate a handoff payload against policy rules GET /api/v1/policies/approvals List pending approvals for org POST /api/v1/policies/approvals/{approval_id}/decide Approve or reject a pending approval GET /api/v1/audit/logs Query audit trail GET /api/v1/audit/verify Verify audit chain integrity POST /api/v1/restart/{correlation_id} Restart from checkpoint

Use case: import Confluence pages into a knowledge base without waiting. docs.title: PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/{user_id}
docs.text:
Provision user

Use case: upsert a User and grant them access to an org/project from an external provisioning system.

This endpoint also upserts a ProjectMembership so a single user can belong to many orgs/projects and switch explicitly via /api/v1/tenancy/switch.

Note: for existing users, this does NOT overwrite the user's active org_id/project_id fields; it only adds membership. The email of an existing user never changes and is_active is applied only when the user is created.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite
docs.text:

Use case: create (or look up) a human admin user by email, grant them access to one or more projects in the org, and return a single-use set-password link suitable for UI onboarding.

For an EXISTING user (matched by normalised email) no link is issued (invite_link and expires_at are null, existing_user is true), global user state is untouched and only memberships in this org are added.

docs.title: InviteOrgAdminRequest
docs.text:
Invite (or re-invite) a human org admin.

This is designed for service-to-service provisioning systems that want a user-friendly onboarding flow: the response includes a single-use link a human can open to set an initial password.

The invited user is granted ProjectMembership (role=admin by default) for the selected projects. A link is issued only for NEW users; an existing user (matched by normalised email) gets memberships only, and a differing user_id is ignored (the existing user is kept).

Field Type Required Description email string (email) yes user_id string (uuid) no project_ids array of string (uuid) no role enum: admin, permission-admin no Role for new memberships (admin when omitted). An existing membership changes only when a role is passed explicitly. is_active boolean no Applied only when the user is created; ignored for existing users. (default true)

Defaults are applied and values are coerced to the declared type; unknown names, missing required inputs and type mismatches give a 422 WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID. Templates read them as input.<name>. Values are recorded in the run trace (session history) unless the input is declared sensitive, which records ***. mcp_enabled boolean no Per-request MCP switch. Null keeps the agent configuration; false registers no MCP tools for this run. Not persisted. mcp_tool_allowlist array of string no Per-request MCP tool allowlist: only tools with these server-side names (without the server prefix, e.g. jira_get_issue) are registered for every agent in this run. Null keeps all tools. Not persisted.

Use case: one-way transform of a legacy-typed workflow's config into an equivalent composite config ({version, graph}).

docs.title: POST /api/v1/workflows/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/workflows/{workflow_id}/execute
docs.text:
Execute workflow

Use case: execute a workflow by id and return a final output plus an audit trail.

For streaming UX, prefer /execute/stream.

Passing the session_id of a run paused at a checkpoint resumes it (implicit resume): only declared sensitive inputs may be sent, the other inputs are restored from the paused run. Invalid inputs give 422 and the run stays resumable, also while another resume holds the claim.

422 has two shapes: {detail: {code: WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID, errors: [{name, code, message}]}} for invalid run inputs, and FastAPI's {detail: [{loc, msg, type}]} for a malformed body. INPUT_UNKNOWN also covers a declared but non-sensitive input sent on resume.

Auth: Bearer JWT; org_id and project_id must match token tenancy.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description org_id path string (uuid) yes Organization id. project_id path string (uuid) yes Project id. workflow_id path string (uuid) yes Workflow id.

Request body (application/json, required)

Field Type Required Description message string yes User input to execute the workflow with. (min length 1) session_id string (uuid) no Optional workflow session id. If omitted, a new session is created; if provided, the existing session is resumed. structured_output_schema object no Optional client-provided JSON Schema (limited subset) that is used to enforce structured output in a finalization step. The final structured payload is returned as structured_output when validation succeeds. structured_output_agent_id string (uuid) no Optional agent id to use as the structured-output finalizer. If omitted, the workflow may use config.structured_output_agent_id or a default agent. instructions_overlay string no Optional per-turn context injected before the user message. Used by interactive-orchestrator workflows to pass protocol, progress state, and template sections without persisting them in the workflow definition. knowledge_base_id_override string (uuid) no Optional knowledge base ID to use for RAG retrieval on this execution. Overrides the workflow config's knowledge_base_id if provided. inputs object no Optional workflow inputs: name -> value for the inputs the composite workflow declares. Defaults are applied and values are coerced to the declared type; unknown names, missing required inputs and type mismatches give a 422 WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID. Templates read them as input.<name>. Values are recorded in the run trace (session history) unless the input is declared sensitive, which records ***. mcp_enabled boolean no Per-request MCP switch. Null keeps the agent configuration; false registers no MCP tools for this run. Not persisted. mcp_tool_allowlist array of string no Per-request MCP tool allowlist: only tools with these server-side names (without the server prefix, e.g. jira_get_issue) are registered for every agent in this run. Null keeps all tools. Not persisted.

Schema: WorkflowExecuteRequest

Example

curlPython 
curl -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/workflows/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "message": "Summarize the onboarding policy"
}'

docs.title: POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/workflows/{workflow_id}/sessions/{session_id}/resume
docs.text:
Resume a workflow paused at a checkpoint

Use case: answer the question of a composite workflow run that stopped at a checkpoint node (status = awaiting_input). The run continues without re-running finished nodes; the answer is nodes.<checkpoint name>.output.

The response has the shape of /execute: completed, or awaiting_input again when another checkpoint is reached.

404: session unknown for this tenant/workflow. 409: the session is not waiting for input (for example an answer was already submitted). 422 WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID: inputs are not valid for the resume (same body as /execute, with errors[] of name, code, message: INPUT_UNKNOWN for an input that is not a declared sensitive one, INPUT_REQUIRED for a sensitive input that must be sent again, INPUT_TYPE_MISMATCH); the run keeps waiting and can be resumed again.

Auth: Bearer JWT; org_id and project_id must match token tenancy.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description org_id path string (uuid) yes Organization id. project_id path string (uuid) yes Project id. workflow_id path string (uuid) yes Workflow id. session_id path string (uuid) yes Session id.

Request body (application/json, required)

Field Type Required Description answer string yes The user's answer to the pending checkpoint (at most 32 KB). (min length 1, max length 32768) inputs object no Only inputs declared sensitive are accepted (they are not stored with the paused run and must be sent again); any other key returns 400. Other inputs are restored.

Execute a workflow and stream progress via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Orchestrator workflows emit: start, step_started / step_completed per agent, then end.

Other workflow types emit: start, optional token / discussion events, then end.

Legacy workflow types (sequential/parallel/routing/dialog/conversation/orchestrator/handoff/debate) additionally interleave the unified trace envelope (run.started/node.started/node.delta/node.completed/edge.active/run.completed), each carrying seq so clients can resume with ?after_seq=N.

This is always the complete, schema-validated object — never a partial/incremental JSON fragment. If the object fails schema validation, no structured_output event is emitted and run.completed carries data.structured_output_error instead.

The final structured payload is returned as structured_output when validation succeeds. structured_output_agent_id string (uuid) no Optional agent id to use as the structured-output finalizer. If omitted, the workflow may use config.structured_output_agent_id or a default agent. instructions_overlay string no Optional per-turn context injected before the user message. Used by interactive-orchestrator workflows to pass protocol, progress state, and template sections without persisting them in the workflow definition. knowledge_base_id_override string (uuid) no Optional knowledge base ID to use for RAG retrieval on this execution. Overrides the workflow config's knowledge_base_id if provided. inputs object no Optional workflow inputs: name -> value for the inputs the composite workflow declares. Defaults are applied and values are coerced to the declared type; unknown names, missing required inputs and type mismatches give a 422 WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID. Templates read them as input.<name>. Values are recorded in the run trace (session history) unless the input is declared sensitive, which records ***. mcp_enabled boolean no Per-request MCP switch. Null keeps the agent configuration; false registers no MCP tools for this run. Not persisted. mcp_tool_allowlist array of string no Per-request MCP tool allowlist: only tools with these server-side names (without the server prefix, e.g. jira_get_issue) are registered for every agent in this run. docs.text:
Execute org-scoped workflow

Execute an org-scoped workflow (project_id=NULL) on org-scoped agents and return the final output plus an audit trail. Org-scoped execution supports sequential/parallel workflow types.

Auth: Bearer JWT; org_id must match token tenancy.

Parameters

Name In Type Required Description org_id path string (uuid) yes Organization id. workflow_id path string (uuid) yes Workflow id. project_id query string (uuid) no Project id.

Request body (application/json, required)

Field Type Required Description message string yes User input to execute the workflow with. (min length 1) session_id string (uuid) no Optional workflow session id. If omitted, a new session is created; if provided, the existing session is resumed. structured_output_schema object no Optional client-provided JSON Schema (limited subset) that is used to enforce structured output in a finalization step. The final structured payload is returned as structured_output when validation succeeds. structured_output_agent_id string (uuid) no Optional agent id to use as the structured-output finalizer. If omitted, the workflow may use config.structured_output_agent_id or a default agent. instructions_overlay string no Optional per-turn context injected before the user message. Used by interactive-orchestrator workflows to pass protocol, progress state, and template sections without persisting them in the workflow definition. knowledge_base_id_override string (uuid) no Optional knowledge base ID to use for RAG retrieval on this execution. Overrides the workflow config's knowledge_base_id if provided. inputs object no Optional workflow inputs: name -> value for the inputs the composite workflow declares. Defaults are applied and values are coerced to the declared type; unknown names, missing required inputs and type mismatches give a 422 WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID. Templates read them as input.<name>. Values are recorded in the run trace (session history) unless the input is declared sensitive, which records ***. mcp_enabled boolean no Per-request MCP switch. Null keeps the agent configuration; false registers no MCP tools for this run. Not persisted. mcp_tool_allowlist array of string no Per-request MCP tool allowlist: only tools with these server-side names (without the server prefix, e.g. jira_get_issue) are registered for every agent in this run. Null keeps all tools. Not persisted.

Schema: WorkflowExecuteRequest

curl -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

docs.text:
Requires httpx (pip install httpx). The class has no other dependency.

"""archy_client.py: a small client for the Archy Agents API."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any

import httpx


class ArchyError(RuntimeError):
    def __init__(self, response: httpx.Response) -> None:
        try:
            detail = response.json().get("detail")
        except ValueError:
            detail = response.text
        super().__init__(f"{response.request.method} {response.request.url.path} -> {response.status_code}: {detail}")
        self.status_code = response.status_code
        self.detail = detail
        self.request_id = response.headers.get("x-request-id")


class ArchyClient:
    """Acts as one user in one organization and project."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, token: str | None = None, *, http: httpx.Client | None = None) -> None:
        self.http = http or httpx.Client(base_url=base_url, timeout=120)
        self.org_id: str | None = None
        self.project_id: str | None = None
        if token:
            self.http.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"

    # --- plumbing --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _send(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            raise ArchyError(response)
        return response.json() if response.content else None

    @property
    def scope(self) -> str:
        if not (self.org_id and self.project_id):
            raise RuntimeError("call login() or use_tenant() first")
        return f"/api/v1/orgs/{self.org_id}/projects/{self.project_id}"

    def use_tenant(self, org_id: str, project_id: str) -> None:
        self.org_id, self.project_id = org_id, project_id

    # --- authentication --------------------------------------------------------------------
    def login(self, email: str, password: str, *, remember_me: bool = False) -> dict:
        body = self._send("POST", "/api/v1/auth/login", json={"email": email, "password": password, "remember_me": remember_me})
        self.http.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {body['access_token']}"
        self.use_tenant(body["org_id"], body["project_id"])
        return body

    def switch_tenant(self, org_id: str, project_id: str) -> dict:
        body = self._send("POST", "/api/v1/tenancy/switch", json={"org_id": org_id, "project_id": project_id})
        self.http.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {body['access_token']}"
        self.use_tenant(org_id, project_id)
        return body

    def whoami(self) -> dict:
        return self._send("GET", "/api/v1/tenancy/whoami")

    # --- agents ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def create_agent(self, name: str, prompt: str, **config: Any) -> dict:
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/agents", json={"name": name, "config": {"sys_prompt": prompt, **config}})

    def list_agents(self) -> list[dict]:
        return self._send("GET", f"{self.scope}/agents")

    def ask(self, agent_id: str, message: str, session_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
        body = {"message": message, **({"session_id": session_id} if session_id else {})}
        return self._send("POST", f"/api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query", json=body)

    def stream_chat(self, agent_id: str, message: str, session_id: str | None = None) -> Iterator[tuple[str, dict]]:
        """Yield (event, data) for start, delta, end and error events."""
        body = {"message": message, **({"session_id": session_id} if session_id else {})}
        with self.http.stream("POST", f"{self.scope}/agents/{agent_id}/chat/stream", json=body, timeout=None) as response:
            if response.status_code >= 400:
                response.read()
                raise ArchyError(response)
            event, data = "message", []
            for line in response.iter_lines():
                if line == "":
                    if data:
                        yield event, json.loads("\n".join(data))
                    event, data = "message", []
                elif line.startswith("event:"):
                    event = line[6:].strip()
                elif line.startswith("data:"):
                    data.append(line[5:].lstrip())

    # --- knowledge bases -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def create_kb(self, name: str, description: str | None = None) -> dict:
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/knowledge-bases", json={"name": name, "description": description})

    def upload(self, kb_id: str, files: list[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> list[dict]:
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/documents/upload", files=[("files", f) for f in files])

    def wait_indexed(self, kb_id: str, timeout: float = 600) -> dict:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            stats = self._send("GET", f"{self.scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/stats")
            if stats["files_total"] > 0 and stats["indexing_total"] == 0:
                return stats
            time.sleep(2)
        raise TimeoutError("indexing did not finish")

    def search(self, kb_id: str, query: str, top_k: int = 5, strategy: str = "hybrid") -> list[dict]:
        body = {"query": query, "top_k": top_k, "retrieval_strategy": strategy}
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/query", json=body)["results"]

    # --- workflows -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def create_workflow(self, name: str, workflow_type: str, config: dict) -> dict:
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/workflows", json={"name": name, "type": workflow_type, "config": config})

    def validate(self, workflow_id: str, graph: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/validate", json={"graph": graph} if graph else {})

    def run(self, workflow_id: str, message: str, inputs: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 900) -> dict:
        """Start an async run and wait for a final or paused state."""
        started = self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs", json={"message": message, "inputs": inputs})
        delay, deadline = 1.0, time.monotonic() + timeout
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            run = self._send("GET", f"{self.scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs/{started['run_id']}")
            if run["status"] in ("succeeded", "failed", "awaiting_input"):
                return run
            time.sleep(delay)
            delay = min(delay * 1.5, 10)
        raise TimeoutError("run still in progress")

    def resume(self, workflow_id: str, session_id: str, answer: str, inputs: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        body = {"answer": answer, **({"inputs": inputs} if inputs else {})}
        return self._send("POST", f"{self.scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/sessions/{session_id}/resume", json=body)


class Provisioner:
    """Service-token client for creating tenants. Keep it on the server."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, service_token: str, *, http: httpx.Client | None = None) -> None:
        self.http = http or httpx.Client(base_url=base_url, timeout=30)
        self.http.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {service_token}"

    def _send(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            raise ArchyError(response)
        return response.json()

    def ensure_org(self, org_id: str, name: str, settings: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        return self._send("PUT", f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}", json={"name": name, "settings": settings})

    def ensure_project(self, org_id: str, project_id: str, name: str, description: str | None = None) -> dict:
        return self._send(
            "PUT",
            f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}",
            json={"name": name, "description": description},
        )

    def invite_admin(self, org_id: str, email: str, **options: Any) -> dict:
        return self._send("POST", f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite", json={"email": email, **options})

Usage:

from archy_client import ArchyClient

archy = ArchyClient("http://localhost:8000")
archy.login("admin@acme.example", "a-long-unique-passphrase")

kb = archy.create_kb("handbook")
archy.upload(kb["id"], [("handbook.md", b"Refunds are available within 30 days.")])
archy.wait_indexed(kb["id"])

agent = archy.create_agent("support", "Answer from the knowledge base.", knowledge_base_id=kb["id"])
print(archy.ask(agent["id"], "What is the refund window?")["output"])

for event, data in archy.stream_chat(agent["id"], "And for enterprise customers?"):
    if event == "delta":
        print(data["delta"], end="", flush=True)

Uses the global fetch of Node 18+ and browsers. Run it on a server: it holds a bearer token.

// archy.ts
export class ArchyError extends Error {
  constructor(public status: number, public detail: unknown, public requestId?: string) {
    super(`HTTP ${status}: ${typeof detail === "string" ? detail : JSON.stringify(detail)}`);
  }
}

export class Archy {
  private token?: string;
  orgId?: string;
  projectId?: string;

  constructor(private baseUrl: string, token?: string) {
    this.token = token;
  }

  private async send<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
    const response = await fetch(this.baseUrl + path, {
      method,
      headers: {
        ...(this.token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${this.token}` } : {}),
        ...(body === undefined ? {} : { "Content-Type": "application/json" }),
      },
      body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
    });
    if (!response.ok) {
      const payload = await response.json().catch(() => ({}));
      throw new ArchyError(response.status, payload.detail, response.headers.get("x-request-id") ?? undefined);
    }
    return (await response.json()) as T;
  }

  private get scope(): string {
    if (!this.orgId || !this.projectId) throw new Error("call login() first");
    return `/api/v1/orgs/${this.orgId}/projects/${this.projectId}`;
  }

  async login(email: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    const body = await this.send<{ access_token: string; org_id: string; project_id: string }>(
      "POST", "/api/v1/auth/login", { email, password });
    this.token = body.access_token;
    this.orgId = body.org_id;
    this.projectId = body.project_id;
  }

  createAgent(name: string, sysPrompt: string, config: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
    return this.send<{ id: string }>("POST", `${this.scope}/agents`, {
      name, config: { sys_prompt: sysPrompt, ...config } });
  }

  ask(agentId: string, message: string, sessionId?: string) {
    return this.send<{ output: string; session_id: string }>("POST", `/api/v1/agents/${agentId}/query`, {
      message, ...(sessionId ? { session_id: sessionId } : {}) });
  }

  async *streamChat(agentId: string, message: string, sessionId?: string) {
    const response = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}${this.scope}/agents/${agentId}/chat/stream`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${this.token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ message, ...(sessionId ? { session_id: sessionId } : {}) }),
    });
    if (!response.ok) throw new ArchyError(response.status, await response.text());
    const reader = response.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
    let buffer = "";
    for (;;) {
      const { value, done } = await reader.read();
      if (done) return;
      buffer += value;
      let cut: number;
      while ((cut = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
        const block = buffer.slice(0, cut);
        buffer = buffer.slice(cut + 2);
        let event = "message";
        const data: string[] = [];
        for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
          if (line.startsWith("event:")) event = line.slice(6).trim();
          else if (line.startsWith("data:")) data.push(line.slice(5).trimStart());
        }
        if (data.length) yield { event, data: JSON.parse(data.join("\n")) };
      }
    }
  }
}

const archy = new Archy("http://localhost:8000");
await archy.login("admin@acme.example", "a-long-unique-passphrase");
const agent = await archy.createAgent("support", "Be concise.");
for await (const { event, data } of archy.streamChat(agent.id, "Hello")) {
  if (event === "delta") process.stdout.write(data.delta);
}

docs.title: Shell helpers
docs.text:
# archy.sh: source this file
archy() {  # usage: archy METHOD PATH [json-body]
  local method="$1" path="$2" body="${3:-}"
  if [ -n "$body" ]; then
    curl -sS -X "$method" "$ARCHY_API_URL$path" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$body"
  else
    curl -sS -X "$method" "$ARCHY_API_URL$path" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
  fi
}
