# archy POST /api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query '{"message": "Hello"}' | jq -r .output

docs.title: For AI agents
docs.text: These docs are written to be read by people and by AI agents (coding assistants, autonomous agents, retrieval systems). This page explains how to consume them efficiently and lists the facts and traps an agent most needs.

docs.title: Machine-readable entry points
docs.text:
Resource URL (relative to the site root) Use llms.txt /llms.txt Index of the documentation in the llms.txt format llms-full.txt /llms-full.txt Full text of the guides, tutorials and MCP pages in one Markdown file. Load it as context. openapi.json /openapi.json OpenAPI 3.1 specification of every public endpoint and schema API reference pages /reference/<group>/ Per-endpoint parameters, examples and responses MCP resources archy://workflows/authoring-guide and three more Live workflow contracts served by the MCP server

A running API also serves its own live copy of the specification at /openapi.json.

Recommended reading order for an agent

  1. llms.txt to pick pages.
  2. This page for the rules and traps below.
  3. The guide that matches the task (provisioning, knowledge bases, agents, workflows).
  4. openapi.json (or the reference page) for exact request and response shapes.

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text:
1. Never print, log or store secrets. Bearer tokens, archy_mcp_ keys, provider API keys and invite_link values are secrets. Read them from the environment.
  2. Check your credential type before you call. User tokens for tenant routes, service tokens for /integrations/provisioning, archy_mcp_ keys only for the MCP server and its tool routes.
  3. Use ids, not names. Every resource has a UUID. Names are not unique keys.
  4. Prefer idempotent calls and verify the result with a read call after every write.
  5. Ask before destructive actions (DELETE, replacing an agent config, deleting a knowledge base or a credential).
  6. Treat model output as untrusted. Validate structured output before acting on it.
  7. Use async runs for long work and poll; do not hold a connection for minutes.

docs.title: Bootstrap a tenant (service token)
docs.text:
1. PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id} with {"name": ...}.
  2. PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}.
  3. POST /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite with {"email": ...}; take the token from invite_link.
  4. POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password with {"token", "new_password"}; then POST /api/v1/auth/login.
  5. Verify with GET /api/v1/tenancy/whoami.

docs.title: Connect a model (admin user token)
docs.text:
1. POST /api/v1/llm-providers/credentials with provider, display_name, api_key (and base_url where needed).
  2. POST /api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/{id}/verify; continue only if success is true.
  3. PUT /api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org with credential_id and model_name.
  4. PUT /api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default before creating knowledge bases.

docs.title: Knowledge base to answer
docs.text:
1. POST .../knowledge-bases, then POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents/upload (multipart files).
  2. Poll GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/stats until indexing_total is 0 and indexed_total equals files_total.
  3. POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/query to check retrieval.
  4. POST .../agents with config.knowledge_base_id; POST /api/v1/agents/{agent}/query.

docs.title: Workflow from a graph
docs.text:
1. Read GET /api/v1/workflow-authoring-guide and GET /api/v1/workflow-node-types.
  2. Create or reuse a workflow, then POST .../workflows/{id}/validate with the draft graph until valid is true.
  3. Save with PUT, validate the saved workflow, then run with POST .../workflows/{id}/runs and poll.

docs.title: Facts that are easy to get wrong
docs.text: Topic Fact Base path Everything is under /api/v1. Tenant routes are /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/... and the ids must match the token. Roles A self-registered user has role permission-admin and cannot create LLM credentials (403 Org admin role required). admin membership comes from provisioning or the invite flow. Verified credentials Only verified credentials run. Attaching an unverified credential returns 422. Model choice Org and project defaults come from model attachments, not from is_default. An agent config.model without credential_id runs on the platform model, not on the customer's key. Embeddings Set the organization embedding default before creating knowledge bases. Do not change the embedding model of a populated knowledge base. Agent update PUT replaces the whole config. Read, modify, write the complete object. Agent config Unknown keys are rejected with 400. Echo mode If no model resolves, an agent may reply Echo: <your message> with meta.mode = "echo". That is a configuration problem, not an answer. Workflow save Saving a composite workflow enforces node-name rules only. Call validate; do not rely on save to reject a bad graph. Expressions A template may read only nodes that run before it (TEMPLATE_NODE_NOT_UPSTREAM). A checkpoint's answer is nodes.<checkpoint name>.output. Sensitive inputs Masked in traces and must be resent when a paused run resumes. Streams Failures arrive in-band (event: error) after a 200. Use fetch/httpx.stream, not EventSource. Async runs POST .../runs returns 202 and a run_id; poll GET .../runs/{run_id} for succeeded, failed or awaiting_input. Service tokens They may call tenant routes for the org and project in the path, but have no org-admin rights. They cannot create credentials through /llm-providers or set model attachments. Provisioning PUT upserts with ids you choose. 409 bodies carry detail.code. Secrets API keys and MCP headers are write-only and are never returned.

docs.title: Using Archy through MCP
docs.text: If you are an agent with MCP support, connect to the Archy MCP server instead of calling REST: see Connect a client. Start with auth_whoami, read the archy://workflows/* resources before you author a workflow, and use workflow_validate before saving. The Tool catalog lists every tool and its arguments.

docs.title: Citing and linking
docs.text: Every endpoint has a stable anchor of the form #op-<method>-<path> on its reference page (for example reference/agents/#op-post-api-v1-agents-agent-id-query). Guides link to the reference sections they use. Prefer linking to these anchors when you report which call you made.

docs.title: Publishing this site
docs.text: This page is for the maintainers of the documentation. The site is a static MkDocs Material build that lives in the developer-docs/ folder of the archy-agents-scope repository.

docs.title: What is generated and what is written
docs.text:
Content Source Regenerate with Guides, tutorials, architecture, concepts Markdown in developer-docs/docs/ Edit the files openapi.json The FastAPI app poetry run python scripts/export_openapi.py MCP tool catalog The MCP server (tools, prompts, resources) The same command API reference pages and schemas developer-docs/openapi/openapi.json Built by hooks/gen_reference.py during mkdocs build llms.txt, llms-full.txt The hand-written pages Built by hooks/gen_llms.py

The two JSON snapshots in developer-docs/openapi/ are committed. A test (tests/test_developer_docs.py) fails when they are stale, so an endpoint or tool change cannot merge without refreshing them.

Public specification

scripts/export_openapi.py removes operator-only route groups (platform administration, operations console, sandbox, promotions, environment transitions) from the public document. Change EXCLUDED_TAGS in that script to adjust it.

docs.title: Build locally
docs.text:
cd developer-docs
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve                      # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict             # the CI build; writes developer-docs/site/

--strict turns warnings (broken links, missing anchors, unknown nav entries) into failures. Set DOCS_SITE_URL to the final public address before a production build so that llms.txt contains absolute links and the sitemap is correct:

DOCS_SITE_URL=https://docs.example.com mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Update after an API change
docs.text:
poetry run python scripts/export_openapi.py        # refresh both snapshots
poetry run pytest tests/test_developer_docs.py     # confirm they are current
cd developer-docs && mkdocs build --strict

Review the diff of developer-docs/openapi/openapi.json: it is the API change log. If you changed behavior that a guide describes, update the guide too.

docs.title: Hosting options
docs.text:
The output is plain static files, so any static host works.

Option Notes GitHub Pages from a public docs repository GitHub Pages is not available for private repositories on the GitHub Team plan, so publish the built site to a separate public repository. developer-docs/publish.sh automates this. GitHub Pages from this repository Possible only when the repository is public or the organization has a plan that supports Pages on private repositories. The workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml includes a Pages deployment job guarded by a repository variable. Cloudflare Pages Upload developer-docs/site/ with wrangler pages deploy developer-docs/site. Any object storage or CDN Sync developer-docs/site/ to a bucket with static website hosting.

docs.title: Publish to a public repository (GitHub Pages)
docs.text:
One-time setup:

  1. Create an empty public repository, for example archy-agents-docs.
  2. In its settings, enable Pages and choose the gh-pages branch, folder / (root).
  3. Optionally add a custom domain.

Publish from your machine:

DOCS_SITE_URL=https://<owner>.github.io/archy-agents-docs \
  developer-docs/publish.sh git@github.com:<owner>/archy-agents-docs.git

The script requires DOCS_SITE_URL, builds the site in strict mode, clones the gh-pages branch of the target (or starts it if it does not exist), replaces its contents with the new build, keeps an existing CNAME, adds .nojekyll, commits and pushes. It never rewrites history and stops if the target cannot be reached.

docs.title: Publish from CI
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the site on every pull request that touches the documentation. On pushes to main it can publish in two ways. Both are off until you configure them:

Repository setting Effect Variable DOCS_PUBLISH_REPO (for example owner/archy-agents-docs) and secret DOCS_PUBLISH_TOKEN (a token with write access to that repository) Push the build to the gh-pages branch of the public repository Variable DOCS_PAGES_ENABLED set to true Deploy with GitHub Pages from this repository

Set DOCS_SITE_URL as a repository variable as well.

docs.title: Content standards
docs.text:
• Write for two readers: a developer who skims and an agent that reads literally. Prefer short sections, tables and runnable examples.
  • Every example must be correct. Run it against a local stack or the in-process test app before you commit it.
  • Never include real tokens, keys, customer data or internal hostnames. Use placeholders.
  • Describe behavior the code guarantees. If you are unsure, read the code or test it, then document what you saw.
  • Keep terminology consistent: organization, project, agent, knowledge base, workflow, run, session, artifact.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Find your symptom, apply the fix. When you contact support, include the request_id from the error body (or the X-Request-ID response header), the endpoint, and the time.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix API not reachable on port 8000 Container still migrating, or crashed docker compose ps, then docker compose logs api 500 when you create an LLM credential LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set on the API Set a base64 32 byte key and restart (Run Archy locally) 401 on every provisioning call The service token was signed with another JWT_SECRET_KEY Mint the token with the API's secret Provider URL rejected SSRF protection blocks private, loopback or http:// addresses Use a public https:// URL; for local Ollama the operator sets SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS=true Invite link points to localhost PASSWORD_RESET_URL_BASE is the development default The operator sets it to your onboarding page

docs.title: Authentication and permissions
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 401 Missing bearer token No Authorization header Send Authorization: Bearer <token> 401 Invalid credentials Wrong email or password, or inactive user Reset the password or check the account 401 Token revoked The password was reset, or the user was deactivated Log in again 403 Forbidden on a tenant route org_id or project_id in the path differ from the token Use the ids from GET /tenancy/whoami or switch tenant 403 Org admin role required The user is not an admin Use an admin (Roles) 403 Service token required A user token was used on a provisioning route Use a service token 403 Missing scopes: ... The service token lacks the scope Mint a token with it 403 Not a member of this project Switching to a project without membership Provision the membership 429 Rate limited Wait Retry-After seconds

docs.title: LLM providers
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix verify returns success: false, "Authentication failed" Wrong key or base URL Update the credential, verify again 422 Credential must be verified before attaching a model The credential is not verified Verify it first Agent replies Echo: ... with meta.mode = "echo" No model resolved Attach a model or pin config.model with a credential_id credential_error No usable credential and platform fallback is off Add, verify and attach a credential The agent uses the platform model, not mine config.model has model_name but no credential_id Add the credential_id, or use an attachment Embeddings fail for new knowledge bases The embedding default is missing, deleted or unverified PUT /llm-providers/embedding-default Azure 404 DeploymentNotFound model_name is not a deployment name Use the Azure deployment name

docs.title: Knowledge bases
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Upload rejected with "Unsupported file type" Extension not supported Convert to PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), text, Markdown, JSON, HTML, PNG or JPEG "File too large (max 50MB)" A file exceeds 50 MB Split it indexed_total is below files_total and indexing_total is 0 Some documents failed GET .../documents; read status; re-run POST .../index after fixing the embedding credential Queries return nothing Documents are not indexed yet, or the question does not match Check stats; try retrieval_strategy: "vector" or more specific wording Scanned PDF returns little text No text layer Provide text based files Results are poor after changing the embedding model Vectors from different models are not comparable Create a new knowledge base and re-ingest

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 400 Invalid config Unknown key or wrong type in config Read detail.errors[].loc; see the config reference Config settings disappeared after an update PUT replaced the whole config Send the complete config 404 on a query with session_id Unknown or deleted session Omit session_id to start a new one Answers ignore the knowledge base knowledge_base_id missing, wrong project, or the KB has no indexed documents Check the config and stats Replies are cut off max_tokens too low Raise it Tool calls loop No max_iters or token_budget Set limits and refine the prompt

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 422 config.agent_ids is required A legacy type is missing required config See the table in Workflows validate returns START_UNREACHABLE_END No path from start to an end Connect the graph validate returns TEMPLATE_NODE_NOT_UPSTREAM A template reads a node that runs later Reorder or read an earlier node 400 Composite workflow must have a Start node on execute The graph has no start node. Saving did not reject it. Validate before you run 422 with WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID Missing or mistyped input Read detail.errors and fix inputs Run failed with MCP_UNAVAILABLE A required MCP server is down Check server health Run failed with SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED The agent output did not match outputSchema Loosen the schema or tighten the prompt Status stays awaiting_input A checkpoint waits for an answer POST .../sessions/{session_id}/resume or /cancel Resume returns an error about inputs A sensitive input was not resent, or a non-sensitive one was sent Send only the declared sensitive inputs save-file node fails with a format error csv needs tabular data Use markdown, json or text, or produce a list of objects

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Nothing arrives until the end A proxy buffers the response Disable buffering for text/event-stream and raise idle timeouts EventSource fails with 401 It cannot send headers Use fetch with a ReadableStream The stream ends with event: error after a 200 A runtime failure Read data.detail and handle it in your client A dropped workflow stream Network interruption A stream cannot reattach to a run in progress. Start long jobs as asynchronous runs and poll

docs.title: MCP
docs.text: See the table in Connect a client.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
1. Reproduce with curl and capture the full response (status, headers, body).
  2. Note the request_id.
  3. Check the API reference entry for the endpoint: required fields and roles are listed there.
  4. Contact your Archy operator with the endpoint, the request_id, the time and what you expected.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
End-to-end builds that combine several guides. Each tutorial is self-contained and tells you what to prepare.

Tutorial You build Uses Support assistant with RAG A grounded assistant, an evaluation script and a streaming backend endpoint Knowledge bases, agents, streaming Research and write pipeline A composite workflow with parallel research, a review gate and a saved file Composite workflows, structured output, artifacts, async runs Onboard customers from your backend An idempotent signup handler that creates a tenant, an admin, a model and starter agents Provisioning, LLM providers, agents Human approval checkpoint A workflow that pauses for a person and resumes Checkpoints, resume and cancel

All tutorials assume the Quickstart is done, so you have an organization, an admin token (ARCHY_TOKEN), a verified credential and an attached model.

docs.title: Human approval checkpoint
docs.text:
Some steps should not run until a person agrees: sending an email, publishing content, spending money. A checkpoint node pauses a composite workflow, shows a question, and continues when someone answers.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant App as Your app
    participant A as Archy API
    participant H as Approver
    App->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/execute {inputs}
    A-->>App: status awaiting_input, pending_input, session_id
    App->>H: show the draft and the question
    H-->>App: approve or request changes
    App->>A: POST .../sessions/{session_id}/resume {answer}
    A-->>App: status completed, output

Prepare: the Quickstart done and the archy.py helper from the support assistant tutorial.

docs.title: 1. Build the workflow
docs.text:
The workflow drafts a customer reply, pauses for approval, then finalizes the text using the approver's answer. It also declares a sensitive input: the customer's email address is masked in stored traces and must be sent again when the run resumes.

# approval_workflow.py
from archy import SCOPE, client


def make_agent(name: str, prompt: str) -> str:
    r = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/agents", json={"name": name, "config": {"sys_prompt": prompt}})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["id"]


drafter = make_agent("reply-drafter", "You draft short, polite replies to customer tickets.")
sender = make_agent("reply-finalizer", "You finalize a reply using the reviewer's instructions. Return only the final text.")

definition = {
    "version": 2,
    "inputs": [
        {"name": "ticket", "type": "string", "required": True},
        {"name": "customer_email", "type": "string", "required": True, "sensitive": True},
    ],
    "graph": {
        "nodes": [
            {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
            {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {
                "name": "draft", "agentId": drafter,
                "prompt": "Draft a reply to this ticket:\n{{input.ticket}}"}},
            {"id": "k", "type": "checkpoint", "data": {
                "name": "approval",
                "prompt": "Approve this draft, or tell me what to change:\n\n{{nodes.draft.output}}"}},
            {"id": "b", "type": "agent", "data": {
                "name": "final", "agentId": sender,
                "prompt": "Draft:\n{{nodes.draft.output}}\n\nReviewer says: {{nodes.approval.output}}\nCustomer address: {{input.customer_email}}\nWrite the final reply."}},
            {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}},
        ],
        "edges": [
            {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
            {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "k"},
            {"id": "e3", "source": "k", "target": "b"},
            {"id": "e4", "source": "b", "target": "e"},
        ],
    },
}

workflow = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/workflows", json={"name": "reply-with-approval", "type": "composite", "config": definition})
workflow.raise_for_status()
workflow_id = workflow.json()["id"]
report = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/workflows/{workflow_id}/validate", json={}).json()
print(workflow_id, "valid" if report["valid"] else report["errors"])

Points to notice:

  • The checkpoint prompt is a template. It may read earlier nodes (nodes.draft.output) but not a sensitive input: a checkpoint prompt that reads one raises the CHECKPOINT_PROMPT_SENSITIVE_INPUT warning because stored prompts show it masked.
  • A checkpoint must have an outgoing connection; otherwise validation warns DANGLING_CHECKPOINT.
  • The checkpoint node completes with the answer as its output, so later nodes read it as {{nodes.approval.output}} (the checkpoint's name is approval).

docs.title: 2. Start a run and detect the pause
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Handle this ticket", "inputs": {"ticket": "My invoice shows the wrong VAT number.", "customer_email": "ada@example.com"}}'

The response reports the pause:

{
  "session_id": "5c9ef9bb-4dd5-4c14-b2ac-0f93f4b5f4d1",
  "output": "Approve this draft, or tell me what to change:\n\nHello, thank you for ...",
  "status": "awaiting_input",
  "pending_input": {
    "status": "awaiting_input",
    "question": "Approve this draft, or tell me what to change:\n\nHello, thank you for ...",
    "node_id": "k",
    "node_name": "approval",
    "iteration": null
  },
  "audit": [],
  "error": null
}

Store the session_id. It identifies the paused run. iteration is set only when the checkpoint sits inside a loop.

Use an asynchronous run for the same flow when your caller cannot wait: GET .../runs/{run_id} then returns status: "awaiting_input" and the session_id.

docs.title: 3. Resume with the answer
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/sessions/$SESSION_ID/resume" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"answer": "Approved. Add an apology for the delay.", "inputs": {"customer_email": "ada@example.com"}}'
  • answer is required, 1 to 32,768 characters.
  • Send every sensitive input again in inputs: they are deliberately not stored with the paused run. Other inputs are restored automatically. Sending a non-sensitive input returns 422 (WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID).
  • Resuming a run that is not paused, was cancelled, or has expired returns an error and never runs twice.

To reject the draft entirely:

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/sessions/$SESSION_ID/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
# {"session_id": "...", "status": "cancelled"}

docs.title: 4. A small approval service
docs.text:
Put the pause behind your own UI. This backend keeps a list of pending approvals and resumes the run when a person decides.

# approvals.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

from archy import SCOPE, client

app = FastAPI()
pending: dict[str, dict] = {}  # approval id -> run info; use a database in production


class Ticket(BaseModel):
    ticket: str
    customer_email: str


@app.post("/tickets")
def start(t: Ticket, workflow_id: str):
    r = client.post(
        f"{SCOPE}/workflows/{workflow_id}/execute",
        json={"message": "Handle this ticket", "inputs": t.model_dump()},
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    run = r.json()
    if run["status"] == "awaiting_input":
        pending[run["session_id"]] = {"workflow_id": workflow_id, "email": t.customer_email, "draft": run["output"]}
        return {"state": "needs_approval", "approval_id": run["session_id"], "draft": run["output"]}
    return {"state": "done", "output": run["output"]}


class Decision(BaseModel):
    approve: bool
    comment: str = ""


@app.post("/approvals/{approval_id}")
def decide(approval_id: str, d: Decision):
    info = pending.pop(approval_id, None)
    if info is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown approval")
    base = f"{SCOPE}/workflows/{info['workflow_id']}/sessions/{approval_id}"
    if not d.approve and not d.comment:
        client.post(f"{base}/cancel").raise_for_status()
        return {"state": "cancelled"}
    r = client.post(
        f"{base}/resume",
        json={"answer": d.comment or "Approved.", "inputs": {"customer_email": info["email"]}},
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return {"state": "done", "output": r.json()["output"]}

docs.title: 5. Things to plan for
docs.text: Topic Guidance Expiry Paused runs expire (7 days by default). An expired checkpoint reports failed when resumed. Remind approvers or cancel stale ones. Who can resume Anyone with a token for the project can call resume. Enforce who may approve in your own application before you call it. Audit The session trace records the question and the answer. Use GET .../workflows/{id}/sessions/{session_id} to show the history. Loops A checkpoint inside a loop pauses on every iteration; pending_input.iteration says which one. Secrets Keep secrets out of checkpoint prompts. Use sensitive inputs and resend them on resume. Idempotency Two simultaneous resumes cannot both run: one holds a claim and the other receives an error. Retry only after reading the session status. Cost on resume Nodes that already finished are replayed from their saved results without calling the model again.

docs.title: What you learned
docs.text: You built a workflow that pauses for a person, detected the pause, resumed it with a decision and sensitive data, cancelled a run, and wrapped the flow in an approval service.

docs.title: Onboard customers from your backend
docs.text:
When a customer signs up for your product you want a ready workspace: an Archy organization and project, an admin who can sign in, a connected model and a few starter agents. This tutorial builds that as one idempotent function that you can call from a signup webhook or a job queue.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant W as Signup webhook
    participant B as Your backend
    participant A as Archy API
    participant M as Customer admin
    W->>B: customer signed up
    B->>B: derive ids from customer id
    B->>A: PUT org, PUT project (service token)
    B->>A: PUT llm-credentials (customer provider key)
    B->>A: POST agents (starter set, pinned model)
    B->>A: POST admins/invite
    A-->>B: invite_link
    B->>M: email the set-password link
    M->>A: reset-password, login

Prepare: a service token with scopes provision:org provision:project provision:user provision:credential. Locally, mint one as shown in Run Archy locally and add the scopes. Production tokens come from your operator, ideally bound to the organizations you manage (tenant binding).

Two ideas this tutorial relies on

  1. Ids are derived, not stored. Every Archy id is a UUID computed from your own customer id, so re-running onboarding always hits the same resources.
  2. A service token cannot create LLM credentials or model attachments through the user endpoints (they need an admin user). It pushes credentials through the provisioning endpoint and pins the model inside each agent's config.

docs.title: 1. The client
docs.text:
# onboarding.py
import os
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass

import httpx

NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("6f1c2f66-8f5b-4c60-9a32-0d8f0a1a2b3c")  # choose once, never change


def archy_id(kind: str, key: str) -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid5(NAMESPACE, f"{kind}:{key}"))


@dataclass
class Customer:
    id: str                    # your customer id
    name: str
    admin_email: str
    openai_api_key: str | None = None  # present when the customer brings their own key


class Archy:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.http = httpx.Client(
            base_url=os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"],
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SERVICE_TOKEN']}"},
            timeout=60,
        )

    def call(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict | list:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code == 409:
            raise RuntimeError(f"conflict: {response.json()['detail']}")
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()

docs.title: 2. Starter agents
docs.text:
Describe the agents you want every customer to have. Names are the idempotency key.

STARTER_AGENTS = [
    {
        "name": "support-assistant",
        "description": "Answers customer questions",
        "prompt": "You are a helpful support assistant for {company}. Be concise and say when you do not know.",
    },
    {
        "name": "summarizer",
        "description": "Summarizes long text",
        "prompt": "Summarize the text you receive in five bullet points for {company}.",
    },
]

docs.title: 3. Verify the customer's key yourself
docs.text:
Pushed credentials are only used at runtime when they are marked verified. Because there is no user in this flow, you verify the key with a cheap call to the provider before you mark it:

def key_works(api_key: str) -> bool:
    r = httpx.get("https://api.openai.com/v1/models", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"}, timeout=20)
    return r.status_code == 200

If you prefer, push the credential unverified and let the customer's admin call POST /llm-providers/credentials/{id}/verify after signing in.

docs.title: 4. The onboarding function
docs.text:
def onboard(archy: Archy, customer: Customer, model: str = "gpt-4o-mini") -> dict:
    org_id = archy_id("org", customer.id)
    project_id = archy_id("project", f"{customer.id}/default")
    credential_id = archy_id("credential", f"{customer.id}/openai")
    provisioning = "/api/v1/integrations/provisioning"
    scope = f"/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}"

    # 1. Tenant (idempotent upserts)
    archy.call("PUT", f"{provisioning}/orgs/{org_id}", json={"name": customer.name, "settings": {"customer_id": customer.id}})
    archy.call("PUT", f"{provisioning}/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}", json={"name": "Default"})

    # 2. Model credential, when the customer brought a key
    model_config: dict = {}
    if customer.openai_api_key:
        archy.call(
            "PUT",
            f"{provisioning}/orgs/{org_id}/llm-credentials",
            json={"credentials": [{
                "credential_id": credential_id,
                "provider": "openai",
                "display_name": "Customer OpenAI",
                "api_key": customer.openai_api_key,
                "is_default": True,
                "is_verified": key_works(customer.openai_api_key),
            }]},
        )
        model_config = {"model": {"provider": "openai", "model_name": model, "credential_id": credential_id}}

    # 3. Starter agents, skipping the ones that exist
    existing = {a["name"] for a in archy.call("GET", f"{scope}/agents")}
    created = []
    for spec in STARTER_AGENTS:
        if spec["name"] in existing:
            continue
        agent = archy.call("POST", f"{scope}/agents", json={
            "name": spec["name"],
            "description": spec["description"],
            "config": {"sys_prompt": spec["prompt"].format(company=customer.name), **model_config},
        })
        created.append(agent["id"])

    # 4. Admin who can sign in (a link only for a new user)
    invite = archy.call("POST", f"{provisioning}/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite", json={"email": customer.admin_email})

    return {"org_id": org_id, "project_id": project_id, "agents_created": created, "invite_link": invite["invite_link"]}

Run it twice and the second run creates nothing new: the tenant calls are upserts, the agents are skipped by name, and the invite for an existing admin returns existing_user: true with a null link.

The pinned model is per agent

Without an admin user the service token cannot set an organization-wide model attachment. Pinning config.model with a credential_id makes each starter agent use the customer's key. Once the customer's admin signs in they can attach an organization default and remove the pins (see Which model runs).

docs.title: 5. Wire it to a signup webhook
docs.text:
# main.py
from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

from onboarding import Archy, Customer, onboard

app = FastAPI()
archy = Archy()


class Signup(BaseModel):
    customer_id: str
    company: str
    admin_email: str
    openai_api_key: str | None = None


@app.post("/webhooks/signup", status_code=202)
def signup(event: Signup, background: BackgroundTasks) -> dict:
    def run() -> None:
        result = onboard(archy, Customer(event.customer_id, event.company, event.admin_email, event.openai_api_key))
        send_welcome_email(event.admin_email, result["invite_link"])  # your email code

    background.add_task(run)
    return {"status": "accepted"}

In production put the call on a queue with retries. Because the function is idempotent, a retry after a partial failure completes the missing steps.

docs.title: 6. Let the customer's users talk to the agents
docs.text:
Your backend can call the tenant routes with the same service token (see Acting on tenant routes):

def ask(archy: Archy, customer_id: str, agent_id: str, message: str, session_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    org_id = archy_id("org", customer_id)
    project_id = archy_id("project", f"{customer_id}/default")
    body = {"message": message, **({"session_id": session_id} if session_id else {})}
    return archy.call("POST", f"/api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query", params={"org_id": org_id, "project_id": project_id}, json=body)

Alternatively give users their own tokens: the invite flow, or an identity provider (how users sign in).

docs.title: 7. Test it without Archy
docs.text:
Mock the transport so tests run offline:

import httpx

from onboarding import Archy, Customer, onboard


def test_onboard_is_idempotent(monkeypatch):
    calls = []

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        calls.append((request.method, request.url.path))
        if request.method == "GET" and request.url.path.endswith("/agents"):
            return httpx.Response(200, json=[{"name": "support-assistant"}, {"name": "summarizer"}])
        if request.url.path.endswith("/admins/invite"):
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"invite_link": None})
        return httpx.Response(200, json={})

    monkeypatch.setenv("ARCHY_API_URL", "http://archy.test")
    monkeypatch.setenv("SERVICE_TOKEN", "t")
    archy = Archy()
    archy.http = httpx.Client(base_url="http://archy.test", transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))

    result = onboard(archy, Customer("c-1", "Globex", "boss@globex.example"))

    assert result["agents_created"] == []
    assert not [call for call in calls if call[0] == "POST" and call[1].endswith("/agents")]

docs.title: Offboarding
docs.text: Archy has no public endpoint that deletes an organization or a user. Remove customer content with the resource endpoints (DELETE agents, knowledge bases, workflows, credentials) and ask your operator about full tenant removal. DELETE .../llm-credentials/{id} on the provisioning channel is idempotent and safe in an outbox.

docs.title: What you learned
docs.text: You built an idempotent tenant onboarding function with derived ids, a customer-owned model credential, starter agents pinned to it and a first admin invite.

docs.title: Research and write pipeline
docs.text:
You will build a composite workflow that researches a topic from two sources in parallel, merges the notes, writes a post, has a reviewer check it, and saves the final text as a file. You run it asynchronously and download the result.

flowchart LR
    S((start)) --> RD[research_docs]
    S --> RW[research_web]
    RD --> M[merge: notes]
    RW --> M
    M --> W[draft]
    W --> V[review]
    V --> C{approved?}
    C -- yes --> F1[save_approved]
    C -- no --> RV[revise]
    RV --> F2[save_revised]
    F1 --> E((end))
    F2 --> E

Prepare: the Quickstart done, optionally a knowledge base for the docs researcher, and the variables from the support assistant tutorial (archy.py).

docs.title: 1. Create the agents
docs.text:
Four agents with narrow roles beat one agent with a long prompt.

# agents.py
import os

from archy import SCOPE, client

KB_ID = os.environ.get("KB_ID")  # optional


def agent(name: str, prompt: str, **config) -> str:
    r = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/agents", json={"name": name, "config": {"sys_prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.3, **config}})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["id"]


ids = {
    "docs": agent(
        "researcher-docs",
        "You research from the internal knowledge base only. Return short bullet facts with the source file name.",
        **({"knowledge_base_id": KB_ID} if KB_ID else {}),
    ),
    "web": agent(
        "researcher-web",
        "You research recent public information. Return short bullet facts with URLs.",
        web_search={"enabled": True, "provider": "duckduckgo"},
    ),
    "writer": agent("writer", "You write clear, accurate blog posts in Markdown. Never invent facts."),
    "reviewer": agent(
        "reviewer",
        "You review drafts for accuracy and clarity. Answer with JSON: approved (boolean) and feedback (string).",
        temperature=0,
    ),
}
print(ids)

docs.title: 2. Define the graph
docs.text:
Notes for reading the definition:

  • inputs declares what a caller must pass. topic is required; audience has a default.
  • variables holds constants, read as vars.max_words.
  • The reviewer has an outputSchema, so its answer is validated JSON. The condition node receives that JSON as its input and its field (approved) is a key of that JSON object, not a template.
  • A template may only read nodes that run before it. The revise node reads both draft and review, which are upstream of it.
# workflow.py
from agents import ids
from archy import SCOPE, client


def node(id_, type_, **data):
    return {"id": id_, "type": type_, "data": data}


def edge(id_, source, target, **extra):
    return {"id": id_, "source": source, "target": target, **extra}


definition = {
    "version": 2,
    "inputs": [
        {"name": "topic", "type": "string", "required": True, "description": "What to write about"},
        {"name": "audience", "type": "string", "required": False, "default": "engineers"},
    ],
    "variables": {"max_words": 600},
    "graph": {
        "nodes": [
            node("start", "start"),
            node("r1", "agent", name="research_docs", agentId=ids["docs"],
                 prompt="Using the knowledge base, collect facts about {{input.topic}}."),
            node("r2", "agent", name="research_web", agentId=ids["web"],
                 prompt="Search the web for recent developments about {{input.topic}}."),
            node("m", "merge", name="notes", strategy="summarize",
                 instruction="Combine both sets of notes. Keep sources."),
            node("w", "agent", name="draft", agentId=ids["writer"],
                 prompt="Write a post of at most {{vars.max_words}} words for {{input.audience}} from these notes:\n{{nodes.notes.output}}"),
            node("v", "agent", name="review", agentId=ids["reviewer"],
                 prompt="Review this draft for accuracy and clarity:\n{{nodes.draft.output}}",
                 outputSchema={"type": "object",
                               "properties": {"approved": {"type": "boolean"}, "feedback": {"type": "string"}},
                               "required": ["approved", "feedback"]}),
            node("c", "condition", name="gate", field="approved", operator="equals", value="true"),
            node("rev", "agent", name="revise", agentId=ids["writer"],
                 prompt="Improve the draft using this feedback.\nDraft:\n{{nodes.draft.output}}\nFeedback: {{nodes.review.json.feedback}}"),
            node("s1", "save-file", name="save_approved", format="markdown", fileName="post",
                 source="node", sourceNodeId="w"),
            node("s2", "save-file", name="save_revised", format="markdown", fileName="post"),
            node("end", "end"),
        ],
        "edges": [
            edge("e1", "start", "r1"),
            edge("e2", "start", "r2"),
            edge("e3", "r1", "m", targetHandle="target-top-1"),
            edge("e4", "r2", "m", targetHandle="target-top-2"),
            edge("e5", "m", "w"),
            edge("e6", "w", "v"),
            edge("e7", "v", "c"),
            edge("e8", "c", "s1", sourceHandle="source-true", data={"connectionType": "route", "condition": "yes"}),
            edge("e9", "c", "rev", sourceHandle="source-false", data={"connectionType": "route", "condition": "no"}),
            edge("e10", "rev", "s2"),
            edge("e11", "s1", "end"),
            edge("e12", "s2", "end"),
        ],
    },
}

created = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/workflows", json={"name": "research-and-write", "type": "composite", "config": definition})
created.raise_for_status()
workflow_id = created.json()["id"]

report = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/workflows/{workflow_id}/validate", json={}).json()
print("valid:", report["valid"], report["errors"], report["warnings"])
print("workflow", workflow_id)

Both the saved definition and any unsaved draft can be checked with validate. A typical mistake is reading nodes.review from a node that runs before the review; validation reports TEMPLATE_NODE_NOT_UPSTREAM.

docs.title: 3. Run it asynchronously
docs.text:
A run with two research steps, a merge and a review can take minutes, so start it in the background and poll.

# run.py
import sys
import time

from archy import SCOPE, client

workflow_id = sys.argv[1]
started = client.post(
    f"{SCOPE}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs",
    json={"message": "Write the post", "inputs": {"topic": "vector databases", "audience": "backend engineers"}},
)
started.raise_for_status()
run_id = started.json()["run_id"]
print("run", run_id)

while True:
    run = client.get(f"{SCOPE}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs/{run_id}").json()
    print(run["status"])
    if run["status"] in ("succeeded", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(3)

if run["status"] == "failed":
    raise SystemExit(run["error"])

print(run["output"])

files = client.get(f"{SCOPE}/artifacts", params={"session_id": run["session_id"]}).json()["items"]
for artifact in files:
    content = client.get(f"{SCOPE}/artifacts/{artifact['id']}/download")
    open(artifact["name"], "wb").write(content.content)
    print("saved", artifact["name"])

run["audit"] lists what each step did. For per-node timing and messages read the session: GET .../workflows/{id}/sessions/{session_id}.

docs.title: 4. Watch it live (optional)
docs.text: Use the streaming endpoint to show progress in a UI. The unified trace events node.started and node.completed tell you which node is running. See Running and streaming.

docs.title: 5. Iterate safely
docs.text:
• Change a prompt or an edge with PUT .../workflows/{id}. Each update stores a version snapshot; to roll back, read the old version (GET .../versions/{n}) and PUT its config back.
  • Add a human gate between review and the save nodes with a checkpoint node: Human approval checkpoint.
  • Pass the result on: a storage-write node can write the file into a connected Drive folder, and the artifact can be downloaded by your application.

docs.title: What you learned
docs.text: You combined parallel agents, a merge, structured output, a conditional branch and file output in one workflow, validated it before running, and executed it as a background run.

docs.title: Support assistant with RAG
docs.text:
You will build a customer support assistant that answers from your documentation, check its quality with a small test set, and expose it through a streaming endpoint in your own backend.

    KB --> AG[Support agent]
    GOLD[questions.json] -->|evaluate.py| AG
    UI[Your web app] -->|/chat| BE[Your backend]

docs.title: 2. Create the knowledge base and ingest
docs.text:
# ingest.py
import pathlib
import sys
import time

from archy import SCOPE, client

SUPPORTED = {".pdf", ".md", ".txt", ".docx", ".html", ".json", ".xlsx", ".pptx"}

kb = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/knowledge-bases", json={"name": "support-docs", "description": "Product documentation"})
kb.raise_for_status()
kb_id = kb.json()["id"]
print("knowledge base", kb_id)

files = [p for p in pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in SUPPORTED]
for start in range(0, len(files), 10):  # upload in batches of 10
    batch = files[start : start + 10]
    response = client.post(
        f"{SCOPE}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/documents/upload",
        files=[("files", (p.name, p.read_bytes())) for p in batch],
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    print(f"uploaded {len(batch)} files")

while True:
    stats = client.get(f"{SCOPE}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/stats").json()
    print(stats)
    if stats["indexing_total"] == 0:
        break
    time.sleep(3)

if stats["indexed_total"] < stats["files_total"]:
    failed = [d for d in client.get(f"{SCOPE}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/documents").json() if d["status"] == "failed"]
    print("failed documents:", [d["filename"] for d in failed])

python ingest.py ./docs

docs.title: 3. Check retrieval before you build the agent
docs.text:
Good answers need the right chunks. Write 10 to 20 real questions, each with a phrase that must appear in the retrieved text.

[
  {"q": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?", "expect": "30 days"},
  {"q": "What are the support hours?", "expect": "08:00"},
  {"q": "Do enterprise customers get a named contact?", "expect": "named contact"}
]

# check_retrieval.py
import json
import sys

from archy import SCOPE, client

kb_id = sys.argv[1]
cases = json.load(open("questions.json"))
misses = 0
for case in cases:
    r = client.post(f"{SCOPE}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/query", json={"query": case["q"], "top_k": 5})
    r.raise_for_status()
    text = " ".join(hit["content"] for hit in r.json()["results"]).lower()
    ok = case["expect"].lower() in text
    misses += not ok
    print("PASS" if ok else "MISS", "-", case["q"])
print(f"{len(cases) - misses}/{len(cases)} retrieved")

If questions miss, try "retrieval_strategy": "vector" or "graph" for multi-hop questions, split very long documents, or add the missing content.

docs.text:
# create_agent.py
import sys

from archy import SCOPE, client

PROMPT = """You are the support assistant for Acme.
Answer only from the knowledge base. If the answer is not there, say you do not know and offer to
connect the customer with a person. Be concise: at most four sentences. Never invent prices or dates."""

agent = client.post(
    f"{SCOPE}/agents",
    json={
        "name": "support-assistant",
        "description": "Answers customer questions from the product docs",
        "config": {
            "sys_prompt": PROMPT,
            "knowledge_base_id": sys.argv[1],
            "knowledge_base_top_k": 5,
            "temperature": 0.1,
            "max_tokens": 600,
            "memory": {"mode": "buffer", "window_messages": 10},
        },
    },
)
agent.raise_for_status()
print(agent.json()["id"])

The agent runs on the organization's attached model (LLM providers).

docs.title: 5. Evaluate end to end
docs.text:
Reuse the same questions, but ask the agent and check the answer text. Use a fresh session per question so one answer cannot leak into the next.

# evaluate.py
import json
import sys

from archy import client

agent_id = sys.argv[1]
cases = json.load(open("questions.json"))
passed = 0
for case in cases:
    r = client.post(f"/api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query", json={"message": case["q"]})
    r.raise_for_status()
    answer = r.json()["output"]
    ok = case["expect"].lower() in answer.lower()
    passed += ok
    print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", "-", case["q"], "->", answer[:100].replace("\n", " "))
print(f"{passed}/{len(cases)} passed")

Run it after every prompt or content change. Keep the questions in version control; they are your regression suite.

docs.title: 6. Expose it through your backend
docs.text:
Browsers must never see an Archy token. Your backend authenticates the end user, calls Archy, and relays the stream. This FastAPI endpoint keeps one Archy session per conversation.

# app.py
import json
import os

import httpx
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

BASE = os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"]
SCOPE = f"/api/v1/orgs/{os.environ['ORG_ID']}/projects/{os.environ['PROJECT_ID']}"
AGENT_ID = os.environ["AGENT_ID"]
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ARCHY_TOKEN']}"}

app = FastAPI()
sessions: dict[str, str] = {}  # your user or conversation id -> Archy session_id; use a database in production


class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    conversation_id: str
    message: str


@app.post("/chat")
async def chat(req: ChatRequest) -> StreamingResponse:
    body = {"message": req.message}
    if req.conversation_id in sessions:
        body["session_id"] = sessions[req.conversation_id]

    async def relay():
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=BASE, headers=HEADERS, timeout=None) as client:
            async with client.stream("POST", f"{SCOPE}/agents/{AGENT_ID}/chat/stream", json=body) as upstream:
                upstream.raise_for_status()
                event = ""
                async for line in upstream.aiter_lines():
                    if line.startswith("event:"):
                        event = line[6:].strip()
                    elif line.startswith("data:"):
                        data = json.loads(line[5:].lstrip())
                        if event == "start":
                            sessions[req.conversation_id] = data["session_id"]
                        elif event == "delta":
                            yield f"data: {json.dumps({'text': data['delta']})}\n\n"
                        elif event == "error":
                            yield f"data: {json.dumps({'error': 'The assistant is unavailable.'})}\n\n"
                yield "data: [DONE]\n\n"

    return StreamingResponse(relay(), media_type="text/event-stream", headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache"})

In the browser, read it with fetch:

const res = await fetch("/chat", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ conversation_id: "c-1", message: "What is the refund window?" }),
});
const reader = res.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
for (;;) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  for (const line of value.split("\n")) {
    if (line.startsWith("data: ") && line !== "data: [DONE]") {
      output.textContent += JSON.parse(line.slice(6)).text ?? "";
    }
  }
}

Do not leak internal errors

The relay turns Archy's error event into a generic message. Log the original detail and the request_id on your side.

docs.title: 7. Operate it
docs.text:
• Update content: delete the old document (DELETE .../documents/{doc}), upload the new one, and wait for indexing. Re-run check_retrieval.py.
  • Change behavior: update the agent's prompt with PUT (send the whole config) and re-run evaluate.py.
  • See what happened: GET .../sessions and GET .../sessions/{id}/activity show conversations and retrievals.
  • Track cost: GET .../token-usage/aggregations?group_by=agent (usage).

docs.title: What you learned
docs.text: You created and indexed a knowledge base, measured retrieval, configured a grounded agent, regression-tested it and streamed it safely through your backend.
